This is a hotfix release for v0.9.4. See the v0.9.4 notes for the full feature release: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.4

### Fixed
- Prefix shortcuts work again when the terminal sends the next key as plain text. This affected Tern, Chinese, Japanese and Korean input methods on macOS, and Ghostty `text:` keybinds that send the prefix and a key together. Workspace navigation had the same problem. (#5255)
- Codex sessions no longer start with a "clamping Interrupt hook timeout" warning. Herdr no longer installs Codex turn hooks, and Codex status comes from screen detection again. Run `herdr integration install codex` to update. (#5246, #5278)
- Claude Code questions show as blocked in named sessions. (#4573, #5192)
- On Windows, plugin panes start even when a folder on `PATH` has the same name as the plugin's program. (#5267, #5269, thanks @JJLiebig)
- On Windows, Claude Code session tracking works when the user folder name contains non-ASCII characters, such as Korean. (#5253, #5270, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Adding a Windows machine no longer prints raw PowerShell progress output. (#4639, #5282, thanks @JJLiebig)

Preview build 2026-10-14-fbd2ae23927f

[View changes](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/compare/v0.9.4...fbd2ae23927fe4923752bdb2db29661917fb05d7)

### Added
- `herdr plugin update` updates plugins installed from GitHub, all at once or by name. Running plugin panes keep working on their old files, and new runs pick up the update without a config reload. Locally linked plugins are left alone. (#4245, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Windows notifications stay in Notification Center. Clicking one jumps to its pane and brings the terminal window forward. (#4773, #4803, thanks @JJLiebig)

### Changed
- An elevated Windows server now only accepts administrator clients by default. To let normal clients from the same account in, set `[server] allow_unelevated_clients = true` or start the server with `--allow-unelevated-clients`. Permission errors now say how to fix them, and sessions you can't reach show as unavailable instead of stopped. (#4717, #4769, #4777, #4779, thanks @JJLiebig)
- On Linux and macOS, closing the shell that started Herdr no longer stops the server. Scripts that stopped Herdr with `SIGHUP` should use `herdr server stop` or `SIGTERM`. The server log now says why the server stopped. (#4920, #4965)
- With mouse capture on, plugins that handle a link get first pick when you click it. Turn capture off to use your terminal's own link shortcuts, like Command-click on macOS. (#4874, #5064, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Antigravity and Grok count as idle once they are back at their prompt, even if their own background tasks or subagents are still running. (#3530, #4735, #4959)
- Ctrl+Shift+letter reaches plain shells as the Ctrl key, like in Alacritty and WezTerm. Super, Hyper and Meta shortcuts no longer type escape-code junk into apps that can't read them. (#4356, #5017)

### Fixed
- Restarting a Mac or shutting down Windows keeps your agents' sessions. Herdr saves before the system starts closing apps, so agents come back where they were. (#4414, #5013, #5057, #5092, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Session saves are written to disk before they replace the old file, so a crash or power cut can't leave an unreadable save. (#5150, #5152, thanks @JJLiebig)
- The server keeps running when the machine runs out of processes or threads, instead of taking every pane down with it. (#3324, #4958)
- An out-of-range workspace number returns `workspace_not_found` instead of crashing the server. (#5096, #5171)
- Suspending an agent with Ctrl+Z and bringing it back with `fg` keeps its name and saved conversation. (#1647, #4964)
- Restoring a session stays responsive when a checkout's Git data is slow or missing. Worktree groups survive checkouts that are temporarily unavailable, and opening the same repository twice no longer nests one workspace inside the other. (#4926, #4736, #4945, #4770, #4772, thanks @minatoaquaMK2 and @JJLiebig)
- Closing a workspace's only pane asks first, like closing its last tab already does. Turn this off with `ui.confirm_close = false`. (#5143, #5173)
- Ctrl shortcuts like Ctrl+W work on non-Latin keyboard layouts such as Russian, Greek or Hebrew. Latin layouts and AltGr characters keep their normal meaning. (#1079, #4961)
- Accent keys and AltGr shortcuts work on Windows. (#4688, #5021, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Shift+Enter and other enhanced keys keep working after the outer terminal resets, for example after VS Code's Reload Window. (#4985, #5088)
- Quick Escape taps work on macOS with WezTerm's Kitty keyboard mode. (#1266, #5089)
- Kitty keyboard apps get key releases and F1, F2 and F4 correctly, and Backspace works when the terminal sends Ctrl+H for it. (#4184, #4403, #3244, #5017)
- Keyboard and terminal color replies no longer leak stray characters into pane input, and a half-finished color reply no longer freezes typing. (#4856, #4025, #5052, #5017, #5087)
- Fish no longer repeats prompt fragments while you resize a pane. The same problem with zsh and Powerlevel10k is still open, waiting on a Ghostty fix. (#3672, #4977)
- Apps that ask for pixel mouse coordinates get them, and clicks land in the right place on terminals that only report cells. (#4750, #3675, #5017, #4971)
- Turning off Kitty graphics makes panes stop advertising image support, so apps fall back to text. (#4978, #4979)
- Typing shows up faster, especially in PowerShell. (#4884, #5149, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Big sessions use less CPU on busy agents and idle shells, hidden panes use less memory, and Windows panes need fewer threads. (#4506, #5083, #4845, #4847, #4849, #4850, #4873, #5085, #5091, thanks @JJLiebig)
- New workspaces, tabs and splits start their shell at the right size instead of borrowing another pane's size. (#4419, #4873)
- Forwarded SSH agents are no longer contacted every second, which could eventually break SSH and Git authentication. (#4931, #4962)
- Sidebar width, collapsed groups and agent sorting on remote machines survive reconnects. Switching workspaces quickly while changing machines no longer gets canceled. (#4364, #5019, #4536, #5061, thanks @minatoaquaMK2 and @JJLiebig)
- The sidebar collapse button stays clickable when the agent list has a scrollbar. (#4692, #4734, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- The welcome screen shows your configured prefix. (#4745, #4747, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Ctrl+[ leaves workspace navigation. (#1431, #2340, thanks @qaz74107410)
- Keybindings that use `+` survive config reloads, and `/` opens Go To search on layouts where it needs Shift. (#4960, #4963, #4983, #5090, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Pasting from WezTerm on Windows into remote panes no longer types encoded key data. Copying no longer adds duplicate clipboard history entries, and closing a pane no longer hangs on a pending Enter. (#4725, #4730, #4709, #4872, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Windows shells started through Scoop or 32-bit wrappers keep their working directory in new tabs and after restarts. (#4472, #4749, #5062, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Windows ARM64 machines can be used as remote hosts through the x64 build, on a best-effort basis. (#4752)
- Codex reports finished turns through its integration when started with `--no-daemon`, its startup update screen shows as blocked, and Codex and Pi status is recognized in more cases. (#4507, #4811, #4756, #5174, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Antigravity permission, question and workspace-trust dialogs show as blocked, and its thinking spinner shows as working. (#3871, #3419, #3530, #4959)
- Hermes started through its Python installer is recognized, and installing or removing its integration keeps your YAML plugin list intact. (#4910, #4909, #4911, #4984, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- On macOS, `pane run` and `agent start` refuse commands too long for a shell that is still starting, instead of silently cutting them off. (#4950, #4988, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)

### Removed
- The experimental `HERDR_WINDOWS_INPUT_BACKEND=crossterm` setting is gone. Windows always uses its native console input. (#5017)

This is a hotfix release for v0.9.2. See the v0.9.2 notes for the full feature release: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.2

### Fixed
- Terminal shortcuts that send Escape followed by a key work again in panes. On macOS, Option+Left/Right and Option+Backspace from Ghostty's defaults or iTerm2's Natural Text Editing preset move and delete by word again, instead of typing `b` and `f` or deleting one character. Escape-based Shift+Enter bindings insert a newline in Claude Code instead of submitting. Clicking a pane still doesn't send a stray Escape. (#4751)
- Alt+[ followed quickly by another key no longer merges into a different key. (#4751)

### Breaking Changes
- The Herdr-specific pane graphics API is gone. `pane.graphics.info`, `set`, `clear`, and `stream` now return `unknown_method`. Apps show images by writing standard Kitty graphics to their terminal, which Herdr renders natively. (#4561)

### Added
- Agents can report their own resume command. Herdr then reopens their exact session after a server restart, with no built-in integration needed. Self-reported agents are also cleared once their pane is back at an idle shell. The new [Add Herdr support to your agent](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) guide covers state, resume, and release for agent authors. (#4687)
- Use more than one prefix key: `prefix = ["ctrl+space", "ctrl+s"]`. Every entry enters the same prefix mode, and `prefix+?` lists them all. (#4653, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Go To shows every agent and terminal as its own row, grouped by workspace, with its status and path. Left and Right jump between workspaces. (#4384)
- Bind `keys.clear_pane` to clear the focused pane's screen and scrollback while keeping the current prompt line. It is unbound by default and leaves full-screen apps such as Vim alone. (#4383)
- `herdr machine status` checks saved machines without prompting. `herdr machine reconnect` finishes SSH authentication, including MFA, in your terminal. Open clients recheck failed machines every 30 seconds, so no restart is needed after fixing a connection. (#3763)
- Interactive `machine add` finds the Herdr sessions already running on the host and lets you pick one. `--label` is optional; the machine is named after its SSH host. (#4204, #4678, thanks @JJLiebig and @dhh)
- `terminal session control` accepts `terminal.mouse` events, so bridge clients can click buttons in apps that enable mouse reporting. (#4685)
- Restored agents start one at a time, 100 ms apart by default, instead of all at once. Change the spacing with `[session] startup_per_agent_delay_ms`. (#4102, thanks @JJLiebig)

### Changed
- Images render faster and more reliably. Local Ghostty receives image data through temporary files instead of terminal output. Popups and notifications crop images around themselves instead of hiding them. Images that scroll out of view stay loaded, so scrolling back no longer resends them. (#4561, #4652, #4686)
- SSH connections request compression. On slow links, remote panes catch up after scrolling in a fraction of the time. (#4340)
- Scrolling output on saved machines sends only the rows that changed, cutting bandwidth for build logs and streaming agents. Older clients and servers keep working with the previous format. (#4711)
- New panes set `TERM_PROGRAM=herdr` and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`. They no longer inherit terminal session IDs, such as iTerm2's, or Claude Code session markers from the terminal that started the server. (#4104)
- Windows panes default to PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) when it is installed, falling back to Windows PowerShell. An explicit `default_shell` still wins. (#4297, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Closing the last tab of a workspace now asks for confirmation. (#4379, #4409, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Event subscriptions deliver bursts in full. A reader that falls too far behind now gets an `events_lost` error instead of silently skipping events. (#4178, #4225, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- On Unix, sending `SIGWINCH` to a Herdr client re-reads the host terminal's colors, so theme switchers that change colors without a light/dark notification can refresh panes. (#4349, thanks @dhh)

### Fixed
- Saved layouts survive host shutdown and failed restores. On Linux with logind, Herdr saves before the system shuts down. Every platform keeps up to 48 layout snapshots in `session-snapshots/` for manual recovery. (#4320)
- Clicking a pane no longer sends a stray Escape that interrupts a working agent. (#3480)
- An agent's first task now counts as done, even when it started with a prompt. Startup, restored sessions, and Pi's `/new` no longer fire false done notifications. Hook-reported status survives live handoff. (#3338, #3990, #3916)
- The server uses far less CPU with many populated panes. The navigator, pane splits, and named targets stay fast in large sessions, and bursts of external events no longer stall rendering. (#4506, #4546, #4426, #4669, #4670, #4671, #4672, thanks @JJLiebig and @minatoaquaMK2)
- Apps that use synchronized output no longer show torn frames while you type. The cursor no longer flickers during status redraws or jumps around an idle Codex on Windows. (#2968, #4303, thanks @JJLiebig)
- The API socket keeps accepting connections after a transient error, so CLI commands and live handoff no longer fail while the server keeps running. (#4601)
- Slow Git operations during worktree lookups no longer freeze typing. (#4492, thanks @JJLiebig)
- `worktree open` no longer takes over the repository's own workspace, so removing the worktree no longer closes it. (#4293)
- Forwarded SSH agents keep working in remote panes after a reconnect. Repeated `--machine` commands open far fewer SSH connections. (#1931, #4252)
- OpenCode V1 panes stay working or blocked while their subagents run. An existing registration in `tui.json` is respected instead of regenerating `tui.jsonc`. (#1362, #4240)
- Codex is no longer reported idle during active output, its mention popups are recognized, and remapped interrupt keys no longer break detection. (#4507, #4196, thanks @JJLiebig and @unmanbearpig)
- Kiro approval prompts are reported as blocked. Grok idle panes settle with custom or disabled OSC titles. (#4203, #4372, #4333, thanks @vinayshah1998)
- Droid's scrollback clears are honored, so its welcome header and old transcript no longer repeat. (#4432, thanks @factory-ain3sh)
- Copy mode stays active while output continues and a movement key is held. (#3812, #4281, thanks @marcomayer)
- Ctrl+Shift+letter keeps Shift in panes that have not enabled enhanced keyboard input, so Ctrl+Shift+C no longer arrives as Ctrl+C. (#4581, #4597, thanks @factory-ain3sh)
- Mouse reports split across reads no longer leak into the shell after a focus switch over SSH. (#4630)
- Windows: multi-line pastes into Claude Code no longer submit at the first newline, and Shift+Enter is preserved. Mouse capture survives focus changes and resizes, Ctrl+Win no longer opens prefix mode with a `ctrl+space` prefix, and remote clipboard image paste works again. (#4251, #4284, #4470, #4314, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Windows: npm-installed OMP and agents launched through hardened runtimes are detected. `machine add` against a Windows host no longer fails as "not ready for saved machines." (#4313, #4579, #4309, thanks @JJLiebig)
- The navigate-mode workspace highlight is visible with `theme = "terminal"`. Session navigator search matches words independently. The sidebar reveals agents selected by cycling or shortcuts. (#4300, #4408, #4273, #4535, #4355, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- `session attach` without a terminal explains the problem instead of leaving a new session running. (#4393)
- Socket error responses keep the original request ID, including subscription setup errors. (#4344)
- `plugin install` accepts options before the repository. (#4446)
- Windows panes pick up the host terminal's light or dark colors from the start, so apps no longer default to dark mode inside a light terminal. (#1530, #4369)
- After `herdr update`, Herdr lists which running servers are still on the old version, with the exact commands to restart each one, and reminds you to update your saved SSH machines.

Preview build 2026-09-21-0ff0f27e2226

[View changes](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/compare/2c29fb29e30220bc48d783af90ba8f53b81fd96c...0ff0f27e222633c97ba4291f6b9be4137002ca84)

### Added
- Control agents, panes, workspaces, and worktrees on saved SSH machines with `herdr --machine <label-or-id>`. Commands use the saved machine's session without needing an open Herdr window. Update Herdr on both machines to use CLI forwarding; failed remote commands never fall back to Local. (#3918)
- Connect to Windows SSH hosts from Linux, macOS, or Windows. Interactive setup can install or update the complete Windows package after confirmation; background reconnects never install updates. (#3651, #3701, #3661, #3687, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Edit names, filters, and search text at the cursor instead of only at the end. Herdr inputs now support character and word movement, Home/End, deletion, and familiar Ctrl+A/E/K/U/W/Y shortcuts, including Unicode text. (#1803, #3698, thanks @markjaquith)
- Added Letta Code detection and native conversation restore, including default conversations. Its experimental integration is installed through `herdr integration install letta`, not the Settings integration list or JSON integration API. (#3106, #3107, thanks @just-cameron)
- Hold Ctrl over a link to highlight it before opening it. Wrapped URLs and OSC 8 links remain clickable even when their beginning or end is outside the viewport. (#1282)
- Sidebar token rules can now hide matching tokens and their separators with `hide = true`; rows disappear when no tokens remain. (#3925)

### Changed
- Workspace keyboard navigation now spans connected machines in sidebar order, with a visible highlight before Enter switches machines. Collapsed machine and worktree groups remain navigable without accidentally sending actions to the wrong machine. (#3754)
- Experimental live handoff can now transfer more than 64 panes when the sending server includes this update. An older running server still has its old limit for the first upgrade; this does not change update installation order or make live handoff non-experimental. (#3393, #3411, thanks @kataokatsuki)
- On Linux and macOS, terminal observers that stop accepting output are disconnected after 30 seconds without write progress. Their pane and other clients keep running; an interrupted stream may end without a final close record. (#3612)
- Windows terminal cleanup now explicitly resets mouse-reporting modes. The remaining standalone Git Bash detach report in #3748 is still under investigation; do not treat this release as a confirmed fix for that report. (#4055, thanks @JJLiebig)

### Fixed
- Remote typing, switching, and popup interaction no longer resend the entire pane screen for small changes. Busy SSH sessions use less bandwidth, and idle attached clients avoid unnecessary redraw work. (#3769, #3745, #3822)
- A stalled SSH machine no longer traps the client away from Local. Clicking a local workspace or agent cancels the unfinished remote switch, and a recovered remote workspace refreshes without an away-and-back selection. Stale screens from before a reconnect are not reused. (#3903, #3842)
- Idle SSH connections use less CPU without losing final output. Repeated connection failures back off instead of reconnecting rapidly, and supported idle bridges clean up without stopping remote panes. (#3728, #4083)
- Large pastes no longer disconnect the client with an output-queue error. (#3833)
- SSH setup now shows authentication instructions and useful errors, including Tailscale login URLs and host-key failures, rather than appearing to hang or only reporting a lost connection. `machine add` also accepts options before the SSH target. (#3606, #3731, #3883)
- Machine and worktree groups collapse correctly without changing the selected workspace. The sidebar respects workspace row gaps, stays stable during resizing, and reveals newly focused workspaces. (#3778, #3738, #3817)
- The agent list keeps its scroll position when switching machines. Current-workspace and current-tab filters distinguish identical IDs on different machines. (#3937, #4101, #3732, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Background machine activation no longer resizes another client's focused pane. Window titles follow each client's own view rather than another client's selection. (#3744, #4091, #4130, thanks @JJLiebig)
- `agent focus` and `pane move --focus` now move attached clients to the requested pane. Moving without focus no longer leaves a client following a deleted tab or later unrelated focus changes. (#3760, #4153, #4171, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Creating a worktree focuses its new workspace again. Partially failed worktree removals can be retried, and worktrees with submodules offer an explicit forced-removal choice rather than failing without a recovery action. (#3766, #3314, #1797)
- Temporary worktree-action error banners expire instead of remaining on screen indefinitely. (#1827, #4063, thanks @JJLiebig)
- The last tab remains fully visible when the tab strip overflows, and the session navigator once again draws connected tree branches. (#4151, #3843)
- Muted sidebar and tab labels remain readable on dark themes, including Windows Terminal. (#2692, #4062, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Mouse drag and copy-mode selections stay active while output continues, even when part of the selection is outside the viewport. Copying uses the current text in the selected range. Selection repainting also avoids building up a backlog of mouse movements. (#3841, #3895)
- Double-click selections remain visible with automatic copy disabled. Holding the second click and dragging extends by whole words, and token selection stops at CJK punctuation. Host selection colors remain visible on transparent backgrounds. (#3847, #1836, #3706, #3798)
- Scrolling no longer combines mismatched terminal snapshots or leaves stale wrapped rows in fullscreen applications such as Neovim. Alternate-screen history reads preserve content across changing headers and scrollbars. (#3900, #3329, #3979)
- Local Kitty graphics keep their direct transport after the first image. Popups and notifications hide only overlapping image placements; uncovered images remain visible. (#3785, #4081)
- Pixel mouse coordinates work independently of image rendering and use the terminal's integer cell size, preventing clicks from drifting across the screen. (#3295, #4140, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Function keys F1–F12 are recognized in Kitty keyboard reports, and F1–F4 also work with parameterized reports from terminals such as foot. (#1809, #2378, #4067, thanks @ashokDevs and @JJLiebig)
- WezTerm control-key reports now preserve Enter, Backspace, Tab, and Escape. Cmd/Super-modified input reaches pane applications with its modifier intact. Modified Enter stays compatible with panes that have not requested enhanced key encoding. (#3589, #3710, #4103, #4110, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Mouse reports split across delayed reads no longer leak their trailing bytes into pane input. Clients reassert mouse reporting after terminal reconnects. (#3911, #4079, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Saved sessions that cannot be loaded are preserved before replacement, rather than silently overwritten. Recovery copies are kept in `session-backups/`; failed preservation leaves the original untouched. (#4125)
- Deleting a session now requires its exact name, including case, on case-insensitive filesystems. Names beginning with a hyphen can be passed after `--`. (#3819, #4233, #3220, thanks @minatoaquaMK2)
- Newly started macOS servers retain access to user lookup and DNS across logout. Existing affected servers need a full session restart; live handoff cannot repair their inherited service context. (#4100)

- Oversized bracketed text pastes are now rejected with a client-local notification instead of disconnecting the client. (#1665)
- Agent prompt waits now report `agent_prompt_stalled` after five seconds without an observed state change instead of waiting indefinitely after an ineffective submission.
- `herdr config check` now reports unknown config keys with their full paths instead of treating ignored typos as valid configuration. (#1573)
- Codex panes with customized static terminal titles now fall back to the live working footer instead of remaining idle, while OSC activity remains preferred. (#1563)

- Kimi question prompts now report blocked until the user answers or dismisses them.
- Pi lifecycle reporting now uses settled events, preventing transient message boundaries from publishing an idle state mid-turn.

- Terminal diff streams now batch contiguous writes, reducing the visible wave effect while scrolling pane history. (#283)
- A standalone Escape arriving beside another key is now preserved as its own input instead of being combined into a fabricated Alt chord. (#541)

- Host-terminal focus redraws now stay pending until the client can send them, so panes refresh after focus returns even when redraw delivery was briefly busy.
- Numeric keypad keys that send VT100 application-keypad escape sequences now enter their digits and operators instead of being dropped. (#493)
- Codex panes now stay marked working when the live status header uses reasoning-summary text such as `Investigating code output` instead of the literal `Working` label. (#501)
- Codex blocker detection now ignores stale prompt text outside the live prompt region, reducing false blocked states from old scrollback.
- Native pane URL clicks now use Cmd-click on macOS and Ctrl-click on other platforms. (#307)
- Worktree open, create, and remove actions now work from bare repositories instead of assuming a normal checkout. (#497)
- Pane mouse handling no longer sends empty PTY writes for mouse events that produce no terminal input. (#496)
- Pane output now renders flag emoji and other multi-codepoint grapheme clusters as complete symbols instead of blank cells. (#243)
- Starting Herdr with no restored workspaces, or closing the last workspace, now opens a default workspace instead of leaving the client on an empty screen where direct keybindings such as `cmd+n` were shown but ignored. (#366)
- Resizing restored panes no longer aborts the server when libghostty-vt reflows a terminal whose pre-resize cursor row is past the new height. (#465)
- Full-screen TUIs such as Neovim now receive resize-generated terminal responses after Herdr internal pane resizes, so grown panes redraw without waiting for extra input. (#471)
- Nested agent session reports from child terminals no longer overwrite the owning pane's restored agent session id. (#511)
- Headless servers now avoid repeated scrollback rendering work for inactive panes, reducing CPU in large sessions. (#512)
- Mouse-click handling now respects `ui.prompt_new_tab_name`, so mouse-created tabs follow the same naming prompt setting as keyboard-created tabs. (#521, thanks @imrajyavardhan12)

This is a hotfix release for v0.6.7, prioritizing a server-crash fix for panes that print complex Unicode or emoji output.

### Fixed
- Fixed a Herdr server crash triggered by pane output containing complex Unicode, emoji, or decomposed accent graphemes. Affected sessions could lose running pane processes or crash again after restore if the same saved pane output was replayed. (#453)
- Direct installs managed by mise now update through the mise install path instead of failing to replace the active binary.
- Claude Code panes that are actively thinking or streaming no longer flicker to blocked because of custom status text. (#409)

### Added
- Added opt-in macOS input-source switching during prefix mode with `experimental.switch_ascii_input_source_in_prefix`, so users typing with a non-Latin IME can run prefix commands through an ASCII-capable input source and return to the previous input source when prefix mode ends. (#400, #434, thanks @sf-jin-ku)

### Added
- Added a compact collapse control to the expanded sidebar so mouse users can collapse and expand the sidebar from visible controls. (#278, #291, thanks @turgaybulut)
- Added an opt-in preview update channel with `herdr channel set preview`, `[update].channel`, automated preview manifests, and GitHub prerelease publishing for users who want fixes before stable releases as Herdr transitions toward less frequent, more stable releases.
- Added a remote SSH bridge keepalive fallback. `herdr --remote` now generates a temporary SSH config that includes the user's SSH config first, then adds `ServerAliveInterval` and `ServerAliveCountMax` only when the user has not already configured keepalives. Set `[remote].manage_ssh_config = false` to disable this. (#354, #355, thanks @SunskyXH)
- Added `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier` so a configured modifier such as `ctrl` can forward right-click hold and drag gestures to mouse-reporting pane apps while normal right-click still opens Herdr's pane menu. (#148)
- Added Kilo Code CLI automatic detection for idle, working, and blocked terminal states. (#270)
- Added `herdr integration install copilot` for GitHub Copilot CLI hooks that report prompt, tool, post-approval progress, permission, `ask_user`, `exit_plan_mode`, idle, session-exit state, and session ids through Herdr's socket API. When native agent session restore is enabled, Herdr can resume Copilot panes with `copilot --resume=<id>`. (#232, #386, thanks @LaneBirmingham)

### Changed
- Native agent session restore is now enabled by default for supported panes with current official integrations. Set `[session] resume_agents_on_restore = false` to disable it.
- Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode integrations now report session identity only. Native state for those agents comes from Herdr's screen detection, while Pi, OMP, GitHub Copilot CLI, Hermes Agent, Qoder CLI, and custom socket integrations can still report state.

### Fixed
- Large long-running sessions no longer hit the frame-streaming crash fixed by the vendored libghostty-vt update. (#276)
- Copy mode now preserves linewise selection after `shift+v` while moving the cursor. (#360, #389, thanks @reobin)
- Leaving copy mode now restores the previous scroll position, or returns to the bottom when copy mode started at the bottom. (#398, #410, thanks @reobin)
- Git branch labels now resolve correctly in repositories that use Git's reftable ref format instead of showing `.invalid`. (#384, #423, thanks @LaneBirmingham)
- The official Nix flake now builds on macOS by providing Darwin SDK discovery helpers and Darwin cctools to the vendored libghostty-vt build. (#405, #407, thanks @DeevsDeevs)
- Commands launched after `--`, such as `herdr agent start ... -- opencode --session <id>`, now preserve child argv flags instead of parsing them as Herdr flags. (#383)
- Pane apps that request any-motion mouse tracking now receive hover/move events, making Textual-style TUI mouse interaction more reliable inside Herdr. (#419)
- Claude Code background-agent wait text in scrollback no longer keeps an idle pane marked working after the background agent has completed.
- Claude Code and Codex transcript or expanded-detail viewers no longer publish a false idle state while the pane is still showing active agent status.
- Claude Code question prompts that use the arrow-glyph selector are now detected as blocked.
- Kiro sub-agent tool approval prompts are now detected as blocked instead of working. (#388)
- Shift-letter prefix bindings such as `prefix+shift+n` now work in legacy SSH terminal sessions that send uppercase letters without separate Shift metadata. (#312)
- Idle panes now avoid repeated full foreground-process scans, reducing idle CPU on sessions with many panes. (#439)
- Restored native agent sessions now resume across background workspaces and tabs after the first client provides terminal context instead of waiting until each pane is focused.
- Pane input no longer waits behind the PTY actor's idle read poll, restoring responsive typing at quiet shell prompts. (#379)
- Pane apps that query OSC 4 ANSI palette colors now receive the active terminal palette response, so OpenCode and similar TUIs can enable system-theme behavior inside Herdr. (#387)
- Pane apps that query terminal capabilities with XTGETTCAP now receive supported capability responses, improving feature detection in Neovim and similar terminal apps. (#393)
- Pane text selection now derives its highlight colors from the host terminal or active Herdr palette instead of forcing the theme's blue accent. (#298)
- `herdr channel set preview` and `herdr channel set stable` now update direct installs from the selected channel immediately, reject preview on Homebrew and Nix installs before changing config, and show package-manager guidance for managed installs.
- Plain `herdr update` and remote binary replacement now ask before stopping running sessions, avoid protocol-heavy prompt text, and leave the current install untouched when the user chooses not to stop active pane processes. Explicit `--handoff` update flows try live handoff without a second handoff prompt.
- Remote bootstrap now uses the remote shell only for PATH discovery and runs internal probes through `/bin/sh`, so `herdr --remote` can detect existing installs when the remote login shell is fish. (#396)

### Added

### Changed

- Restored sessions now land in terminal mode, while fresh sessions still start in navigate mode.

### Breaking Changes Please Read
- The update flow changes in `0.4.11`. Herdr no longer installs updates silently in the background. Starting with this release, herdr only checks for updates and shows them in the UI. To install a new release, quit herdr and then run `herdr update` manually in your shell.
- This prepares the upcoming `0.5.0` persistence release. Herdr is moving from the old single-binary update model toward a persistent server/client session model, so your workspace can keep running while clients attach, detach, and reconnect.
- The reason for this change is upgrade safety. Herdr needs to stop the old running process cleanly before the new client/server model takes over, so manual update avoids mixed-version states during the transition.

`pip install phone-harness` — https://pypi.org/project/phone-harness/0.2.0/

## Android
Drive a real Android phone the same way you drive an iPhone — same helpers, same agent code. Pure adb: `screencap` for eyes, the phone's own accessibility tree for exact text and boxes (`ocr()` is exact here; `tap_ui("url_bar")` finds what OCR can't), `input` for hands, `back()` exists. USB (plug in, tap Allow) or Wi‑Fi (`phone-harness android pair CODE` — the phone is found over mDNS; only the 6‑digit code crosses). Paired phones are remembered by name and reconnected automatically. A locked phone is refused honestly (`locked`), never PIN'd. `phone-harness android awake` keeps the phone unlocked for a session without changing a setting, with a live scrcpy mirror if installed; `rest` puts it to sleep. `phone-harness --doctor android`. (#39, #40)

## The seam
Every device sits behind one `send(op, **kw)` vocabulary (`transport.py`); helpers are platform-agnostic; `connect("ios"|"android")`. This is what made Android one file. (#19)

## iPhone reliability
Window discovery by PID, focus tracking that reflects reality, and dead-session detection that is structural — interstitials ("iPhone in Use", "Connect", "Mac Locked") are recognised by shape, quoted verbatim, and never tapped through. (#18)

## Interactivity
`type_text` pastes by default (exact, no autocorrect); `keystrokes=True` for real key events; real modifier chords. The typed text stays on the clipboard — restoring the previous clipboard raced the phone and could paste it instead. (#20, #43)

## Config
`phone-harness config` — settings with their source; `config set platform android` makes Android the default; remembered devices in `~/.local/state/phone-harness`. Precedence: argument → env → file → default. (#40)

## Onboarding
One short setup prompt (README and phone-harness.com); the guided first-run flow lives in `onboarding.md`; `install.md` covers both phones. (#44)

## Also
`--doctor [ios|android]` and two long-standing doctor bugs (verdict, capture crash) fixed; `SKILL.md` covers both platforms; `phone-harness skill` works from an installed wheel; PyPI publishing on tag via trusted publishing (0.1.1 was the first PyPI release).

## Known limits (stated, not hidden)
Android's tree costs seconds on a slow phone and is unavailable on screens that never go idle (read the screenshot); `input text` is ASCII; a PIN-locked phone needs the user. The cloud backend (#42) is not in this release.

4.4.0 was not published to npm. 4.5.0 is the first release with everything in it (the [4.4.0] section below), plus these changes.

New since the first 4.5.0 cut: privacy-safe telemetry v2 with a one-time notice, videos (MP4, MOV, WebM) that convert to `.ogv` on import, and a game that goes from export to live over MCP with no staff wait.

- **The `launch-ready` skill: get a game ready to launch and take it live.** Where `release-checklist` reports what is missing, `launch-ready` makes it pass: it exports and uploads the build, captures real gameplay screenshots with `summer_capture_gameplay`, makes the key art, icons, tall cover and capsules from a real capture under the `store-art` rules, writes the store text and fills every listing detail from the project (GameSoul, project memory, README, what it saw in play), runs the checklist again until it passes, shows the creator the preview link, every image and all text, and goes live with `summer_go_live` after one yes. It asks the creator once, before anything is uploaded or spent, for what the project can't tell (price, support contact, developer name, release stage), and has the creator confirm the content rating, the content questionnaire and the AI disclosure. It never invents a fact, never edits a screenshot and picks only true tags, genres and features. Library-only, because the installed-description budget is full: `release-checklist`, `publish-your-game` and `/summer` point to it. It uses only operations the engine profile already has, so the tool count does not change.
- **Telemetry: a few more fields and a one-time notice.** Every field is listed in the README section "Telemetry". Summer never sends prompts, code, file contents, file names or paths, project names, tool arguments or results. `SUMMER_NO_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns all of it off.
  - **First run:** the first `summer` command on a computer (`summer mcp` too) prints a one-time notice to stderr and sends one anonymous `cli_first_run` line: a random install id, the command name, the agent app and the operating system. Not in CI. Signing in joins that line to the account.
  - **New fields on signed-in tool-call and command lines, when they apply:** `projectIdHash` (the hash of the random project id the engine already uses for routing; never the project name or path), `templateId` (the catalog template the project started from; on `summer create` also its library domains), `instanceCount` (how many game clients `engine.play` started) and `engineState` (four yes/no facts on `engine_not_running`: engine installed, engine running, project open, signed in).

- **Videos import as Ogg Theora by themselves.** Summer Engine plays video only as `.ogv`, and an `.mp4`, `.mov` or `.webm` import used to fail and roll back. `summer_import_from_url`, its batch, `summer_import_asset_by_id` and `summer_import_asset` now convert a video on the way in: a video Summer generated or stores imports as its Theora rendition from Summer's media host; any other video converts with ffmpeg on this computer when it has Theora (video quality 8, Vorbis audio, same frame rate, at most 1920x1080), else on summerengine.com (needs the Summer sign-in). The `.ogv` lands at the requested path with the extension swapped, and the answer says so (`videoConversions`, `note`). A generated video saved with `out` into a Godot project saves as `.ogv` too. The `animated-loop`, `cinematic-cutscene` and `trailer-shot` skills no longer tell agents to run ffmpeg by hand.

- **From export to live over MCP, with no staff wait.** A game goes live as soon as Summer's automated checks pass; Summer's staff review it afterwards, and no tool or skill tells a creator to wait for a review any more.
  - **`summer_go_live` (`store.go_live`, `summer store go-live`):** releases the uploaded Build to every platform that passed its checks and publishes the store page, through the same store routes Studio uses, then watches until players get it. It needs no owner approval link while the person's Agent permissions allow Publish (the default; otherwise `needs_permission`). Confirm-gated. It answers `live`, `blocked` (each failure with its fix), `needs_changes` (Summer's feedback) or `waiting`; a hold on Summer's side is reported as Summer's, with nothing to fix. Calling again continues without asking twice.
  - **`summer_store_set_details` (`store.set_details`):** the store page sections `store.update_listing` does not edit: the content questionnaire, the AI disclosure, genres, features, credits, language support and system requirements.
  - **`summer_publish_build` waits for Summer's automated checks** and reports each platform (`checks`: passed, or failed with `code`, `owner` and `fix`). A running malware scan is a wait, not a failure. Intake refusals the platform names (`engine_build_unreleased`, `malware_detected`, `verifying_failed` and others) come back with a fix.
  - **`summer.bundle.v2` exports are read.** `summer_export_game` and `summer_publish_build` refused every export from Summer Engine 0.7.4 and newer (the fixed layout); they now take v2 with its six paths and still take v1. `summer_export_game` reports the export's paths.
  - **The `release-checklist` skill:** before going live, check the export (preset, Summer version, the fixed layout, a server pack for a game with a server), the upload and its checks, the store art per slot and every required listing field, each rule with its MCP check, its fix and the platform rule it comes from.
  - The engine profile leaves out the hosted `summer_store_releases` and `summer_store_version_status`, which `summer_go_live` supersedes, so the two new tools fit its tool limit.

- **The MCP opens the project itself.** When a tool needs the engine and no editor runs, the engine is installed and the session has a project (the agent's folder or `--project`), the local MCP launches it in the background, waits and retries; a slow first open answers "call again in 30 seconds". It never starts a second editor while one is registered for the project, was launched on it and still runs, or does not answer (busy); an editor that exits at once ends the wait, and Linux with no display answers at once. 3.9.0 and 3.9.1 were not published to npm. 4.0.0 is the first release with everything in them (the [3.9.1] and [3.9.0] sections below), plus these changes.

Summer 4.0: every Summer capability is one operation, named `area.action` (`assets.generate_image`, `store.publish`), with one answer shape, and `summer mcp` serves them by default. Engine tools keep their 3.x names. For everything else, `summer_search` finds the operation and its exact input, and `summer_call` runs it. The `summer` CLI runs the same operations.

**To get the 3.x tools back:** start the server with `summer mcp --surface v3`, or add `SUMMER_SURFACE=v3` to the `env` of your agent's Summer MCP entry. That serves the 3.x tools as before. `SUMMER_SURFACE=v3` in your shell also leaves out the new `summer <area> <action>` commands.

**If you signed in with 3.8.0 or earlier,** run `npx -y summer-engine@latest login` once. Generation and the other cloud operations now run on Summer's hosted server, which needs the store sign-in that `summer login` adds since 3.9.0.

### What changes when you update

- **3.x tool names keep working.** `summer_call` runs any 3.x tool by its old name, on the local server and on Summer's hosted server. While the Summer skills `summer setup` installed for your user are older than 4.0, `summer mcp` also lists every 3.x name again (the legacy toolset, local and hosted), each saying which operation replaces it and running as in 3.x. `--toolsets legacy` or `SUMMER_LEGACY_TOOLS=on` keeps them listed; `SUMMER_LEGACY_TOOLS=off` hides them. `npx -y summer-engine@latest setup <agent> --yes` installs the 4.0 skills. With skills from a plugin or a project folder, update them, or set `SUMMER_LEGACY_TOOLS=on` to keep the 3.x names listed.
- **`summer mcp` serves the v4 surface by default** (`--surface v3` or `SUMMER_SURFACE=v3` brings back the 3.x tools). It lists the engine tools under their 3.x names, `summer_docs_search` and `summer_docs_read`, and two new tools: `summer_search` finds any operation, local or cloud, with its exact input, and `summer_call` runs it. Engine operations run here. Cloud operations run on Summer's hosted server, with the same approvals. Every 3.x tool can still be called through `summer_call`, by its old name too.
- **One answer shape.** Every 4.0 tool answers `{ok, status, result}`: `done`, `running` with a job (`jobs.wait` waits up to 50 seconds per call), `needs_approval` with a link for the person, or `dry_run` with a preview. An error has a `code` (`engine_not_running`, `not_signed_in`, `no_credits`, `invalid_input`, ...), a message and exactly one `next` step. Every change takes `dryRun: true` (it changes and spends nothing) and an `idempotencyKey`, so a retry never runs twice.
- **A failed cloud call says what happened.** `not_signed_in` only for a sign-in problem (a revoked or expired store sign-in says `npx -y summer-engine login --store --force`); `forbidden` when Summer refuses the account (for example an unconfirmed email). `unavailable` when nothing reached Summer's hosted server (no connection, the sign-in server down, a 503), or when a read or a dry run was cut off: it is safe to try again. `outcome_unknown` when a change was cut off after it was sent, because it may have run: call it again only with the same `idempotencyKey`, or check first. `--wait` keeps the job id when a wait does not get through. This holds for `summer_call`, the hosted direct tools and `summer <area> <action>`.
- **Approvals.** A change that needs a person answers `needs_approval` with a link (`https://www.summerengine.com/studio/approvals/<id>`) and changes nothing until they approve; `jobs.wait` follows it to the end. Today that covers publishing a game (Summer Games asks the game's owner), price, sale and A/B test changes, member changes, deletes and anything that contacts people. Studio > Settings > Agent permissions lists the defaults; you can change them soon.
- **`summer <area> <action> --field value`** (left out with `SUMMER_SURFACE=v3`). The CLI view of the same catalog, with `--dry-run`, `--wait` (follows a job or an approval to the end) and `--json`. It also adds `summer whoami`, `summer ops search <words>` and `summer ops describe <op>`.
- **Generated files land on this machine again.** On the v4 surface and in the v4 CLI, `assets.generate_image`, `generate_audio`, `generate_3d`, `generate_video`, `generate_motion`, `assets.get` and `jobs.wait` take `out`: a folder or a file path (`res://` in a Godot project). The package keeps it (Summer's server never sees it), downloads each file the answer names and adds `localPath` beside its URL. 3D, video and animation save when `jobs.wait` sees the job finish, also after an approval. Without `out`, a generation in the assets profile or the CLI saves into the project's asset folder: Godot `assets/`, Unity `Assets/Summer`, Unreal `Content/Summer`, three.js `public/assets`. `assets.get` saves only with `out`, and sessions with engine tools save only with `out`, because `summer_import_asset_by_id` already puts the file in the project. A save never overwrites a file (it takes the next free name and says so), writes only media and model file types (never `.cs` or `.dll`), keeps `res://` inside the project, downloads only from public https hosts, up to 500 MB. Whatever is not saved is a warning; the answer stays as it was.
- **The assets profile on 4.0.** `summer mcp --profile assets` (what `summer setup <agent> --assets-only` writes) lists Summer's hosted asset reads and generators, jobs and `whoami` as direct tools, plus `summer_search`, `summer_call` and the docs tools, and its instructions name only tools it lists. Generators run on Summer's hosted server by their 4.0 names; a 3.x generator name called through `summer_call` still runs the local 3.x tool.
- **Skills use the 4.0 names.** The asset, publishing, plans, Summer Apps and Studio skills name the operations (`assets.generate_image`, `store.publish`, `plans.create`, `apps.call`, `studio.open`), every skill and reference names the docs tools `summer_docs_search` and `summer_docs_read`, and the asset skills save files with `out`. `validate:library` fails when a skill or reference names a 3.x docs tool. Engine tools keep their names.
- **The docs describe 4.0.** README, AGENTS.md and `docs/` now say how to connect (one hosted URL and one sign-in for cloud work, the local server for engine work), how agents call Summer (operations, `summer_search` and `summer_call`, one answer shape and its error codes, 3.x names that keep working), what an agent may do on its own (Agent permissions, approvals, Agent activity), how credits and auto top-up work, the two store versions for ChatGPT and Claude's connector directory, and the `summer <area> <action>` CLI.
- **`summer_run_script` takes `scenePath` and is stable.** The script runs against the scene you name: Summer opens it first (on its own, never in a batch with an edit), runs the script, then opens the scene you were looking at again. If the scene cannot be opened, the script does not run. The result says what happened in `scene_target`. Without `scenePath` it runs against the open scene, as before.
- **Engine operations in the 4.0 catalog.** Every engine tool keeps its 3.x name and is now an operation with a title, a summary of 300 characters or fewer, its effect and an example (`src/core/ops/engine.ts`). On the v4 surface each engine tool lists that summary plus a pointer to its full guide, its hints come from its effect, and it answers in the one answer shape: `{ok, status, result}`, or one error code with one next step (`engine_not_running` says to open the project, instead of plain text). The v4 engine tools list takes about half the tokens of the 3.x one.
- **Each engine tool has a guide.** `summer_docs_read` with id `tool/<slug>` now also returns the tool's full how-to (`library/tools/<slug>/GUIDE.md`, the text the 3.x MCP description carries). `npm run generate:tool-guides` keeps the two the same.
- **Reads split from changes.** `summer_camera_bookmark` becomes `engine.list_camera_bookmarks` (read), `engine.save_camera_bookmark` and `engine.delete_camera_bookmark`; `summer_ui_actions` becomes `engine.list_ui_actions` (read) and `engine.invoke_ui_action`. On the v4 surface each is its own tool; the 3.x tools stay as they are.
- **`summer_call` for engine operations**: a dry run checks the input without the engine, `ops.describe` answers for local operations here, and a bad input points at the tool's guide.
- **Skills teach one script for multi-step scene work.** 28 code blocks in 23 skills chained 4 to 15 single scene edits (`summer_add_node`, `summer_set_prop`, ...), 197 calls in all; each is now one `summer_run_script` call with `scenePath` (the kit-placement example is one `summer_batch`). `scene-scripting` is stable and under 200 lines, with the extended ctx API and the recipes in its `references/`. AGENTS.md, `/summer`, `using-summer`, `make-game` and the agent playbook say it once each: 3 or more scene edits are one `summer_run_script` with `scenePath`. 46 script lines in 10 skills that wrote `var x := ctx.…` (which does not compile: `ctx` is untyped) now write `var x = ctx.…`. `validate:library` fails on a code block with 4 or more single scene edits (unless the line before it says why with `<!-- single-edits-ok: … -->`) and on `:= ctx.`.
- **The operation contract.** `registry/schemas/operation.schema.json` describes an operation (name, effect, approval, input, output), and `registry/operations/legacy-names.json` maps every 3.x tool name to its operation (`summer_set_prop` is `engine.set_prop`, `summer_store_submit` is `store.publish`). Conformance fixtures sit next to it.
- **Official MCP Registry.** `package.json` names the server `io.github.SummerEngine/summer` (`mcpName`), and the generated `server.json` lists the npm package and the hosted server. The name keeps the GitHub org's own case, because the registry matches it exactly against the org.
- **The hosted 3.x tools ask for 3.x.** The local server mounts Summer's hosted 3.x tools (the 3.x surface and the legacy toolset), and `summer tool` and `summer doctor` call them, with `?surface=v3`, so they keep their 3.x names when Summer's hosted server serves 4.0 by default.
- `summer doctor` checks for the tools of the surface `summer mcp` will serve (`summer_search` and `summer_call` on v4).
- The per-call usage line also says which operation the call ran, the surface (`v3` or `v4`) and the profile. It never sends arguments or results.

## [3.9.0] - 2026-10-14

One sign-in for every Summer tool, tool profiles that fit every agent, shorter tool results, and Summer sees which agent app made each request.

- **Summer sees which agent app made each request.** Every request to Summer's servers (generation, jobs, assets, Summer Apps, the store upload, the hosted Summer Engine MCP, library search and the usage line) now carries the agent app's id (`X-Summer-Agent-Host`, for example `claude-code`), the name and version the app sent in the MCP handshake, and the tool that made the request (`X-Summer-MCP-Tool`). Before, the app was never sent. Outside an MCP session (`summer tool`, `summer login`) the id comes from the agent's environment; `SUMMER_AGENT_HOST` overrides it. `SUMMER_NO_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` removes these headers and keeps only the CLI's own name and version.
- **One sign-in.** `summer login` now signs you in to your Summer account and then, in the same browser, to the store, publishing and Grow tools: one Allow click, or none if this machine was approved before. Before, that took a second `summer login --store`. If the store step does not finish within 3 minutes, your account sign-in is kept and `summer login --store` adds the store later. `summer login --no-store` skips the store step; `summer login --store` still runs it alone.
- **Every tool says what it does.** Each local MCP tool now carries `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint`, mapped from its `authority` in the library. Agents and apps that ask before a change can let reads run and still ask before an edit, a generation that costs credits, or a publish. A test fails when a tool has no hints.
- **Agents script runs of scene edits.** The MCP instructions now say: more than 3 scene edits, write one `summer_run_script` (snapshot, script, diff, screenshot). After the 4th single edit in a row (`summer_set_prop`, `summer_add_node`, `summer_remove_node`, ...), the result adds one line that points to `summer_run_script`, then again every 6th.
- **Tool profiles.** `summer mcp --profile` (env `SUMMER_PROFILE`): `full` is every tool and stays the default, so existing setups do not change. `engine` has the engine, generation and store tools and stays under 128 tools; `summer setup vscode-copilot` now writes it, because VS Code Copilot takes at most 128 tools per request (`--profile full` keeps every tool). `assets` has generation, the asset library, account and library search, and no engine tools. `--toolsets` (env `SUMMER_TOOLSETS`) adds toolsets by name. Engine tools load at start in every profile that has them, and no tool is renamed.
- **Assets-only setup.** `summer setup <agent> --assets-only` writes the `assets` profile, installs only the asset skills instead of the whole library, and leaves out Summer Games. The README's assets-only path now uses it. `summer skills install --assets` installs the same skills.
- **Shorter results.** Tool results are compact JSON instead of pretty-printed JSON. Results that can be long (scene and runtime trees, console and debugger reads, inspect reads, library reads) stop at a default size and say so: 4,000 characters, 8,000 for `summer_get_scene_tree`, 24,000 for `summer_read_library`. Pass `maxCharacters` for more. Writes, job ids and file reads are never cut.
- **Usage reports.** When you are signed in, the MCP server now reports each tool call to Summer: the tool name, whether it worked, how long it took and your agent app's name. Nothing else: no arguments, results, code or file names. `SUMMER_NO_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns it off, and now also turns off the once-per-session report.
- `summer_app_guide` starts with section `overview` by default and answers Markdown text instead of one long JSON line; `all` still returns every section.
- `summer_app_screenshot` takes `steps` (click a selector, press a declared action, wait) to show a dialog or a second state before the capture, and waits until the app's calls settle.

Agents build Summer Apps, team tools inside Summer Studio, and asset-only requests skip the engine.

- **Summer Apps tools.** A Summer App is a tool your team uses inside Summer Studio: a balance table, a quest editor, an asset tracker, a pick-one grid. Your agent builds it and it works on the team's data. New tools: `summer_app_guide` (the build guide), `summer_app_list`, `summer_app_create`, `summer_app_publish` (from a local folder, files or a layout), `summer_app_get`, `summer_app_events` (what the app sends to agents), `summer_app_page` (fill the app's fields and press its buttons), `summer_app_data` (read and write the app's shared data; `as: "seed"` for starter data), `summer_app_tools` and `summer_app_call` (the agent tools an app declares), `summer_app_dock` (dock an app as a panel in the editor) and `summer_app_report_gap` (tell Summer what the app needed and did not have). All but `summer_app_dock` work without the engine; they need `summer login`. If Summer Apps is not open for your account yet, they answer `not_found`.
- **Two new skills: `summer-apps` and `summer-apps-design`.** `summer-apps` is the build loop, Layout or code, the manifest, the SDK, data and agent tools, with a complete working app. `summer-apps-design` is how an app should look: page layout, the Summer UI kit components, tables, charts, states, and a check before you publish.
- **`summer_app_screenshot`: see your Summer App without opening Studio.** Summer renders the app's published version with your data and returns the picture plus what to fix: console lines, uncaught errors, calls it refused, whether the SDK connected, and the fields and buttons the app declared. It is read-only: writes, sends and paid calls are refused, so nothing changes. `width: 390` shows the phone layout, `theme: "dark"` the dark theme, `fullPage` the whole scroll; `out` also saves the PNG (`summer tool app-screenshot` saves it to `./summer-app-screenshot.png`). - **`summer_enable_plugin` enables an editor plugin (`res://addons/<name>/`) and reports what really happened.** On engines that wait for the plugin, it answers `enabled` with the plugin's autoloads, or the failure code with a hint. Pick your sound effects by ear, and hosted games: agents check that players can actually join before a release.

- **Three versions of a sound effect, picked in Summer Studio.** The best sound-effect model changes a lot from one sound to the next. The first time you ask for a sound effect in a chat, the `sound-effect` skill now asks whether you want three versions from three models. If you say yes, the new `summer_generate_sfx_choices` makes them and shows them on a Summer Studio page: in your open Studio tab when you are signed in to the store, else in your browser, else as a link. You listen and approve one or more; `summer_get_choices` tells the agent which ones, and it imports and wires them. The model you approve becomes your default for later sound effects.
- `summer_generate_audio` sound effects take `modelId` (`eleven_text_to_sound_v2`, `sonilo-sfx-1.1`, `stable-audio-3-sfx`; left out, your approved default runs, else ElevenLabs) and `loop` for seamless loops (ElevenLabs only). Existing calls work as before.
- The `sound-effect` skill has prompt shapes that held up in testing: a Foley one-shot with the materials, the attack and the tail; exact event times for sequences such as a rifle reload; "air movement only" for whooshes; and the minimum length of each model. `ambient-bed` names the looping model, and `audio-direction` makes its first sounds through `sound-effect`.

- **`release-readiness` check 10: a signed-in player keeps playing for three minutes.** A released game closed for every player about a minute in, with "That link can't be opened", and left them signed out: a Summer service refused the player's sign-in and the app ended play. The fault was Summer's, and no check on the game's files could see it. The check asks the user to play the released version for 3 minutes in each Summer Games app, through an analytics event, and to report a close or sign-out to Summer with the time. `multiplayer-publish` step 6 points to it.
- **`release-readiness` checks 8 and 9: every file the game reads is in the pack, and the export is on the apps' Summer version line.** A release's uploaded pack left out a font file the game read with `FileAccess`; it fell back to `SystemFont`, which draws every glyph as a box on iPhone, while desktop looked right. Check 8 traces every by-path read, checks the summer.games preset's non-resource filter, lists `client.pck` with a short `--script` probe, bans `SystemFont` for phone text and asks for a look at the text on an iPhone. Another release was a 0.6 export, and a Summer Games phone app that carries 0.7 refused it with "The game could not start" while desktop ran it. Check 9 compares the export's MAJOR.MINOR with the current Summer release. `export-and-ship`, `ui-basics` and `multiplayer-publish` point to both.
- **`release-readiness` check 7: export with a released Summer, and prove the scripts compile on the runtime players get.** Players' apps run a bundle on the released Summer of the version its export stamp names. A development build that still stamps an older released version can use APIs that release lacks; its scripts then fail to compile on every player's device (`Parse Error: Static function "…" not found`, `Failed to load script`) and the game opens to an empty window, while every upload check passes. The check reads the stamp from `summer-bundle.json`, compares `engineSha` with the release's, and runs `client.pck` on that released Summer with `--headless --verbose --main-pack`, failing on `SCRIPT ERROR`, `Parse Error` or `Failed to load script`. `multiplayer-publish` adds the run as step 4e, and `export-and-ship` says to export summer.games bundles with the released editor only.

- **New `release-readiness` skill.** Before a version reaches players, it runs six checks on the summer.games `.zip` you upload: the bundle's `server.pck`, started with no scene, loads the authority scene; a real online join with the released version reaches the game; online play is reachable by default; the server saves online progress through player data; players can get back to the title; and `Summer.initialize` passes no hard-coded Game ID. It reports pass, fail, not applicable or not run for each, and grows by one check after every release that fails in a way none of them caught. The same checklist is in the docs at `/publishing/release-readiness`.
- **The multiplayer skills call `Summer.initialize()` with no Game ID.** The summer.games bundle leaves `gameId` out, so an ID in code (or a fallback when it is missing) fails on the hosted server with `game_identity_mismatch` and every online join ends in `world_start_timeout`.
- `multiplayer-publish` explains why the server preset needs the `summer_authority` custom feature, adds a pre-upload step that runs the bundle's `server.pck` with no scene, a real online join after release, and what an empty server log does and doesn't mean. `multiplayer-testing` lists what Local Play can't catch; `make-game` plans online play reachable by default, server-saved progress and a way back to the title, and runs `release-readiness` before shipping.

Publishing a game from your agent now works end to end, with fewer surprises:

- Take store screenshots of real gameplay without opening the editor (`summer_capture_gameplay`).
- Make store-size art: ask `summer_generate_image` for an aspect ratio or a size.
- See the store tools as soon as your agent connects, and use them from the terminal (`summer tool`). `summer doctor` checks that the store accepts your sign-in.
- An export tells you first when your Summer Engine is too old, shows the engine's real error when it fails, and lists the project files it changed.
- A publish preview checks that the game exists before it asks you to confirm.
- `summer install --path` installs Summer.app into the folder you name, and every command uses that engine.
- New skills for running the engine safely from an agent and for games that also run on the Compatibility renderer.

### Added
- `summer_capture_gameplay` (CLI `summer tool capture-gameplay`): saves real gameplay frames (HUD included) without a running editor. It starts the game in the engine's offscreen verify instance (`--summer-verify`, real renderer, window offscreen, no focus, never `--headless`) at `resolution` (default `1920x1080`), waits `waitSeconds`, and saves `frames` PNGs to `<project>/.summer/captures/<time>/`. It imports a never-opened project first, passes `--summer-no-api`, and returns each frame's path with its real width and height. It warns when the stretch settings render another size.
- `summer_generate_image` `aspectRatio` (1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 5:4, 4:5, 21:9) and `width` + `height` (64 to 4096), sent to the image route as top-level fields. The server picks a model that reaches the size, or refuses a named model that cannot, before any spend. The result reports the real size and the model. The `options` description now says what the server really does. Until the server side ships, the new fields are accepted and ignored.
- `summer tool` runs a name that is not a local tool on the hosted Summer Engine MCP with the store sign-in (`summer tool summer_store_list_games`). `summer tool --list` lists the hosted tools after the local ones, or says to run `summer login --store`.
- `summer doctor` store-access check: with a store sign-in it calls `summer_store_list_games` (8 s limit) and shows the answer, or the store's code, message and request id on a refusal. Without a sign-in it says only publishing needs one.
- `summer doctor` shows the installed engine version and warns below 0.7.0, the first version that exports for summer.games.
- Skills `bounded-engine-runs` (run the engine from an agent with a time limit, a memory cap, one engine per project, muted and offscreen) and `compatibility-renderer-traps` (Forward+ games that also run on Compatibility: the instance-uniform budget, black MultiMesh colors, sRGB vertex colors, paired captures).

### Changed
- With a store sign-in, the first `tools/list` waits up to 5 s for the hosted mount, so hosts that list tools once see the store tools. Without a sign-in nothing waits. A slower mount still adds them later.
- `summer_export_game` reads the engine version before it writes any preset. Below 0.7.0 it stops with `engine_too_old` and says how to update; nothing is written to the project.
- `summer_export_game` runs the engine with `--summer-no-api`, so an export no longer starts the local engine API. The result lists `projectChanges` (top-level files created, changed or deleted) and warns when the engine rewrote `project.godot`.
- `summer_publish_build` checks the game in the store before the confirmation preview. An unknown id returns `game_not_found` with your real games. A platform the store page does not list returns a warning. The preview shows the game name and id.
- `summer install --path` on macOS installs to `<dir>/Summer.app` (before, the bundle's contents went loose into the folder). Each install is recorded in `~/.summer/engine-install.json`, and run, doctor and export use that engine before the default locations. Without a terminal, progress prints one line per 10%. After an install, a note says the first start of a new engine version can take several minutes.
- `export-and-ship` skill: store key art, covers and icons carry no text, logos or UI; screenshots are real gameplay and may show the game's own HUD. On the hosted-game error "is in the source graph's authority_engine domain", narrow the authority root in `source-domains.json`.

The old-engine hint appears only when the engine names a missing or invalid preset. A source-graph domain error gets its own recovery step.
