# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.38

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This release is about tools, templates and what an agent learns. Every harness (pi, Claude Code,
Codex, OpenCode) now calls MCP tools through one gate, finds tools with `tools_search` and runs scripts with `codemode`.
A template package installs from a GitHub address, names where its tools come from, takes typed input and answers in a
schema. A learning agent compiles its job into a learned workflow, runs it first, and serves a new version only after a
replay on graded runs. A Linux desktop opens apps and reads plainly in the timeline, and a program inside a computer can
no longer reach the desktop's session bus. A capped Codex, OpenCode or pi run pauses less often. There is no fresh store
this time: the SQLite store stays at version 11 and Postgres migrates itself. The launcher is `@parcha/agentrun` 0.4.6,
the Python client `parcha-agentrun` is 0.3.6, and the server image is
`ghcr.io/parcha-ai/agentrun-server:v0.1.0-beta.38` (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64).

> **No fresh store: beta.38 opens the data beta.37 left.** The SQLite schema is still version 11, and Postgres goes from
> 9 to 11 (migrations 0010 and 0011). Keep the same data folder and the same start command. On the Docker image that is
> `--data /data/b37 --listen 0.0.0.0 --port 7340 --drain-timeout 6s` as before, and on Render the Docker Command you set
> for beta.37 stays. Change only the image to `ghcr.io/parcha-ai/agentrun-server:v0.1.0-beta.38`. The console keeps its
> login, and your agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins are all still there.
>
> - **SQLite.** Two changes, both made by the server when it opens your folder, so there is nothing to run: a new table,
>   `imported_templates` (templates installed from GitHub, #2728), and an agent revision's MCP pin in a new column,
>   `revisions.mcp_pin`, in place of the per-run pin table `mcp_pins`, which is dropped (#2719). **Copy the data folder
>   before you upgrade.** beta.37 still opens the folder afterwards (it checks the schema version only, 11), but it writes
>   each run's MCP pin to `mcp_pins` at the run's first claim, so a run that grants an MCP tool fails on beta.37 once
>   beta.38 has dropped that table. To go back, restore the copy and set the image back to `v0.1.0-beta.37`; the command
>   stays.
> - **Postgres.** Migrations `0010_imported_templates.sql` and `0011_revision_mcp_pin.sql` run when the server starts,
>   and the server moves the schema to version 11. **Going back does not work without a backup:** beta.37 refuses a
>   schema at version 11, with `the Postgres schema agentrun is schema version 11, set up by a later release than this
>   one (this release knows version 9). Run that release or a later one.` **Take a backup of the store's schema before
>   you upgrade** (for example `pg_dump --schema=agentrun <url>`, with your own schema name if you set one), and to go
>   back restore it and run beta.37 on the restored data. Start the server first: a beta.38 runner started on a schema
>   the server has not yet migrated refuses to start, and so does a beta.37 runner on a migrated one, so upgrade the
>   server, then the runners.
> - Nothing else under the store changed shape. Agents you saved on beta.38 may carry fields beta.37 does not know
>   (`input_schema`, a computer's `surface` and `exec`, a template record); beta.37 reads past them.

## Highlights

- **One tool plane on every harness.**
  - A run's MCP tools are host tools on every harness: each call passes the run's one tool gate, the runner calls the
    server with the credential and books it, and OpenCode now runs MCP tools too (#2722).
  - Every harness offers `tools_search` (find a tool by what it does), `tools_call` (run one by name) and `codemode` (a
    JavaScript script over the run's tools), each gated, recorded and booked as the tool's own call (#2749). Past 20
    catalog tools (MCP and monid) a run defers them behind search, and each of the three has a setting you can deny
    (#2759).
  - On pi, a script's or `tools_call`'s nested calls show in the timeline as on the other harnesses (#2767).
  - One grammar for tool names, one MCP scrubber, cap and client, and `grant_problems` served on a saved server say why
    a tool can't be granted (#2690, #2738).
- **Templates from GitHub.** Install a template package from `github:<owner>/<repo>[/<path>]`, pinned to a commit, with
  an "Add from URL" box on Templates, `agentrun template install` on the CLI and a page that shows the publisher, the
  commit and every file before anything is stored (#2728). A template's MCP needs now name where their tools come from
  (Composio, GitHub or a URL), and apply maps each need to the saved server that matches (#2732). Apply grants only the
  tools you tick (#2718). The install and Apply screens show each run input, eval case and tool reason (#2789).
- **Typed run input.** An agentic agent can take a JSON Schema input (`definition.input_schema`); every path that starts
  a run checks it, and the console draws the run form from it (#2731). A template parameter is an input in the same
  grammar (#2775), and a list parameter fills a schedule's typed input (#2733).
- **An answer that meets its schema.** An agent with an `output_schema` is told the schema on every harness, is asked
  once more when its answer misses it, and the run serves `output_error` if it still does; the console's Report reads
  the structured answer (#2725).
- **Learning that compiles and proves itself.**
  - A learning agent writes its whole job as a learned workflow in a compile turn, with a record of each attempt in
    `GET /runs/{id}/learning` (#2641).
  - A run starts on a fitting learned workflow before the agent's own model takes a turn, and a money rule asks for a
    new version when the workflow costs more than the agent by hand (#2603).
  - A workflow step can carry a guard that hands the job back below a threshold (#2639).
  - A new version serves first only after a replay on the agent's graded runs, with thresholds refit from them (#2644).
  - The console's Learning tab walks through the loop: a five-stage strip says what is learned and what happens next, and
    the cost chart flags each new version, promotion, hold and refit on the run it first affected (#2654).
- **A Linux desktop that opens apps** (#2727, #2735). `computer.apps` lists, opens and closes apps on E2B and Agent37
  desktops, with a window manager so they are framed and focused, and a Mac and a Linux desktop read the same way.
- **A run on a computer reads plainly.** The timeline says what the agent did ("Pressed “Display”", "Typed “dark”"), one
  voice in the row, the call list and a Mac movie, with a code-mode script's calls on its own row (#2729, #2762,
  #2747). The Screen tab reads sooner and has one Take over (#2730, #2745, #2736).
- **Computer isolation.** A program running inside an E2B or Agent37 computer can no longer reach the desktop's
  accessibility bus or session bus (#2780, #2787, #2790, with the check in #2723). Nothing about what a computer can do
  for the agent changes: `nsenter` and rootless podman still work inside a computer.
- **Caps, tighter.** A capped Codex, OpenCode or pi (on OpenAI's Responses) run's next-step estimate is closer to its
  real input, so it pauses for a raise later and less often (#2772). The wrap-up note, the reserve and admission price a
  warm request alike, so a capped Codex or Claude Code run is no longer told to finish with most of its cap left
  (#2786).
- **ask_person on Claude Code and Codex** (#2743): a Claude Code or Codex agent can ask you a question mid-run. The run
  parks waiting for your reply, and your answer resumes it.

## Before you upgrade

- **A gateway must serve `/v1/messages` for Claude** (#2799). With `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` set, pi now sends a Claude model
  to `<base>/v1/messages` (as LiteLLM's proxy and OpenRouter serve it) instead of `/v1/responses`. A gateway that serves
  only Responses fails those runs. If you set `AGENT_MODEL_PRICE` for a Claude model, give it the fourth number, the
  cache-write price (Anthropic's is 1.25 times input): with three numbers, a cache write is booked at the input price.
- **A pinned tool takes only its listed arguments** (#2798). A call of an MCP tool that has a pin, in the agent's settings
  or the server's, is refused when it carries a top-level argument the tool's listing does not declare under `properties`
  (and is not pinned), and the model reads which one. A pin that relied on a server's undeclared alias (Slack's
  `channel_id`, Gmail's `to`) now fails that call: use the listed name, or drop the pin. Tools with no pin are unchanged.
- **A label goes with the grade** (#2648): a client that sent a grader's label as a follow-up message
  (`POST /runs/{id}/messages`) sends it as the grade's `label` (`PUT /runs/{id}/grade`) instead.
- **monid is granted per endpoint** (#2765). `monid.discover`, `monid.inspect` and `monid.run` are gone: an agent that
  grants one is refused at its save (422 `not_an_option`). Grant the endpoints it calls instead, `monid:<provider>/<endpoint>`
  (say `monid:apollo/people/match`) or `monid:<provider>/*` (at most 50), with a monid key saved in Settings → Tool keys.
  Each is pinned at the save with its description, input schema and price, and is one tool of its own on every
  harness. An endpoint monid prices by usage can't be granted (no hold could keep the cap), and a workflow can't bind a
  monid endpoint yet.
- **An agent's MCP tools are pinned when it is saved** (#2719), on its revision, not at each run's first claim. Every run
  of that revision calls the tools as the server listed them at the save, with their prices.
  - A save (a create, a definition PUT, a template's apply, an inline agent's first run of a version) is refused with 422
    on the tool's field when a granted server can't be listed right now or no longer lists a granted tool, and nothing
    is saved: save again once the server answers. Applying a template with a GitHub tool ticked on a server with no
    GitHub App connected is refused this way: connect GitHub in Settings and apply again.
  - To pick up a tool a server changed, save the agent again: that is a new revision with the new pin.
  - A revision saved before this release pins at its first run, once; nothing needs saving again. If one of its servers
    can't be listed then, the run is refused (409 `agent_not_runnable`) and the next run tries again.
- **The store.** No fresh store; see the note at the top. Copy the SQLite data folder, or back up the Postgres schema,
  first (#2719, and migration 0010 on Postgres): going back to beta.37 needs that copy.
- **Tool-call budgets are gone** (#2771). `max_tool_calls` on an agent definition and `budget.tool_calls` in a template
  manifest are refused as unknown fields, and the `subagent` tool takes no `max_tool_calls`. The count only ever held on
  pi; the run's spend cap and its wrap-up stop a runaway loop on every harness. Remove the field, put a count in the
  instructions if you want one, and set `per_run_usd` (a template's `budget` is now `{per_run_usd}`, required when
  `budget` is given).
- **MCP tools run as host tools** (#2722). A run parked on an MCP call before the upgrade does not resume that call:
  cancel it and start it again. A Codex thread started before the upgrade loses its MCP tools when it resumes: start a
  new run. claude-agent offers a granted tool as `mcp__hands__mcp__<server>__<tool>` and codex as `mcp_<server>__<tool>`;
  the Timeline, tool settings and approvals still name it `mcp:<server>/<tool>`.
- **Tool names are held to one rule** (#2690): `mcp:<server>/<tool>`, the server's name in lowercase letters, digits and
  `-` (at most 32, starting with a letter), the tool's in letters, digits, `_` and `-` (at most 64). A tool setting or
  template that names a tool with a `.`, a capital in the server name or an over-long name now gets 422 `not_allowed`.
  Rename it to the server's listed name, or drop it: no run could call it.
- **Tools you have not registered ask by default** (#2625): `mcp:<server>/<tool>` and a monid endpoint (#2765) default
  to ask, not allow. No tool of today's table changes.
- **Capped runs carry three more tool definitions** (#2749): `tools_search`, `tools_call` and `codemode` ride on every
  model request, about 2,000 bytes (639 tokens on Sonnet), so the smallest caps rise. A pi desktop run on Sonnet through
  a gateway needs $0.07 for its first request and $0.13 for five steps in `strict` mode, or $0.07 in `expected` mode (it
  was $0.06, $0.12 and $0.06). Straight to Anthropic it needs $0.04 for its first request. A run you cap at the old
  floor pauses for a raise.
- **Templates.**
  - **Parameters** (#2775): a parameter is required unless it says `required: false`, and a `default` is allowed only
    beside `required: false`. A package that left a parameter optional by omitting `required` adds `required: false`.
    `GET /v2/templates` serves `parameters` as a closed JSON Schema object, so a client that read
    `parameters.<name>.required` reads `parameters.required` and `parameters.properties.<name>`.
  - **MCP needs** (#2732): `server: <name>` in a template's `mcp` is removed; a package that still has it is refused with
    the new shape in the message. Replace it with `source` (`composio`, `github` or `url`) and `toolkit`. Inside the
    package its tools are `mcp:<toolkit>/<tool>`, and an apply's `grants` name them that way.
  - **code-review and release-notes** (#2732): their `repo` parameter is now `owner` and `repo`, their GitHub tools are
    pinned to that one repository, and the free-text searches that could not be pinned are dropped. Apply them again to
    get the new shape; an agent applied earlier keeps its own.
  - **inbound-lead** (#2732) reads nothing from HubSpot; its one HubSpot tool is an optional note on the contact the
    event names.
  - **market-monitor and inbound-lead** (#2810) no longer pin Slack's `channel_id` or Gmail's `to`: the gate refuses an
    argument a pinned tool doesn't list (#2798).
  - **Unticked tools are not granted** (#2718): an agent applied from a template before this release may still hold every
    tool of its MCP servers. Review its tools (or apply the template again) and remove the ones you did not mean to grant,
    above all on an agent set to `never`.
  - **Package folders** (#2774): the `schema` grader is gone (a graded run of a package that declares `output` is held to
    its schema by an `output` verdict, and a case with `graders/schema.md` is refused), the `examples/` folder and the
    `checks` field in agent.md are refused, and `GET /v2/templates` no longer serves `examples`.
  - **kyb** (#2731, #2766): it takes its subject as typed input (`company`, optionally `website`, `country`,
    `registration_number`, `reason`); a newly applied kyb refuses a run without `company`. Its report's `subject.input`
    holds those names, where it held `name` and `domain`. An agent applied from the earlier kyb keeps its own definition.
  - **Answer schema** (#2725): applying a template no longer copies its answer schema beside a skill's SKILL.md, because
    the runner gives the agent the schema itself. code-review's `findings.schema.json` is now
    `skills/review/findings.schema.json`.
- **Agents with an output schema** (#2725) have the schema appended to their instructions and get one more turn when the
  answer misses it, booked like any turn, under the run's cap.
- **Learning** (#2644, #2603): a learned workflow draft that gives two steps one label is refused at learn time, as a
  saved one already was. A learning agent whose workflow fits a run's input now answers it before the agent's model is
  asked; set `workflow_first: false` on a run to send it to the agent from its first turn.
- **Computers.**
  - **Daytona** (#2624, #2742): a Daytona computer's network can no longer be changed after create (it is refused), and
    Daytona takes no Archil mount: a create that asks for one is refused up front, and `DAYTONA_ARCHIL_EGRESS` is no
    longer read. A Mode 2 agent on a Daytona sandbox is refused at its save and its run's start. A Daytona computer made before this release carries no `agentrun.computer.name` label, so the provider no
    longer lists, attaches to or releases it: delete it in Daytona.
  - **Archil label** (#2712): an Archil computer made before this release on E2B, Daytona or Agent37 carries the mount
    in the older label form, so the provider reads it as one it never makes: delete it at the vendor. Modal's already
    held the new form.
  - **Daemon version** (#2715): a computer's daemon must match its provider's version and protocol exactly; a daemon
    whose `hello` names no `protocol` is refused.
  - **Agent37** (#2692): it never follows a redirect now, and reads a 408, 409, 410, 422 or 507 with no code of its own as
    timeout, invalid, not_found, invalid and limit, where it answered `vendor` for all five.
  - **Live view** (#2768): `screen.watch` on a Linux desktop needs the X server's DAMAGE extension and is refused
    without it. E2B, Agent37 and Orgo desktops, and Xvfb, have it.
  - **Timeline readers** (#2747, #2762): a `computer_calls` record always carries `started_at`; `computer_act` and
    `computer_observe` rows no longer show typed text, a click's point or a scroll's direction; `callWords` and
    `stepWords` answer the past tense. A reader that built its own start time or matched the old words reads the new.
  - A run's own computer can be code-only or tools-only, and can have no shell (`computer.surface`, `computer.exec`,
    #2740); nothing changes for an agent that sets neither.
- **For developers:**
  - The kernel's MCP door is removed (#2722): `SessionSpec.mcp`, `SessionMcp`, `McpClient`, `AdapterCapabilities`,
    `AgentAdapter.capabilities()`, `AdapterFacts.mcp`, `ModelProxyOptions.mcp`, `mcpRoute`, `McpHandler`,
    `McpRouteOptions` and `McpCallResult.parked` are gone; hand a session its MCP tools as host tools in
    `SessionSpec.tools`.
  - `@parcha/agentrun-harness-claude` no longer exports `CLAUDE_WEB_SEARCH_USD`; read `NATIVE_SEARCH_USD` from
    `@parcha/agentrun-kernel/host` (#2688).
  - The computer package: `E2BSandbox.commands` is now `rpc`, `sendStdin`, `closeStdin` and `kill` (#2716); the E2B and
    Modal SDK slice types are replaced by the SDKs' own (#2694); `HostFacts.labelRules` takes `maxBytes` and `measure`
    and `tagsOf` and `labelsOf` are gone from `dist/modal.js` (#2712); Daytona's `listLabelled`, `probe`,
    `daytonaCommands`, `DaytonaCreateOptions`, its timeouts and `dist/conformance/daytona-sweep.js` are gone (#2624);
    `Agent37Error` no longer carries `status` (#2692).
  - A computer `MachineHost` has twelve members (#2793): `prepare` and `testConnection` are gone (a keys test is one
    `list`, which must create nothing), `setTimer` and `setLabels` are one optional `extend`, `id` is `descriptor`, a
    provider's mounts and capabilities are read from `descriptorOf(id)` (the `MOUNT` and `CAPABILITIES` exports are
    gone), `hostedProvider(...)` is `new HostedProvider(...)`, and `Agent37Error` and `Agent37TunnelError` are gone (a
    tunnel failure is an `SshTunnelError`). The changelog lists each with what to do.
  - On the shared machine-host adapter, every `MachineHost` member answers its value or throws (a `HostError(code,
    message)`), never a `Result`; `exec` takes no `{ stdin }` flag; `Machine` is `{ id, labels, state, endsAt? }` with
    `state` one of `starting`, `running`, `stopped`, `gone`; `prepare`, `stop` and the stop facts are gone, and a hosted
    computer is deleted, never stopped and kept (#2792).
  - `GET /agents/{agent_id}` and its revisions serve the pin as `mcp_pin`: per server, the pinned tools and their prices,
    never the server's URL (#2719).
  - `computer-bench` (a private package) renames fields in `report.json`, counts a computer call as a step, and requires
    each `needs.apps` entry (#2778, #2739, #2741).
  - Template API: each template in `GET /v2/templates` has `id`, `bundled`, `source`, `sha`,
    `publisher`, `category` and `tags`; an agent applied from one carries `template: {id, version, sha}` (#2728, #2732).
    `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}` serves `input` and `file_ids` (#2774), and `result.output_error` is new on the TypeScript and
    Python clients (#2725).

## What you can do now

- Install a template from GitHub: `agentrun template install github:<owner>/<repo>/<path>@<ref> [--dry-run] [--trust]`,
  or Templates → Add from URL, and read the package before it is stored (#2728, #2789).
- Give an agent a typed input and get a run form drawn from it; a bad input is a 422 with one issue per field (#2731).
- Set a list in a template (`type: array`) and have it reach each scheduled run as a typed list (#2733), and filter a
  template's webhook trigger by a parameter, so a Composio project's one URL starts a run only for your repository
  (#2757).
- Ask a person a question from a Claude Code or Codex agent (#2743).
- Find a tool, call it by name or script several calls from any harness (#2749), and see Settings → Tools list each
  saved MCP server's tools with the permissions the server offers (#2764).
- Open an app on a Linux desktop, and let an agent do it (#2727, #2735).
- Give a desktop or a phone a code-only or tools-only surface, or no shell (#2740).
- See what the cost of a run reads like on every harness, and which tool calls were not priced (#2761).
- Let `web_fetch` read a site's atom, rss and JSON-LD feeds, such as a repository's `releases.atom` (#2773).
- Read why a saved MCP server's tool can't be granted, on every harness it fails on (#2738).
- Grant a monid endpoint by name, with its price held on the run's ledger before each call and named on the charge
  row ("Tool cost: monid charged $0.0260 for monid:apollo/people/match"); a re-priced endpoint is refused unsent
  (#2765).
- Fence an MCP tool's object argument to named keys in a pin, so an unattended CRM write sets one field and nothing else
  (`{"keys": ["hs_lead_score"]}`), also from a template parameter (#2798).
- Read why a learned workflow is held when its replay could not run an MCP tool: the hold names the tools with no
  `readOnlyHint`, and the Learning tab says what a promoted workflow was decided on (#2801).
- Replay a learned workflow on graded runs before it serves, and read each decision at
  `GET /agents/{id}/learning/promotions` (#2644); grade a run with `PUT /runs/{id}/grade`.
- Run an agent's computer use against a benchmark with `computer-bench`, now with a Linux desktop suite (#2577, #2744).
- Turn on **Allow reads** for a saved MCP server: its read-only tools run with no one asked, its writes keep asking, and
  a destructive call takes a second click to allow. A tool's effect comes from the server's annotations, and a tool with
  none still asks (#2782).
- Grant monid endpoints in the console's agent editor (Tools step, `monid:<provider>/<endpoint>` or
  `monid:<provider>/*`), with the server's own words for what a save left out or refused (#2822).
- Let a learned workflow's replay record an escalate that reads a judge's field instead of stopping on it, and let its
  refit switch an escalate or a guard off; a replay that hands back every input is held (#2815).

## Fixed

- **Runs:**
  - A run starts sooner: a runner in the server's process claims a new run as soon as it is queued, and a first claim no
    longer asks the vendor to list older computers of the run (#2754).
  - A trigger's message that reaches a run just as it comes to wait on a person is delivered after the person's answer,
    where before it was refused and its firing still read `sent` (#2769).
  - A code-mode script replayed after a restart records each computer call once (#2755).
  - A CLI look-back cut by a lost runner is asked again once, not twice, and its spend stays the look-back's (#2668).
- **Spend:**
  - A capped Codex, OpenCode or pi run's input estimate counts text at its own bytes, and on a route straight to OpenAI
    counts the input exactly (#2772).
  - A capped run on Codex or Claude Code prices its next request from the cache its previous request left warm, so a
    Codex run under $0.50 is no longer told to finish with $0.45 left (#2786).
  - A Codex or Claude Code run under a small cap (say $0.50) now finishes a job of a few cents, including after an
    approval or a deny (#2791, with #2786). A run resumed within 4 minutes, or a request sent after Codex's own side
    request, is priced from the cache. A request leaves room in the cap for the tool calls it starts while it streams.
    The cap still holds: a run never spends past it.
  - Behind serve's gateway, pi sends a Claude model on Anthropic's Messages API, so its prompt cache works: the second
    turn of a run reads the prompt from cache where every turn paid full input. The gateway must serve `/v1/messages`
    beside `/v1/responses` (LiteLLM's proxy and OpenRouter do); other models stay on the Responses API (#2799).
  - A CLI turn cut by a park (a host tool call held for your approval) is booked at the usage its provider reported,
    where the run's cost read `unpriced` (#2737).
  - A monid call's approval card shows its price: the hold at the endpoint's pinned price (#2687, #2765).
  - A paid call books on the run's one ledger or is not sent: a monid call, Parallel search and extract, and the browser
    refuse a call with no run to book under, and a learned workflow's web nodes book on the run's ledger (#2714).
  - The per-process spend engine is deleted; the run's ledger is the only count (#2724).
  - A run's usage row reads the same on every harness: "Cost: …" once a run ends, "Cost so far: …" only while it goes,
    Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode count tool calls with no price, and a failed request with no price says its cost is
    unknown (#2761).
  - An agent's cost per run counts only its own runs, and a run's cost and path land under load (waits up to 30 s, not 2
    s); the series says how many runs' paths are not known (#2642).
  - A long answer through an OpenAI Responses gateway that writes its JSON with spaces (LiteLLM) is priced; a request
    that answered while its runner's claim was lost is booked at its cost when the run resumes, also in a learned
    workflow; a run cancelled while its first request is being admitted never sends it and costs $0; and an unknown

# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.37

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This release opens the second phase of computers: Take over works end to end, a person can pair
their own computer (a Mac runs Computerd, a phone runs phoned), and every harness drives a desktop or a phone through
one surface. Composio is a preset and a trigger source. A run's grade stays under its cap, a Postgres race that lost
commands is fixed, and a web search setting now decides every native search. The learning loop is still in progress: a
note must hold beyond its one input, and the Learning tab and a CSV are in, but the compile, guard and promote stack is
not. The launcher is `@parcha/agentrun` 0.4.5, the Python client `parcha-agentrun` is 0.3.5, and the server image is
`ghcr.io/parcha-ai/agentrun-server:v0.1.0-beta.37` (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64).

> **Breaking: beta.37 needs a fresh store again.** The store's schema moved since beta.36: SQLite goes from version 6
> to 11 (five bumps) and Postgres gains five migrations (0005 to 0009). A server from beta.36 or earlier will not start
> on its old data folder. It stops with `the store at <folder>/store.sqlite is schema version 6; this build knows
> version 11`. There is no migration for SQLite. Start beta.37 on a new, empty folder with `--data <new folder>`, and
> leave the old folder as it is: the earlier release still opens it, so you can go back. On the Docker image, keep the
> volume at `/data` and give the image these arguments in place of its default command (`docker run ... <image>
> <arguments>`, or `command:` in compose): `--data /data/b37 --listen 0.0.0.0 --port 7340 --drain-timeout 6s`. On
> Render, the Docker Command replaces the image's entrypoint too, so set it to the whole start:
> `/opt/agentrun/packages/serve/launcher/agentrun-serve -- /usr/bin/tini -- node
> /opt/agentrun/packages/serve/dist/cli.js --data /data/b37 --listen 0.0.0.0 --port 7340 --drain-timeout 6s`. To go
> back, set the image to beta.36 and clear the command (the beta.36 folder, `/data/b36`, is as you left it). The console
> asks for setup again on the new folder (paste `AGENTRUN_TOKEN` and set a password). Your `AGENTRUN_TOKEN` and
> `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` stay as they are. Then add your agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins again. A Postgres store
> migrates itself.

> earlier release still opens it, so you can go back. On the Docker image, keep the volume at `/data` and give the
> image these arguments in place of its default command (`docker run ... <image> <arguments>`, or `command:` in

> `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` stay as they are. Then add your agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins again. A Postgres store
> migrates itself.

## Highlights

- **Computers, phase 1.** Every computer, browsers included, is made from its provider's one descriptor:
  - One browser stack: every browser session is a browser computer, driven by pi-browser's raw-CDP driver, whether the
    agent's computer is a browser or the tool plane picks the vendor (#2550).
  - An agent's own computer, kept between its runs: `computer: { ..., persistent: true }` on Orgo's Linux desktop. Each
    run's end suspends it with its memory and disk, and the next run resumes it (#2547).
  - An Archil disk per agent, made on its first run; a run's start can name another disk with `archil_disk` (#2296).
  - A phone says its Android version, and the server image carries adb. A server without adb says so in Settings, at the
    claim and at the run's start (#2453).
  - A GPU computer that can't mount the run's folder is refused in the provider's own words (#2548).
  - A person can take over a runner run's desktop or phone and hand it back (#2581).
- **Stop ends the turn, not the run** (#2430). A stopped run waits for your next message, and a completed agentic run
  takes a follow-up. Cancel still ends a run for good. This changes the SQLite schema; see below.
- **Current model defaults** (#2569): Claude Agent `claude-sonnet-5-5`, Codex `openai/gpt-6-luna`, OpenAI and OpenRouter
  `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- **Retired packages** (#2278, #2553, #2554): `@parcha/pi-transport`, `@parcha/agentrun-pi`, `@parcha/pi-durable-disk`
  and `@parcha/pi-durable-agent` are no longer built or published. The server runs workflows on its own code.

## Before you upgrade

- **SQLite data directories need a fresh start** (#2430). The SQLite schema is now version 6. This release refuses a
  data directory an earlier release set up (`SchemaVersionUnknown`): start it on a new, empty data directory and add your
  agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins again, or keep the old directory on the earlier release. A Postgres store
  migrates itself (migration 0004).
- **Archil: one disk per agent** (#2296). `PUT /v2/workspace/archil` no longer takes `diskId` (sending it is a 422); send

  `@parcha/agentrun-pi`, `@parcha/pi-durable-disk` or `@parcha/pi-durable-agent` keeps 0.1.0-beta.35. The server needs
  none of them. If your code imported `@parcha/agentrun-pi` because the server brought it in, add it to your own
  dependencies (#2251). The research example takes `--config <module>` for its agent steps.
- **Capabilities** (#2278, #2553): `capabilities.runtimes` is `["runner"]`; a box's `state` is `ready` or `unavailable`,
  never `preparing`. A Daytona or Modal box reports `network: none`. The server no longer builds an `agentrun-box` image
  at its start; an `agentrun-box:*` image left on a Docker host can be removed.
- **Browsers** (#2550): Browserbase and Kernel browsers refuse run code and `browser_upload`; `run` takes actions only and

  `@browserbasehq/sdk` peer dependency; put a session's options in `spec.browser`. The Browserbase and Kernel providers
  take no host transport (`api`, `request`, `urls`, `liveUrls`) (#2586).
- **Orgo persistence** (#2547): an Orgo spec whose labels carry `agentrun.owner`, `agentrun.owner-server` or

- **Learning** (#2256, #2455): a run that merged before this upgrade reads as merged, with no item decisions and no
  `skills` or `workflows` listed. A learned item whose front matter can't be read reads `retired` with
  `by: "host", why: "unreadable"`.
- **For developers:** exports nothing in AgentRun used are gone from `@parcha/agentrun-dsl` and its `/recovery` entry
  (#2554), `@parcha/agentrun-kernel` (the delegate tool, the follow-up turn and some helpers, #2431; `BoxRecorder` and

  `@parcha/agentrun-serve` (`ASK_TOOL`, `ToolEntry`, `FauxHelpers`, `TokenSource`, `banner`, #2560).
  `ServeOptions.messageOrigin` (#2590) and the test hooks `beforeAbort`, `beforeReopenLaunch`, `hostMemory` and
  `onRunLoad` (#2591) are gone. A workflow run's decision receipts are read only in the keyed form (#2557).

## What you can do now

- Run subagents: a pi agent that names `subagent` in its tools hands a fresh conversation a prompt and a subset of its
  tools, on its own model or a `fast` or `strong` tier, under the run's one cap (#2493).
- Start a run in a checkout of the pull request that started it, with no GitHub token in the agent's reach:
  `checkout: pull_request` (#2485).
- Let a template name the computer it prefers and fall back: `computer: [shell, none]` (#2495).
- See which model each node ran on, and its tier, on a learned workflow's call and a workflow run's graph (#2513).
- Keep the browser while you answer: a run waiting on its person keeps its browser for the person's window, 15 minutes by

## Fixed

- **Runs:** a stop wins over a queued run's first input and over an answer that slipped past it (#2372); a second answer
  to one approval is refused as already answered on SQLite and Postgres alike (#2528); a message to an archived run says

  carries that version's name (#2395); model requests wait out a provider's 429 or 5xx for about two and a half minutes
  instead of ending the run (#2561).
- **Spend:** a run parked at its cap sends nothing more on that claim (#2493); a spend under a cent reads "less than a
  cent" (#2536); a CLI run whose requests weren't booked reads its cost as unknown, never $0 (#2487); a cap-refused

- **Claude Code and Codex:** a run installs its harness on first use again (#2375).
- **Computers:** an agent with no computer is shown only the shell tools its run gets (#2366); Settings offers no
  computer that needs a network where the server allows none (#2390); a phone's screen no longer stalls the server

- **Learning:** learning keeps one copy of each rule, and a standing rule proposed as a skill is kept as a note (#2256);
  a learned workflow's text answer comes back as written (#2452).
- **Server:** the run-end reader no longer rebuilds every recent run's view four times a second (#2535); a store timeout
  names who held the store (#2367).
- **Security:** the Docker egress proxies run Node 22.23.5 (#2538).
- **Docs:** an MCP server's preview says its tool list is the server's offer, not what the credential allows (#2499); the

- **Releases:** a fragment the previous release's tag carried stays in that release's changelog section when a later pull

- **Computers:** Archil settings can come from the server's environment (#2521), and Archil is reached through an egress

- **Templates:** code-review template 0.3.0 runs eight particle-1 reviewers on a read-only checkout of the pull request
