# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.35

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This is a security release: AgentRun now requires Node.js 24.22.3, and the server image runs on
it. It also caps an agent's tool calls, makes a learned workflow an agent of its own, shows learning at work in the
console, and fixes runs on the runner. The launcher is `@parcha/agentrun` 0.4.3, and the Python client `parcha-agentrun`
is 0.3.3.

## Before you upgrade

- **Node.js 24.22.3 or later is required** (#2516). Node's November 2026 security releases fix 16 CVEs, seven of them
  HIGH (HTTP/2 use-after-frees and crashes, an HTTPS heap disclosure, a TLS handshake crash and a client-certificate
  bypass through TLS 1.2 renegotiation). We checked each against AgentRun's own code: none is reachable there. AgentRun
  runs no `http2`, `https` or `tls` server (the server, the model proxy and the egress proxies speak cleartext HTTP/1.1
  behind your TLS proxy, and the egress proxies pass TLS through without terminating it), uses no `https.Agent`, and
  never runs under `--permission` or Node's built-in env proxy. The upgrade still matters: the release updates llhttp,
  which parses every request the server and the egress proxies receive, and undici behind `fetch`; and a host that
  embeds AgentRun's packages in its own `https` or `http2` server gets the fixes.
  - Every package's `engines` asks for `>=24.22.3`, and the checks now compare the patch: `npx @parcha/agentrun` on any
    older Node, 24.22.0 to 24.22.2 included, exits with one line: `AgentRun needs Node.js 24.22.3 or newer; you have
    v24.22.2.`
  - The server image runs Node 24.22.3 over `debian:trixie-slim` (pinned by its multi-arch index digest), installed from
    nodejs.org by a script that fails the build unless the release's signed `SHASUMS256.txt` verifies against the pinned
    release key and the tarball matches it. The official `node:24.22.3` image wasn't yet published for amd64 and arm64;
    the image moves back to it in the next release. A Render or compose deploy picks up the new server image with the new
    image tag.
  - The Docker egress proxies stay on Node 22.23.4 in this release, behind Node 22's own patch (22.23.5). None of the
    release's CVEs reaches them: they speak cleartext HTTP and pass TLS through without terminating it. They move to Node
    22.23.5 in the next release (#2538).
- **Why the launcher is 0.4.3, not 0.5.0:** the launcher's only change is that Node floor. It stays on the 0.4 line so
  `npx @parcha/agentrun@0.4` (the line agentrun.ai pins) reaches this security release at once; a 0.5.0 would leave
  everyone on that pin on 0.4.2 until the site moved. A Node below 24.22.3 is refused in words, never run.
- **Learned workflow nodes of a tier run on the tier's model** (#2408): on the runner, a learned workflow node that names
  `fast` or `strong` now runs on the host's `AGENT_MODEL_FAST` or `AGENT_MODEL_STRONG`, at that model's price, under the
  run's cap, on every harness. A host that sets one of those to a model it can't reach should unset it or make it
  reachable: such a node now fails the workflow call with why, where it used to run on the run's own model.
- **Computers** (#2312):
  - Local Chrome is now the provider `local-chrome`: an agent saved with `{ kind: "browser", provider: "local" }` is
    refused at its run's start; set it to `local-chrome`.
  - Orgo offers Linux desktops only; an agent whose Orgo computer names the `windows` or `macos` image is refused at its
    run's start, naming `linux`. Release Orgo computers made by an earlier release before upgrading: the janitor sweeps
    them at its next pass.
  - A vendor's own failure is error code `vendor`, with the provider's id in its `vendor` field, where it was `docker`,
    `daytona`, `modal`, `e2b`, `orgo` or `phone`.
- **For developers:** `@parcha/agentrun-dsl` and its `/recovery` entry drop exports nothing called (#2494);
  `@parcha/agentrun-computer`'s root no longer exports the provider classes: import each from its subpath, or build one
  with `providerFor(id, options)` (#2312).

## What you can do now

- Cap an agent's tool calls: `max_tool_calls: N` on its definition (a template's `budget.tool_calls`) gives each
  conversation of a pi run N tool calls; past N the gate refuses each further call with one message telling the model to
  stop calling tools (#2501).
- Make an active learned workflow an agent of its own: "Make this an agent" on the Learning tab makes a workflow agent
  whose runs run the workflow's nodes with no agent loop; pipelines and triggers can call it (#2340).
- See learning at work: a learned workflow's call lists the nodes that ran on the run's Timeline, with each node's
  status, label, kind and time; the server's `tool_result` row carries `learned_nodes` (#2337).
- Write a learned workflow draft whose call node runs an MCP tool the agent's revision grants, by name or under
  `mcp:<server>/*` (#2479).
- See a run's cost beside its spend cap in the console header ("$0.0059 est. of $1.00"), and the new cap after a raise
  (#2482).
- `release-notes` makes its own GitHub trigger on the repository it was applied to (#2423).
- Pick a computer's image: `computer: { kind, provider, image }` selects one of the provider's configurations (such as
  `{ kind: "desktop", provider: "orgo", image: "linux" }`), and `GET /v2/computers` lists each provider's images (#2312).
- Run a read-only shell on Archil with its egress denied: a run whose bash has a policy runs each command on Archil's
  serverless exec with no network (#2507).
- Read a schedule in your own time: "At 3:00 AM your time (08:00 UTC), only on Monday · next Mon Nov 16, 3:00 AM EST"
  (#2488).

## Fixed

- **Security:** a shell under a read-only bash policy runs git with its config locked down, so reading another checkout
  can't run a program git config names (#2476); on Archil, execs run in an image with git 2.47 by default, so a
  read-only agent gets git there (#2505); a tool call the runner runs again after a crash meets the run's gate again
  (#2379); a GitHub disconnect reaches running runs at once, and no run's GitHub token outlives it (#2241); a Claude
  Code, Codex or OpenCode run's CLI starts under `no_new_privs` on Linux, as pi's commands do, so a setuid program grants
  it nothing (#2540).
- **Spend:** a capped run that reads screenshots is no longer refused at its cap after the first one (#2496); a raised
  run's follow-up on the runner is the server's ("AgentRun: The cap was raised to $X; continue the task."), and the
  raise's answer names it (#2470); a learning run whose cap was raised mid-run looks back on the raised budget (#2491); a
  paid tool call's cost row names the tool it ran (#2439); a paid call's pause counts the spend when the pause lands,
  and never refuses a person's answer to the question the turn ended on (#2542); a capped workflow run's raise too
  small for its step shows the new pause at the raised cap, and a decision whose price can't be read for a moment is
  read again before its node fails (#2437).
- **Console:** an agent card's chips stay on one row at every width (#2543).
- **Runs on the runner:** a run keeps the files it was started with, and a message sent mid-turn is answered (#2466); a
  run a provider's content filter stopped fails `moderated` in words a person can act on (#2468); runs left by a stopped
  server are taken up correctly by the next start (#2459); a data root serves one server again, and a replacing server
  waits for the old one (#2410).
- **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode:** a run's scratch folder on the server's machine is removed when its claim ends (#2460);
  a Claude Code or Codex call that needs approval shows on the Timeline while it waits, and a stop withdraws it (#2445).
- **Browser:** a browser that opens with the agent's saved profile tells the model that sites open signed in (#2498).
- **Postgres:** a write held up by the server's own process no longer rolls back a transaction that was fine (#2454).
- **Docs:** the server reference's Daytona GPU section says what the code allows: one H100 from the `daytona-gpu`
  snapshot, with 16 vCPUs, 100 GiB of memory and 400 GiB of disk, and no mount (#2517).
- **Releases:** the release workflow folds the changelog fragments the tag carries, so a pull request that merges just
  before a release's tag ships with its changelog line, with no refold (#2511).

## Known limits

- `deploy/compose.yaml` (a server and runners) has no Docker socket, so its agents get file tools and `web_fetch` but no
  shell; for a Docker sandbox, use the root `compose.yaml`, run the server on the host, or use a Daytona or E2B computer.
- The other limits listed for beta.32 still hold.

# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.34

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This patch prices Claude Code, Codex and workflow runs, queues starts past the run limit instead
of refusing them, makes a stop drain, and adds GPU computers on Modal and Daytona. The launcher is `@parcha/agentrun`
0.4.2, and the Python client `parcha-agentrun` is 0.3.2.

## Before you upgrade

- **Save the outbound webhook again.** The webhook (its URL, signing secret and outbox) now lives in the store, on SQLite
  and Postgres alike. The server no longer reads `webhook.json` or `webhook-outbox.json` from the data directory, so a
  webhook saved before must be saved again (`PUT /v2/settings/webhook`, which shows a new secret once), and messages
  still pending in the old outbox are not sent; let them drain first. The old files can be deleted (#2346, #2295).
- **A gateway model the catalog lists only at $0 has no price now**: set `AGENT_MODEL_PRICE` for it, or a run under a
  spend cap is refused (#2359).
- **An agentic run's structured answer is `result.output`**: a client that parsed `result.final_answer` reads
  `result.output` instead. An agent applied from a template before this release has no `output_schema`: apply the
  template again, or `PUT` its definition with the template's schema. A trigger's run message now ends with the
  previous result (#2467).
- **A learned skill or draft whose front matter doesn't read one way now reads retired**: fix its front matter (one
  plain `status:` line) to use it (#2465).
- **`/api/*` is gone** (the old store page's read-only JSON): read the same through `/v2` (#2086). The clients and the
  CLI drop the routes only a browser or GitHub calls (#2264).
- **A Daytona GPU computer** is made from Daytona's `daytona-gpu` snapshot with its one H100, and no mount (#2411).
  Browser hand-over requests an earlier server wrote as files in a run's workspace are not read (#2403).
- **If a Claude Code or Codex install fails after upgrading**, delete `<data>/harnesses` and start the server again:
  each harness installs anew on its first use. The server no longer removes the install an earlier build left at the top
  of that folder (#2305).
- **A stop now drains.** The server's own runner lets each busy run finish its turn for up to `--drain-timeout` (default
  30s), and a runner process for up to `--drain-timeout` or `AGENTRUN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (default 6s), before handing the rest
  back. For the old instant hand-back, pass `--drain-timeout 0s`. A runner now holds at most `--max-runs` runs (a runner
  process: `--loops`), by default as many pi runs as the host's memory holds, where it took up to 300 (#2267).
- **A start over the run limit is queued, not refused**: it answers `202` with the run `queued`, where it answered `429
  rate_limited`. A client that retried on that 429 can drop the retry and follow the run (#2345).
- **API changes** (#2294): `GET`/`PUT /v2/agents/{id}/home` are gone (use `/v2/agents/{id}/home/files`);
  `POST /v2/runs/{id}/kill` is gone (use `/stop` or `/cancel`); the `no_sealing_key`, `store_unreadable` and
  `file_unreadable` codes are gone; `seal_key_missing` reads `seal_key_changed` (tool keys) or `unreadable` (webhook). A
  run's `place` and capabilities' `models`, `places`, `tools` and `learning` are now always present.
- **A `tool-settings.json` in the data directory is no longer read**: set the tools once in Settings → Tools (or `PUT
  /v2/settings/tools`), then delete the file (#2299).
- **Computers made by an earlier version** on Daytona, E2B, Orgo and Modal are refused at `attach` and `connect`
  (their daemon names no fence; Modal's spec tag records no runtime): release them and make them again (#2276).
- **Forgotten sign-ins:** a forgotten browser sign-in's pointer is now kept for good (the server kept the newest 32 per
  agent). If an agent forgot more than 32 before the upgrade, read its learning for an old pointer and retire any note
  that holds one (#2250).
- **Learning:** `reflectTimeoutMs` is gone from `startServe` (the runner's deadline holds); learning grades recorded
  before the upgrade read unknown in `/v2/usage` (#2120). A run started before the upgrade whose learning seed failed
  reads no reason (#2257).
- **For developers:** `@parcha/pi-browser` drops `/coding-agent`, `/recorder` and `/providers/assigned`, with no shim
  (#2280); a `TOOLS` entry bound with a run ledger must pass the ledger's `flush` (#2324); the computer conformance
  report's `daemon` is now `daemons` (#2378); `@parcha/agentrun-kernel`'s registry has no browser kind (a host drives a
  browser computer with its own browser tool) (#2284); `startServe` drops nine options it never read (#2442); a
  program that calls the kernel's `checkedOnce` with its own check passes an async one (#2389).
- **An API client reading approval cards** finds `mcp_arguments` and `mcp_calls` first on a `learned_workflow` call whose
  workflow calls MCP tools set to ask (#2424).

## What you can do now

- See what Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and workflow runs cost: their model requests are counted at what the run's model
  proxy booked (#2303, #2232), and a learning run's grade is priced (#2289).
- Give an agentic run a structured answer: `output_schema` on its definition, and a completed run's `result.output` is
  its final answer's last fenced JSON block when that meets it; templates set theirs at apply (#2467).
- Let a learned workflow call the agent's MCP tools, held to the run's tool gate: allow runs, deny refuses the workflow,
  ask parks once with the tools named on the approval card (#2424).
- Make an agent's bash read-only (`tool_settings.bash.policy: "read-only"`) (#2418); see a tool its runs wouldn't get
  marked unavailable on the agent's page, with the reason (#2469).
- Ask for a template's schedule in words: a string parameter can say it is a `cron` line or a `timezone`, and the
  console shows a schedule picker (#2370).
- See a consolidating note's "Replaces N older notes" on the Learning tab (#2351); workflow drafts are dry-run before
  they are kept (#2293); MCP call nodes read "<tool> on <server>" on the workflow graph (#2417).
- Run GPU computers on Modal and Daytona; the loopback fence now holds on gVisor (#2276). On Daytona a GPU computer is
  one H100 from the `daytona-gpu` snapshot, with its 16 vCPUs, 100 GiB of memory and 400 GiB of disk, and no mount
  (#2411).
- Run browser computers (Browserbase, Kernel, Local Chrome) on a real server, where a run used to fail at its claim;
  Local Chrome needs no vendor and no key. Only pi drives a browser computer; another harness is refused at the start
  (#2284).
- Fence Local Chrome with the operator's `AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW`: its proxy then reaches only those hosts; unset, it stays
  open, and under `none` it is refused at the start (#2400).
- Start runs past the limit and have them queue (#2345); a runner never takes more runs than its host's memory holds
  (#2352).
- Recreate a Postgres deploy and have the schema handed over at once; a lost owner connection is taken back (#2263).
- Let a learned workflow ask its typed questions on the runner (#2338), get workflow drafts once a job repeats (#2282,
  #2325), and give each run the notes that bear on it once they outgrow the budget (#2274).
- Read an MCP answer too long to read whole, with `read` and no shell, so the code-review template reviews a large diff
  without a sandbox (#2329).
- Run `particle-ai/particle-1` on OpenRouter mostly from the prompt cache, about a sixth of the cost (#2361).
- Replay recorded data in `agentrun-serve eval-template`, and keep each run's metrics in its report (#2332, #2347).
- Read the computer protocol as a published spec, `spec/computer/` (#2268).

## Fixed

- **Runs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode):** an MCP call waiting for approval shows on the Timeline with its approval and
  runs once when allowed (#2237, #2376); a call the gate refuses shows as on pi (#2355); a skill-file read shows (#2313);
  a learning run reads "reflecting" during its end-of-run turn (#2365).
- **Runner:** a command held before the run's loop was chosen is no longer lost (#2201); a stop sent before then can't
  end the whole runner (#2362); `--drain-timeout` and `--max-runs` are honoured (#2267).
- **Approvals:** an answer after a stop or cancel is a 409 (#2353); an answer while the run parks or ends no longer fails
  with "Session is closed" (#2297); `run.needs_input` is sent once per wait (#2295).
- **Computers:** a person's take-over ends in words when the run changes runner (#2357); a run no longer lets go a
  desktop or phone a person holds (#2290); an explicit `AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW=none` is honoured for vendor-network computers
  (#2272); three small fixes (#2273); a browser hand-back resumes the agent within half a second, not up to 30 s later
  (#2391).
- **Spend:** a run with a spend cap no longer passes it quietly: it ends `spend_cap_reached`, and a paid call cut by a
  crash or a model with no price never reads $0 (#2386); a browser run's money is counted once (#2405); a workflow run
  stopped mid-stream books what streamed (#2420).
- **Runs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode):** a message sent while the run works is no longer lost (#2404), and says so
  when sent again after a runner restart (#2461); a run's effort falls back to its revision's `thinking`, then
  `AGENT_THINKING` (#2448); thinking shows on the Timeline for bridged models (#2433).
- **Approvals:** on Postgres an approve and a deny sent at once write one answer (#2401), and a store holding two
  refuses the start in words (#2428); on a run with no computer, `bash` asks first when no setting names it (#2450).
- **Server:** writes no longer answer 500 while the server's process is held up (#2354); computers a crashed runner left
  are ended (#2321); a SIGTERM during a runner's start stops it (#2451); `AGENTRUN_BOX_CPUS`, `_MEMORY` and `_PIDS` size a
  Docker computer again (#2456); a run's folder is its workspace, which the server neither trusts nor writes (#2419).
- **Console:** Settings → Computers no longer shows Docker ready with no Docker daemon (#2298).
- **Clients and CLI:** list commands take `--all`, and the CLI and clients say what the server does (#2342); a client's
  wait lasts its whole time (#2387).
- **Learning:** a note proposing a bank account, IBAN, routing or sort-code number is refused (#2358); a held secret is
  cut in more spellings (#2238); a grade that contradicts itself is asked again (#2425).
- **macOS:** a local run's file calls work again (each folder open failed with EINVAL) (#2384).
- **Deploy:** `deploy/compose.yaml` passes `AGENTRUN_STORE_POOL_SIZE` to the server and every runner (#2373).
- **Security:** on macOS, a run's folder can't reach host files through a symlink swapped in mid-walk (#2260, #2364);
  learning reads cut more of what the server never shows (#2250); the grader drops a note holding an account number
  (#2348); a loopback address at a sentence's end is rewritten whole (#2317).
- **Agents:** an edit racing a revision change is rebuilt or answers `412` with `If-Match` (#2294).
- **Console:** leaving the agent builder with unsaved changes asks first (#2314); a Learning card's footer isn't squeezed
  (#2309); a live timeline never says `working` before its message's row (#2308).
- **Learning:** a run keeps what it can when part of its answer breaks a cap (#2254); a run whose only work was its
  learned workflows skips the end-of-run turn (#2287).
- **Workflows:** a dry run no longer builds an unbounded value from a workflow's schemas (#2326).

## Known limits

- `deploy/compose.yaml` (a server and runners) has no Docker socket, so its agents get file tools and `web_fetch` but no
  shell; for a Docker sandbox, use the root `compose.yaml`, run the server on the host, or use a Daytona or E2B computer.
- The other limits listed for beta.32 still hold.

# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.33

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This is the first patch release after beta.32: fixes from launch QA, Docker sandboxes when the
server runs in a container, and the seal key kept with the data. The launcher is `@parcha/agentrun` 0.4.1, and the Python client `parcha-agentrun` is 0.3.1.

**Before you upgrade:** the seal key now lives in the data directory. If you started beta.32 without
`AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`, its key was made under your config home (`~/.config/agentrun/seal.key`), and beta.33 no longer
reads it there. Set `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` to that key's value before you start beta.33, the same in every process, or the
server refuses to start on a store sealed with another key. See "Upgrading".

## What you can do now

- Run Docker sandboxes from a server in a container: the root `compose.yaml` starts each run's sandbox beside the
  server on the host's Docker (Engine 26 or later), the run's folder mounted from the data volume. The sandbox's egress
  proxy refuses the Docker host's own addresses, which the server reads at its start; `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_HOST_ADDRESSES`
  adds ones no interface shows (a NAT'd or elastic public address). Where that can't be made safe, Docker is
  unavailable at the start in words, so a run that names it is refused at its start instead of failing at create.
- Raise a paused run's spend cap and have it hold: the next model request is admitted under the raised cap, on this
  runner or any that takes the run over, and a later pause names the raised cap. A raise of a run a person stopped is
  refused in words.
- Keep the seal key with the data: with no `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`, the server keeps its key in `seal/seal.key` in the data
  directory, beside the store, so a disk or volume carries its key. Back the two up together. The store records the
  key's fingerprint, and the server, every runner and `import` refuse a key that doesn't match it.
- Read what a run's learning changed again: `GET /v2/runs/{id}/learning/diff` and the run's "What it changed" box answer
  from the store.
- See, per model key in Settings → Model keys, the harnesses that key runs on this server.
- Get started from an empty console: the Playground, Runs and Triggers pages say what to do first, with buttons to
  create an agent, start a run or browse templates.
- Use a console that's all on its design system: the sign-in page follows the light or dark theme, orange text passes
  4.5:1 in the light theme, every field has a visible edge and focus ring, a failed read shows one error with Try again,
  tabs move with the arrow keys, and a page image opens in a dialog with a Close button.
- See each provider's icon on Settings → Model keys. The icons load from Google's favicon service, so the console now
  loads one thing from the network (the page's `img-src` allows those hosts); blocked or offline, a provider shows its
  bundled mark or a key icon.
- Hand an agent to your own coding agent: "Build with your coding agent" on the agents list, "Edit with your coding
  agent" on an agent's page and "Run with your coding agent" in its run bar open a dialog where you pick Claude Code or
  Codex (app or CLI), then review, edit and copy a prompt that points it at this server. The prompt holds no
  credential; copying sends nothing.
- Run the server on a Postgres schema an administrator made ahead of time, with a role that owns that schema and has no
  `CREATE` on the database. On a schema that doesn't exist, such a role is refused at the start in words that say what
  to do.
- Size the Postgres store's pool: `AGENTRUN_STORE_POOL_SIZE` sets how many connections the server and each runner hold
  (1 to 1000, default 10).
- Serve the run routes alone: `AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1` runs the server behind your own backend, with only a run's routes
  (launch, read, lists, timeline, messages, stop, cancel, kill, cap raise, files, uploads), capabilities, health and
  usage. Every other address answers 404 and the server has no accounts. Off by default.

## Fixed

- **Runs:** a run's final answer is served whole in its result, Report and Timeline; it was cut at 2,000 characters
  (#2224).
- **Runs:** cancelling or stopping a run parked at its cap ends it at once.
- **Runs:** a pi run's tool screenshots (browser, desktop, phone) reach the model on OpenRouter and OpenAI routes (#2184).
- **Runs:** a run parked at its cap no longer shows a "Model request failed" row for the cap's own refusal.
- **Runs:** Claude Code and Codex Timeline rows carry the time they were written, never 1970.
- **Runs:** a Claude Code or Codex run that starts while its harness installs waits for the install; the very first
  Claude Code run on a new server no longer fails (#2196).
- **Runs:** a tool call refused before it ran (a tool set to deny, or a call a person denied) reads "Refused: …" on the
  Timeline, never as a call that ran and failed.
- **Security:** `render.yaml` no longer trusts every private address as a proxy, so a peer on Render's private network
  can't name its own address in `X-Forwarded-For` to get past the sign-in limit's per-address count. The owner's first
  sign-in through an untrusted proxy logs that proxy's address, the one to set `AGENTRUN_TRUSTED_PROXIES` to.
- **Security:** the console's build fails when its browser bundle would ship a credential (a private key, a provider
  key, a JWT or a URL with a password) or a test fixture.
- **Computers:** the conformance sweeps delete only the computers their own run made, never another user's on the
  same account.
- **Server:** the old run engine (the per-run process and the file-era run kernel) is gone from the package. Every run
  already went through the runner and the one store; nothing you see changes.
- **Console:** the console offers Raise the cap only where the cap holds the run, and a template's refused choice reads
  by its label and clears once you choose (#2229).
- **Schedules:** a one-time schedule set to a time already passed is refused in words, on its time field: "Pick a time
  in the future" (#2248).
- **Workflows:** a workflow whose model node names `browser` is refused when it is saved, instead of failing at its run.
- **Security:** a learned workflow's call nodes never run a tool on a default of allow: its run must give the tool
  policy they are held to.
- **Security:** a held secret is cut wherever a path tool's error names it, with its "." segments dropped or
  percent-encoded as a URL writes it.
- **Security:** a run's live view (its running tools, their streamed output and the answer still being written) is cut
  with the run's redactor before it is stored, so a key a tool echoed no longer sits there uncut (#2151).
- **Security:** a workflow's call and model nodes fail closed when the server's tool settings can't be read, as an
  agent's calls do, instead of running on the revision's own allow over a deny the server holds.
- **Console:** a fresh server whose address answers a proxy's 502 page for its first minute (Render) no longer opens on
  a sign-in it can't take; the page says the server is starting and asks again on its own.
- **Console:** the window no longer scrolls away from its sidebar.
- **Templates:** `kyb`'s risk appetite and `inbound-lead`'s destination take their documented defaults when left out,
  and the owner's first Apply answer no longer says a webhook's signing secret is not shown while showing it.
- **Install:** the server image has `agentrun-serve` on its PATH, so the sign-in page's "Forgot it?" command works in
  the image's shell, Render's Shell included.
- **Computers:** an aborted Docker create no longer leaves a container behind.
- **Client:** a `runs.wait` whose deadline passes ends in `AgentRunTimeout`, never a refusal or "unreachable".

## Upgrading

- **The seal key moved.** beta.33 keeps its key in the data directory and no longer reads or makes one under the config
  home. If your beta.32 server made its own key (no `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`), copy that key's value into
  `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` for the first start of beta.33, the same in every process; the store then refuses any other key.
  A Render or compose deploy that already sets `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` needs nothing.
- Nothing else changes for an upgrade from beta.32: same data directory, no migration.

## Known limits

- Claude Code, Codex and workflow runs show $0 cost (in the run view, the runs list, the usage ledger and the workflow
  graph) even though their spend cap is enforced (#2205).
- `deploy/compose.yaml` (a server and runners) has no Docker socket, so its agents get file tools and `web_fetch` but no
  shell; for a Docker sandbox, use the root `compose.yaml`, run the server on the host, or use a Daytona or E2B
  computer with an Archil disk.
- The other limits listed for beta.32 still hold (desktop and phone take-over on the runner, Ctrl-C draining, reopening
  a completed run, a local Chrome).

# AgentRun 0.1.0-beta.32

AgentRun is an open-source platform that supercharges your agents. It adds self-improvement, durable execution and a
control plane on top of your favorite agent harness. Your agents become smarter, more fault tolerant and use fewer
tokens with every run. This is its first v0 beta on the new core: one store holds every agent, run, trigger, setting and
sealed key; runners claim runs from it and run them; each run's files live in a workspace; and an agent's computer is
chosen by kind (none, sandbox, desktop, phone or browser). Changes since beta.31.

**Before you upgrade:** this release refuses a data directory that beta.31 or any earlier build wrote, and nothing
converts it. Keep the earlier version on that directory, or start this one on a new, empty directory and add your
agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins again. The rest is under "Upgrading".

## What you can do now

### Runs and runners

- Run every run through a runner, on one store. The default start is a server with one runner beside it, so a
  one-machine install starts with one command, as before.
- Scale out with more runners: start the server with `--no-runner`, then start each runner from the same image with
  `runner --data /data --name <name>`. Give every process the same `/data` and the same `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`.
- Run the server and its runners on one Postgres database: set `AGENTRUN_STORE_URL` on every process, and the server,
  the runner beside it, import and each `--no-runner` runner open the same store. Runners still share `/data`.
- Lose a runner without losing its runs. A runner that stops hands its runs back at once; the runs of one that dies are
  claimed by another runner once their 30 s lease lapses, and each step is done once.
- Start a run of an agent another system owns and sends inline: `POST /v2/runs` takes the agent's definition with the
  run.
- Hand a person the run's own page: every run and agent the API returns carries `console_url`, at the address the
  caller reached the server on (or its public URL). `runs start` and `runs get` print it.
- Resume a Claude Code run whose last call never started (held for approval, or cut before it was written): the call
  now runs once on resume instead of reading "interrupted". A call that had started is never run again.
- See a Codex or Claude Code tool call on the Timeline while it runs. A call cut off by a crash says it was interrupted
  and may or may not have taken effect.
- Give Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode runs their granted `web_fetch`, `web_search` and monid tools on the runner, as pi
  runs have them.
- Give Codex and OpenCode agents their skills as the harness's own, as Claude Code already had: the revision's and the
  ones the agent learned. Reading a learned skill's file runs under the `read` setting, so by default it needs no
  approval.
- Show the model an image from anywhere in its sandbox: `read` opens a png, jpg, gif or webp at any absolute path in the
  run's box, up to 3.75 MiB. Codex models now receive a tool's images as images.
- Keep a sandbox's `bash` bounded: a call with no timeout runs 120 s, and no call runs past 600 s. Longer work goes to
  `bash_background`.
- Run pi agents behind an Anthropic gateway: pi follows `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on Anthropic models, as Claude Code does.
- Run agents on a model gateway (`AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL`) on the runner: a run sends the gateway the same model id the
  server would, priced by the provider its model names.
- Have pi's file and shell tools on the runner size images for the calling model and stream their output.

### Computers and workspaces

- Give an agent a computer by kind with one setting, `computer: {kind, provider?}`: `none`, `sandbox` (Docker, Daytona,
  Modal or E2B), `desktop` (Docker, E2B or Orgo), `phone` (a rented Android from the phone harness service) or `browser`
  (Browserbase or Kernel). The older `place` field still reads and writes as a view of it.
- See what this server offers in Settings → Computers: each kind, its providers, and whether each provider's keys are
  saved (never their values). "Test connection" makes one read at the provider and starts nothing.
- Run on a Daytona or E2B sandbox on a server with the default allowlist: once the provider's key is saved in Settings →
  Computers and workspaces are on Archil (Mode 2), its runs start.
- Let a run's tools follow its computer: a desktop adds `desktop_screen` and `desktop_input`; a phone adds the `phone_*`
  tools; a browser adds the browser tools. Screenshots come back as images, and a desktop or phone run gets a skill for
  its kind.
- Keep run folders on this server (Mode 1) or on your own Archil disk (Mode 2, turned on with the disk's id, region and
  storage URL and the account key). In Mode 1 a sandbox runs on Docker only; Mode 2 refuses Docker's sandbox, and a
  Daytona, Modal or E2B sandbox mounts the run's folder with a disk token held only for that run. A desktop, phone or
  browser runs in either mode.
- Find the run's files at `/workspace` in every computer that mounts them.
- Start the Docker sandbox with nothing to pull: its image is built here from its recipe on first use, and Mission
  Control says while it is still building. `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_IMAGE` names another image instead.
- Start a dev server, a watcher or a long build from a new Docker-sandbox agent's first run: an agent that names no tools
  gets the background tools with its shell.

### Approvals

- Let an agent run unattended: Approvals → "Never ask (run unattended)" (`approvals: "never"`) allows each tool that
  would ask. It never lifts a deny, and an agent or run that never asks reads Unattended.
- Deny a tool for every agent: a deny set on the server now holds over any agent's own setting, a template's grant and
  Never ask. The console says so and won't let you tick the tool.
- Pin an MCP tool's arguments on the server (`pin` in `PUT /v2/settings/tools`, shown under Settings → Tools): a call
  outside the pin is refused before it runs or asks, and an approved call is checked again before it runs.
- On a server with accounts off, where no one can approve, an ask is refused at once in words instead of waiting.
- Read an approval in order on the Timeline: the call, held for your approval; your answer; then what came of it, in
  plain words, with no call ids. A write held for approval no longer shows a "Saved" row before it runs.
- A deny tells the model what really happened: "It was not run: nothing was sent and nothing was charged.", or, for a
  call that had started, that whether it took effect is not known. It also says whether the deny was set on the agent
  or on the server.

### Tools and MCP

- Add a remote MCP server in Settings → MCP servers, with a bearer token, headers, or Sign in with OAuth. The server runs
  the sign-in, keeps the token sealed, and refreshes it at a run's launch when it's near expiry.
- Allow named private-network hosts for an MCP sign-in (Settings → MCP servers → Private network hosts). Loopback,
  link-local and this machine's own addresses stay refused.
- Grant a saved MCP server's tools to Codex agents, as on pi and Claude Code. Codex never holds the server's credential.
- Give an MCP server GitHub App credentials (`auth: {type: "github_app"}`): each run gets a token narrowed to its one
  repository, minted at each launch and minted again 5 minutes before it expires, so a long run never calls with an
  expired token.
- Keep MCP tool prices when you save a server without `prices`; send `"prices": {}` to clear them. A tool no price
  meters reads "not metered".
- Read each tool's short line for people, such as "Read a public web page" or "Ask you a question mid-run".
- Run Parallel decisions with only an OpenRouter key. Web citations count as evidence either way, and a $0 cost report
  counts as unknown, not free.

### Templates

- Apply one of five ready-made agents from the console's Templates page: `code-review`, `kyb`, `market-monitor`,
  `inbound-lead` and `release-notes`. None needs a sandbox; each answers in its own JSON shape and ships eval cases.
- Consent one MCP tool at a time on the Apply screen: nothing is granted until you tick it. A fixed-choice parameter is a
  choice, the title fills in as you type, and a webhook trigger's signing secret is shown once there.
- Let a template that runs on triggers run unattended: code-review, inbound-lead, market-monitor and release-notes apply
  as Never ask by default; kyb asks. The Apply screen lets you choose.
- Review pull requests: `code-review` makes its own GitHub trigger for the repository you applied it to. Its review
  write is pinned on the agent so it can only comment, never approve or request changes.
- Screen a company with `kyb`, with OpenSanctions as an optional source (CC BY-NC 4.0: commercial use needs a paid
  licence). A registry status flag rests only on the record's own status and filing fields.
- Get a weekly digest from `market-monitor` that names every company you watch, says why each page it couldn't read
  failed (blocked, not found, error or skipped), "nothing new this week (checked: …)"
  for a quiet one, and finds a company's real pricing page when `/pricing` is missing.
- Score leads with `inbound-lead`: each webhook lead is its own run, at most 3 at once.
- Draft notes with `release-notes`: when the GitHub App can't write issues, the draft stays in the answer with the
  reason, and the apply warns about it beforehand.
- Measure a template: `agentrun template eval DIR` runs its eval cases as real runs on a throwaway server and grades
  them. `template list`, `apply` and `validate` are in the CLI too.

### Triggers and code review

- Make and manage schedules, signed webhooks and GitHub triggers on the console's Triggers screen, with their firings.
  A schedule reads in words ("At 08:00, only on Monday · UTC"), and a one-time schedule that ran reads Done.
- Connect GitHub from Settings → GitHub: one GitHub App per server, made from the console. GitHub triggers start runs on
  pull requests and on comments, and turn off when you disconnect.
- Point GitHub or any Standard Webhooks sender at a webhook trigger: it checks either signature and fires only on the
  events its `accept` rules take. A duplicate delivery starts nothing, and `max_active_runs` holds extra events due
  instead of skipping them.
- Start a workflow from a trigger, and give a trigger a name unique per agent. A webhook trigger's view carries its
  `hook_url`.
- Archive an agent and its triggers turn off with it; unarchiving turns none back on.
- Trust what a trigger sends: its input enters the run as the trigger's, never as your words, and a webhook's signing
  secret never shows on the Timeline, in a run's title or in its answer.
- See a signing secret once, in the console (your signed-in session, or the launcher's console on loopback when
  accounts are off); the API token gets a note sending you to the console.

### Browser take-over

- Watch a run's browser live from the run page's Screen tab, in a viewer only you can open. A sandbox run's Screen tab
  says it has no screen.
- Take over the agent's browser, drive it, and hand it back; the agent can also ask you to. The viewer says when you
  are only watching, and the Timeline shows when you took it and handed it back.
- Trust downloads and lost requests: a file Chrome is still writing reads as still downloading, never filed empty, and
  a request the browser lost is told to the agent so it can send it again.
- Keep the browser live while the agent asks you something: the run waits with its session, live view and page open,
  so you can watch or take over and your answer resumes it on the same page. The wait is bounded at 15 minutes from the
  question, and your time on the session counts under the run's cap.
- See the agent's ask above the run page and in Mission Control's Needs you ("The agent asks you to: …", "Done when:
  …"), with Done and Cancel. The console reminds you that you never need to type your AgentRun password for it.

### Watching a run

- See what a run on a runner is doing while it does it: the tools running now, with the output they've streamed so far,
  and a partial answer, refreshed about four times a second.

### Learning

- Keep a trigger's text apart from your words: a webhook or GitHub trigger's message is never graded as yours, and a
  rule found only there is treated as planted. A schedule's fixed prompt still counts as yours.
- See which notes a run was given and which it opened; each note counts both.
- Have a standing rule from your own user or team kept, as a note or as a skill that carries it, even when it names the
  team; a rule for every reply is kept as a note rather than a skill.
- Have the grader read every message you sent, whole, including the end of a long one, so a rule you took back is
  not kept as yours.
- A run that held a note for your OK stops saying it waits once you approve or retire it.
- Keep learning on git 2.32 or later (was 2.40).
- Use learned workflows on every harness and on the runner: their model calls go through the run's own model route,
  under the run's one cap.

### Spend

- Cap what a run spends and get about what you paid for: caps price each request at its expected cost, cached input at
  the cached price. A run pauses at the cap; a cache miss can overshoot it by a bounded amount, which the Timeline
  states. `cap_mode: "strict"` keeps worst-case pricing.
- Have a run near its cap told once to finish ("About $X left of this run's budget: finish now with your answer."), on
  every harness. On a small cap it hears the budget instead.
- Read a cap pause in plain words ("Raise the cap to at least $0.11 to continue."), as a pause, not a failure. The
  console shows "Least to continue" and "Suggested" apart. (On pi and CLI runs a raise holds for one request in this
  release; see Known limits.)
- Cap a workflow run: model nodes, `llm` calls, paid tool calls and decisions are each held to the cap, and a step with
  no room waits unsent until you raise it.
- See unknown costs as unknown: a model with no price reads unknown everywhere, never $0, and a capped run on one is
  refused before it starts.
- Run OpenRouter's `particle-ai/particle-1` capped and priced, at Particle's list price.
- Read an ended run's cost as its cost, not "so far". A browser call counts as one paid tool call.

### Console

- Handle secrets as write-only: each key, credential or sign-in is one row saying Set or Missing, where it came from, and
  when it changed. Paste, Replace and Remove appear only in the console (your signed-in session, or the launcher's console on
  loopback when accounts are off).
- Sign out this browser only, or use "Sign out everywhere".
- Set up a server at a public address with the setup code or the server's token; a refused code says what to do.
  Pages carry HSTS over https.
- Open a retired note, skill or workflow read-only on the Learning tab, and Restore it after a confirm.
- Use the agent and run pages on a phone: the header and tabs take far less of the screen.
- Read the console more easily: the focus ring is 2px in the text colour, secondary and error text pass 4.5:1 contrast
  in the light theme, a working run shows in the brand's colour, and reduced motion turns animation off.
- Create an agent as soon as it has a name: the form opens with instructions to edit.
- See which trigger started a run: its run is titled from the trigger, never its input, and its Timeline row names the
  trigger as it is now called (a rename shows at once; a deleted trigger is named by its id).
- A working run's header cost follows the Timeline.

### Install, CLI and deploy

- Run the server and its runners from one container image (Node 24, with the computer daemon for amd64 and arm64).
  `deploy/compose.yaml` runs a server and two runners on one volume (no Docker sandbox there yet; see Known limits).
- Deploy on Render from the blueprint: a 2 GB instance with a 10 GB disk, with `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` generated for you.
- Run Claude Code and Codex agents with a plain `npx @parcha/agentrun`: each installs itself on first use, at a pinned,
  locked version, and runs show "Installing … (first use)…" meanwhile.
- Point a coding agent at the CLI: it ships an Agent Skill (`agentrun skill install`) with recipes to make an agent,
  start a capped run and wait, answer a run, read its cost and raise a cap. `agentrun login` takes the token from stdin.
- Get `agents create`, `runs start` and `triggers create` right the first time: their help ends with a working `--body`,
  and a refused field says what it accepts, with an example.
- Wait for a run with `runs wait RUN_ID` or `runs start ... --wait` (exit 0 done, 1 failed or cancelled, 8 waiting on
  you), and follow it live with `runs timeline RUN_ID --follow`.
- Hear about refused requests and ignored webhook deliveries on the server's stderr, in plain words.
- Call your server from code: `npm install @parcha/agentrun-client` (a typed TypeScript client with no dependencies,
  including `runs.wait` and following a timeline) or `pip install parcha-agentrun` (the Python client, 0.3.0 on its own
  version line; code for the old hosted SDK pins `parcha-agentrun<0.3`).
- Use `@parcha/agentrun-computer`, published with this release: one daemon in every computer, a provider per vendor,
  and a conformance suite.

## Fixed

- **Spend:** a gateway model whose version is written with dots and dashes swapped (`gpt-5-4-mini`) is priced from the
  catalog.
- **Tools and MCP:** a trigger's message can never answer a run's question, approve or decline a held call, or lift a cap
  pause. It is refused and its firing skipped: "The run is waiting on a person."
- **Tools and MCP:** a provider's error that echoes its key no longer hands that key to the harness.
- **Tools and MCP:** the PDF tools' helper programs start with no server secret in their environment.
- **Tools and MCP:** MCP sign-in never sends anything to a private address you haven't allowed, and a refresh outage
  never sends an expired token. An unreachable MCP server reads "could not be reached …; nothing was sent."
- **Tools and MCP:** with the server's tool settings unreadable, Never ask lifts no ask and turns on no harness's own
  search.
- **Tools and MCP:** on Codex, a code-mode model is no longer offered an `apply_patch` that always failed, and a script's
  call held for approval is never reported as done.
- **Spend:** a capped Claude Code run told to wrap up at a turn's start no longer fails that turn, and a run is no longer
  told to finish before it has done any work.
- **Spend:** a Claude Code run that waits for an approval books the request that asked for the call at its price.
- **Spend:** a run whose cap you raise reads `queued` at once; `runs wait` no longer stops on it.
- **Spend:** a stopped run reads its cost as unknown plus the known part from the moment it stops.
- **Learning:** a run on the runner gets its agent's own skills and its learned workflows; before, an agent with skills
  failed there.
- **Learning:** a run's learning never keeps a key or sign-in it was handed.
- **Learning:** an end-of-run answer that gives a skill twice is read once, and an unclosed block drops only that block.
- **Browser:** a cancelled browser call returns at once; a run of several actions stops before one that would land on a
  new page.
- **Browser:** a run kept across a server restart never shows its browser sign-in's pointer, and a sign-in can't be
  forgotten while a run holds it.
- **Console:** links and images from server data open only for http and https URLs.
- **Console:** a code or mono line no longer joins characters (`==` read as one bar).
- **Runs:** a long final answer (about 1 MB) no longer holds the runner for most of a minute and leaves the run never
  ending.
- **Security:** a run with no computer that mounts its folder no longer gets a shell on the server's own machine, where
  a command could read the server's data and keys.
- **Security:** a server listening on a non-loopback address (the image listens on 0.0.0.0) takes the printed setup
  code at first visit; before, anyone who reached the port first could set the password.
- **Learning:** a run on a runner never learns a secret the server keeps: MCP headers and tokens, trigger signing
  secrets, the GitHub App's keys, keys it wasn't handed, or the API token.
- **Templates:** `code-review` and `release-notes` refuse a repository name ending in a dot, and `code-review` reviews
  a pasted diff with no repository without failing its reads, saying the repo's own rules weren't read.
- **Computers:** a cloud phone or hosted browser starts on a server with the default box allowlist (it asks for the
  vendor's own network), and a remote sandbox asks for `none` instead of the allowlist it refused.
- **Tools and MCP:** an MCP server stays signed in: an owner's save or tools refresh keeps a runner's rotated token, and
  a refresh never re-sends a spent refresh token.
- **Security:** the sign-in limit can no longer lock the owner out behind a proxy (Render, or a TLS proxy), and an IPv6
  /64 counts as one address: ten tries in 15 minutes per address.
- **Security:** a saved secret or sign-in pointer is cut from a run's Timeline, answer and learning however it is
  written (case, dashes, separators, or quoted as a file path).
- **Learning:** with no grade model named, a run's learning is graded on its agent's own model again, and a server whose
  only model key is OpenRouter's grades on a named Anthropic or OpenAI grade model through OpenRouter.
- **Learning:** an installed server runs learned workflows (it now carries the package their model nodes need), and a
  learned workflow's call nodes are held to the run's own tool permissions on the runner.
- **Install:** when Docker refuses the server because its user just joined the `docker` group, the message says how to
  fix it without a reboot.
- **Install:** the launcher tightens its own config folder before making the seal key, instead of refusing the key it
  just made.
- **Install:** `npx @parcha/agentrun` with a public URL shows the setup-code line again, never reads a half-written
  server record, and says plainly when the server stopped before printing anything.
- **Install:** started with `AGENTRUN_TOKEN`, the server removes a stale `.token` file that held a token it no longer
  takes.
- **Install:** a request refused for its Host gets a tunnel example on the server's real port, not always 7340.
- **Install:** a server stopping mid-install of Claude Code or Codex stops npm within 5 s instead of waiting on the
  registry.

## Upgrading

- **An earlier data directory is refused.** A directory beta.31 or earlier wrote (runs under `<data>/runs/`, an earlier
  `store.sqlite`, or store version 1) stops the start, in words, and nothing is migrated. Start on a new, empty
  directory or volume and re-create agents, MCP servers, keys and sign-ins there. There is no rollback either: a run
  store written by this release (pi 1.5) can't be opened by an older one.
- **Set `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`.** The server never starts without a seal key. Left unset, it makes one at
  `~/.config/agentrun/seal.key`; in a container, each container makes its own, which no other shares. Make one with
  `openssl rand -base64 32`, keep it, and give the same key to the server and every runner. A check that every process
  holds the same key is a follow-up after launch.
- **Setup on a public listener needs the code.** A first visit to a server listening on anything but loopback must give
  the printed setup code (or the server's token); open setup holds only on loopback.
- **A run with no computer has no shell on the server.** Give the agent a computer (the Docker sandbox, or a remote
  one) if it needs `bash`.
- **Runners share `/data` and the seal key.** Each runner mounts the server's `/data` and runs the same image tag; start
  the server first (a runner exits 3 on a store it doesn't know) and give a runner 35 s to stop.
- **`fetch_page` is gone:** grant `web_fetch` instead. A definition that names `fetch_page` is refused.
- **Secrets are written only from your signed-in session.** Saving a model or tool key, rotating a trigger's secret or
  removing the outbound webhook with the API token is a 403; use the console, or set keys where the server starts (the
  environment wins). The CLI's `tool-keys set`, `save` and `delete` and `mcp-servers oauth-start` are gone. The API token also
  gets a 403 for starting an MCP sign-in, removing or re-saving an MCP server in a way that drops its credential,
  Connect or Disconnect GitHub, and forgetting a saved browser sign-in.
- **Signing secrets moved.** The value shown once is now `signing_secret` (trigger create and rotate, outbound webhook,
  template apply's `webhook_secrets`), and `secret` is its metadata. The API token gets no value.
- **A server deny is absolute.** An agent that set a tool to ask or allow on a server that denies it now has the tool
  refused; lift the server's deny to restore it.
- **Sign in once more.** Sign out now signs out only this browser, and a session from before this release has no id.
- **The run's folder is at `/workspace`** in its box, where it was `/run/agentrun/run/work`.
- **Where an agent with no setting runs:** with no `computer` or `place`, the server decides at each run's start from
  its own Docker: the Docker sandbox where the server has Docker, and no computer otherwise. Save
  `"place": {"mode": "runner"}` to keep one off the box. `capabilities.places.default` is gone; read
  `places.default_place.mode`.
- **Spend caps default to expected-cost pricing**, so a cache miss can overshoot by a bounded amount; set
  `cap_mode: "strict"` for the old behaviour. A capped run on a model with no price is refused before it starts (409 on
  `definition.model`).
- **Gateway rules for pi:** an `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` that is plain http to a non-loopback host, names a user, or has a
  query, fragment or dot segment is refused on pi, as on Codex and OpenCode. With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set, pi needs
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` alone isn't enough.
- **Harness installs:** Codex and Claude Code install on first use from npm into `<data>/harnesses/`, so the first run
  needs your npm registry. The server image no longer carries a Codex CLI.
- **CLI exit codes:** `runs start --wait` now gives up at its bound (pass `--timeout`); a malformed `--follow` stream is
  exit 1, not 3; a bad server record is exit 4, not 2. `skill install --codex` writes `~/.agents/skills/agentrun-cli`;
  remove an older copy under `~/.codex/skills` by hand.
- **API shapes:** a 422 field issue's message may end with ", e.g. <value>" (compare `field` and `reason`); a run's
  learning `used` is now `read`; a trigger has no `overlap` field (a firing while its last run works is skipped, except a webhook with `accept` or a
  GitHub trigger, which starts a run per event up to `max_active_runs`);
  `GET /runs/{run_id}/graph` has no `stale`; decisions is `decisions/3`; a refused MCP meta tool is under
  `error.details.not_grantable`.
- **A workflow that grants an MCP tool is refused at save.** Grant MCP tools to an agentic agent.
- **Library users:** `@parcha/pi-browser` is on Stagehand 4.4 (a local Chrome must be 137 or later). `@parcha/pi-durable-disk`
  no longer places runs on Archil or keeps a lease file (`run` needs `--epoch N`). `@parcha/pi-transport` drops its
  `home` and `place` entries. `@parcha/agentrun-computer` reads no environment: pass every setting as an option. The
  kernel's `SessionWriter.sync()` is required. `@parcha/pi-agent-learn`, `@parcha/pi-git-remote` and `@parcha/pi-vision`
  get no new release.

## Known limits at launch

- Runners on Postgres still mount the server's `/data`, so every runner needs that shared volume.
- A local Chrome is not set up on any server in this release: the browser runs at Browserbase or Kernel.
- A Daytona, E2B or Modal sandbox's programs have no outbound network of their own (loopback only, and the vendor's
  own agent is kept out of their reach). Open networks and allowlists for remote sandboxes come later, through a proxy.
  The Docker sandbox keeps the `AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW` allowlist.
- Running the server in a container (the compose files): Docker sandboxes don't work in this release. The root
  `compose.yaml` still offers one, so a new agent there gets it by default and its run fails when the sandbox is
  created; change its `AGENTRUN_BOXES: docker` line to `none` so agents run with file tools and `web_fetch`, no shell. `deploy/compose.yaml` has
  no Docker socket, so its agents already run that way. For Docker sandboxes, run the server on the host, or use a
  Daytona or E2B computer with workspaces on Archil. Fixed in the first patch release (#2160, #2163).
- A runner with Docker behind a server without Docker doesn't give no-setting agents the Docker sandbox; the server
  decides. Set `computer` on the agent instead.
- On OpenRouter or OpenAI model routes, a pi run's screenshots (browser, desktop, phone) don't reach the model yet;
  use an Anthropic key for computer agents (#2184).
- A running tool's streamed output is kept in the store's live-view row before its secrets are cut (#2151). It's never
  served (the Timeline and the step's saved result are cut), but it sits uncut in the store until the step ends; the
  first patch release cuts it before it's stored.
- Claude Code, Codex and workflow runs show $0 cost (in the run view, the runs list, the usage ledger and the workflow
  graph) even though their spend cap is enforced; the real cost shows after the first patch release (#2205).
- The very first Claude Code run on a new server can fail while Claude Code is still installing; run it again (#2196).
- A cloud iPhone is refused; the phone kind is Android.
- With a run folder on Archil and no computer, a command runs through Archil's serverless exec for at most 295 s, and
  once sent it can't be stopped.
- A workflow's nodes can't use MCP tools.
- One data directory serves one server at a time.
- An E2B computer lives at most an hour (the provider's longest).
- Not in this release, coming in a patch release:
  - watching a desktop or phone run live and taking it over on the runner (#2063): the Screen tab frames the browser
    only;
  - Ctrl-C letting runs finish their turn before the server stops, and a start waiting for a stopping server (#2053);
  - sending a message to a completed agentic run to open it again (#2058): it answers 409;
  - a raised cap that sticks: today a pi or CLI run paused at its cap and raised resumes for one request, then parks
    again at the old cap; raise it again, or start the run with the cap you need (#2133, the first patch release).

AgentRun observation CLI 0.1.10 with the Node launcher @parcha/agentrun-cli 0.1.1.

Connect selected Claude Code and Codex sessions to an AgentRun workspace using device authentication or an explicitly configured enrollment credential. Observation reports activity; it does not execute or control agents. Session selection, metadata consent, and login startup remain explicit choices.

## Installation

Verified platform: Linux x64 with glibc, Node.js 20 or newer. The launcher provisions Python 3.12, verifies release checksums, and installs a persistent runtime outside the npm cache. macOS, Windows, and other architectures are not supported by this launcher release.

The npm launcher is published as `@parcha/agentrun-cli@0.1.1`:

```sh
npx --yes @parcha/agentrun-cli@0.1.1 --help
```

The GitHub-hosted package also works directly:

```sh
npx --yes --package https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/releases/download/cli-v0.1.10/parcha-agentrun-cli-0.1.1.tgz agentrun --help
```

For enrollment, use `connect --device-auth --origin <your-api-origin> --workspace-id <your-workspace-id>`. Keep any selected `--state-dir` on subsequent commands. Device approval uses a browser on any device and requires no local callback server.

## Release integrity and source

`release.json` names each runtime artifact and its SHA-256. The launcher accepts only this repository's pinned CLI release URLs and one HTTPS redirect to GitHub's exact release-assets.githubusercontent.com host. Explicit preview download sources retain their no-redirect policy.

The `agentrun-cli-source-0.1.10.tar.gz` asset contains the exact build inputs for these artifacts. Extract it and run `python3.12 scripts/agentrun/build_cli_release.py --output /tmp/agentrun-release-rebuild` with Node/npm available. All release files were rebuilt byte-for-byte from this source snapshot. The repository tag identifies the release location; use the attached source snapshot to reproduce the CLI assets.

## Validation

45 launcher process/HTTP/HTTPS tests passed. Fresh Node-only Linux containers completed installation, discovery, explicit synthetic enrollment, HTTP telemetry delivery, daemon start, npm-cache deletion, stop, and disconnect through a local release server, the preview HTTPS source, and the public GitHub release. The public npm-to-GitHub install path passed the same full lifecycle, and the short `npx --yes @parcha/agentrun-cli --help` command passed in a separate fresh container. This release does not change the main AgentRun platform release.
The viewer gallery's recordings (one tar, checked by apps/viewer/recordings.lock.json): market-street, fair-robot and document-check.

## Session Continuation Fixes (v0.5.46–v0.5.51)

- Fix SSH session continuation: race-proof resume probe, stale buffer finalization, and thin-transcript amnesia (v0.5.46)
- Replace baseline split with native-delta conversation sync on resume (v0.5.47)
- Prevent transcript hydration from dropping visible assistant messages (v0.5.48)
- Per-session turn mutex and drain-ordering fix to prevent rival remote process spawns (v0.5.49)
- Make turn lock reentrant for recursive retries and unify recovered-job filter (v0.5.50)
- Deliver full Build transcript as in-message conversation_sync on fresh starts (v0.5.51)

### Highlights

**Turn Mutex**: All remote Claude spawns per session are now serialized behind an async lock, eliminating the dual-process race where queue-drain resume and reattach-resume could spawn rival remote processes 400ms apart.

**Fresh-Start Context Recovery**: When a doomed resume drops the SDK session and starts fresh, the full Build transcript is now delivered as a `<conversation_sync>` block *inside* the user message — models treat it as their own conversation memory instead of dismissable system-prompt metadata.

**Native-Delta Sync**: On resume, Build fetches the native SDK transcript, computes the true missing message set via content-normalized comparison, and injects only the delta — eliminating "I don't have context from earlier" after session hiccups.

## Fix: CPU death from git polling storm

- **Guard git IPC handlers** against missing directories — return safe defaults instead of throwing 471 exceptions per cycle for sessions whose working directory doesn't exist locally
- **Skip git polling for SSH sessions** in ChatContainer — branch info is already refreshed by SessionCard; redundant polling triggered expensive remote SSH exec calls saturating the main process

Root cause: With 523 sessions (158 SSH), the app was throwing hundreds of exceptions per polling cycle and running dozens of concurrent SSH `echo ok` health checks, generating enough DNS lookups to crash Electron's c-ares resolver (EXC_BREAKPOINT in `ares_dns_rr_get_ttl`).

## Highlights

**`file_manager:download` / `file_manager:upload`** — built-in virtual tools for generic binary IO through the proxy. Agents in hardened sandboxes (egress locked to the proxy host) can now fetch arbitrary URLs into sandbox files and ship local files to operator-allowlisted destinations.

```bash
ati run file_manager:download --url https://v3b.fal.media/.../clip.mp4 --out /tmp/clip.mp4
ati run file_manager:upload --path /tmp/shot.png --destination fal
# → https://v3b.fal.media/files/.../shot.png
```

**CLI handler binary output capture** — new manifest fields let any CLI provider that writes binary output (screenshots, PDFs, downloads) round-trip the bytes back to the sandbox instead of stranding them on the proxy filesystem:

```toml
# manifests/bb.toml
cli_output_args = ["--output", "-o"]

[provider.cli_output_positional]
"browse screenshot" = 0
```

```bash
ati run bb browse screenshot /tmp/shot.png   # PNG lands inside the sandbox
```

## Security model

- **Upload destinations allowlist** — uploads go only to destinations declared under `[provider.upload_destinations.<name>]` in `manifests/file_manager.toml`. Unknown destinations return 403. No env-var escape hatch. Two sink types shipped: `gcs` and `fal_storage` (fal.ai's signed-token CDN upload flow).
- **`ATI_DOWNLOAD_ALLOWLIST`** — opt-in host allowlist for `file_manager:download`, comma-separated with `*.example.com` wildcard support. Suffix-collision tricks (`evilfal.media` vs `*.fal.media`) are correctly rejected.
- **Always-on SSRF guard** on server-supplied URLs (e.g. fal's `base_url` from the token mint) — refuses non-HTTPS, private addresses, metadata endpoints, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms like `::ffff:169.254.169.254`.
- **Body-size ceiling** raised in the proxy's `/call` handler + axum `DefaultBodyLimit` layer — uploads up to `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (1 GB) now actually work through proxy mode.
- **Per-file cap** `ATI_CLI_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` (default 500 MB) on captured CLI outputs.

## Performance

- GCS upload retry wraps the payload in `bytes::Bytes` — O(1) clone per attempt instead of a 1 GB memcpy.
- CLI upload shim frees raw bytes after base64 encoding — halves peak sandbox-side RAM.
- `materialize_outputs` / `collect_capture_results` / `run_download` switched to `tokio::fs` — no more tokio worker stalls on 500 MB reads/writes.
- `fetch_bytes` preallocates Vec capacity from Content-Length — eliminates log-N regrow memcpy on large downloads.

## What's new in v0.7.1

### CLI aliases
`ati tools` and `ati skills` now work as aliases for `ati tool` and `ati skill`. Agents typing the plural form no longer get "unrecognized subcommand".

### assist/help no longer requires a scope
`ati assist` and proxy `/help` work for all authenticated callers — no `help` scope needed in the JWT. Assist is a discovery tool; gating it behind a scope nobody added was broken by design.

### All tools now participate in JWT scope filtering (breaking)
Hand-written HTTP tools and CLI auto-tools previously had `scope: None`, bypassing JWT scope filtering entirely. Now all non-internal tools get `scope: "tool:{name}"` auto-assigned during manifest load, consistent with OpenAPI and MCP tools. Agents only see tools their JWT grants.

**Migration**: existing provisioners that include tool names in JWTs are unaffected — the scope strings match. Tools that were only visible because they had no scope (e.g., `google_workspace`, `google_ads`) now require their scope in the JWT.

## Upgrading
`0.7.0` → `0.7.1`. No new env vars. The auto-scope change is the only behavioral difference.

## What's new in v0.7.0

### Proxy skill registry transport
Sandboxes without GCS egress can now fetch skills through the ATI proxy. Set `ATI_SKILL_REGISTRY=proxy` and skill reads route through `ATI_PROXY_URL` — zero GCS credentials needed in the sandbox.

```bash
# Proxy holds GCS creds; sandbox just needs the JWT
ATI_SKILL_REGISTRY=proxy ATI_PROXY_URL=http://proxy:8090 ati skill fetch catalog
```

All `/skillati/*` endpoints are now scope-enforced — callers only see skills their JWT allows.

### Remote skill fetch (`ati skill fetch` / `ati skillati`)
Lazy reads from GCS skill registry. New subcommands: `catalog`, `read`, `resources`, `cat`, `refs`, `ref`, `build-index`.

### JWT scope enforcement hardened
- Scopes enforced on all paths: `ati run`, proxy `/call`, `/mcp`, `/tools`, `/skills`, `/help`, `/skillati/*`
- Legacy underscore scopes (`tool:github_search_repos`) normalized to colon form for backward compat
- Scope-filtered discovery: endpoints only return what the caller's JWT allows

### SSRF protection
`ATI_SSRF_PROTECTION=1` blocks requests to private/loopback/link-local IPv4 and IPv6 ranges via DNS resolution.

### Python client
`ati-client` bumped to 0.7.0 — install with `pip install ati-client==0.7.0`.

## Upgrading
No breaking changes. New env vars: `ATI_SKILL_REGISTRY=proxy` (opt-in). Existing `gcs://` registries and all other configs unchanged.

## GREP Research Skills v0.2.0

Deep research superpowers for your AI agent. Connects Claude Code, Cowork, and OpenClaw to GREP — the #1 deep research engine.

### What's new

- **Auth-aware API routing** — API-key sessions use the full `/api/v2` surface; email-OTP (JWT) sessions automatically route to `/api/v1`. Fixes the 401 "Invalid OAuth access token" that broke `/research` for OTP-authenticated users.
- **16 skills** (up from 8): domain experts, HTML app / slidedeck / spreadsheet builders, multi-step research workflows, file-attachment research, job continuation, and Grep MCP server setup.
- **Expanded Cowork bundle** — single `/research` router skill with 16 intent routes and bundled scripts.
- **Report extraction fixes** — handles both v2 (`report.markdown`) and v1 (`status_messages`) response shapes.
- **Anti-narration guidance** — agents stay silent during long research polls instead of burning context on status commentary.
- Correct API key prefix in docs (`parcha-*`)

### Install

**npm (Claude Code & Cowork desktop):**
```bash
npx grep-research-skills
```

**Cowork (org plugin):**
1. Download `grep-research-skills-v0.2.0.zip` below
2. In Cowork, go to **Settings → Plugins → Add Plugin**
3. Upload the zip — all team members get access

**Claude Code plugin marketplace:**
```
/install-plugin parcha-ai/grep-research-skills
```

**Git clone:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/parcha-ai/grep-research-skills.git ~/.grep-research-skills && ~/.grep-research-skills/setup
```

Fix: the HTTP read timeout now outlasts the in-box command timeout, so a long `exec` (e.g. apt/pip install on a slower network) no longer trips `httpx.ReadTimeout`. Supersedes 0.1.1.

- `stop(delete=True)` (Harbor's default) now permanently removes a box instead of only archiving it, so finished trials don't accumulate as snapshots; `delete=False` archives a resumable snapshot. Both stop compute billing (validated live).
- New [`examples/dockerfile_to_box.py`](https://github.com/ariana-dot-dev/harbor-box/blob/main/examples/dockerfile_to_box.py): run a `FROM`/`RUN`/`COPY`/`WORKDIR` Dockerfile on Box by reproducing it at runtime.
- Live tests for the migration path and the delete/archive billing behavior.

First release of **harbor-box** — a [Harbor](https://pypi.org/project/harbor/) environment adapter backed by the [Ascii Box](https://box.ascii.dev) public API.

- `BoxEnvironment`: Harbor `BaseEnvironment` over the Box API (lifecycle, exec, env, file/dir upload+download, mount-dir prep).
- No-env boxes by default for trial isolation; `no_env=False` to use your account environment.
- Unsupported features (network policies, image builds, GPU/TPU, Windows) are validated and rejected.
- Unit + live-Box test suite validating every documented feature.

`pip install harbor-box`

Docs: explain how the box environment is prepared (files from your Harbor environment directory are uploaded in, env passed via config — no Docker image build), slim the isolation section, and drop defensive wording. No code changes from 0.1.1.

## What's new

- **No-env isolation by default.** `BoxEnvironment` now creates Box *no-env* boxes by default (`no_env=True`): trials get none of your account's secrets, credentials, or cloned private repos and can't act on your account or other boxes — the right default for evals and for boxes handed to third parties. Pass `no_env=False` to opt into your account environment (configured in the Box dashboard). `task_env_config.env` is forwarded as per-box env at creation.
- **End-user docs polish.** README/eval wording cleaned up; eval-only setup moved out of the main README.

Verified: adapter self-test and both Claude-agent evals pass on no-env boxes.

First public release.

- `BoxEnvironment`: a Harbor `BaseEnvironment` backed by the Ascii Box public API (lifecycle, exec, env vars, file/dir upload+download, mount-dir prep) + a small async Box client.
- End-to-end eval suite running a from-scratch Claude Agent SDK coding agent inside a Box; authenticates with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a Claude subscription token (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`).
- Verified: adapter e2e self-test passes against the real Box API.

Install: `pip install -r requirements.txt` — needs `BOX_API_KEY` (https://ascii.dev).

Siglake 0.4.1 is a focused maintenance release with JSON attribute lookup optimizations, clearer WAL fallback diagnostics, and dependency security updates.

- JSON attribute queries reduce repeated scans of nested objects while preserving literal dotted-key precedence, mixed row layouts, duplicate keys, NULLs, and numeric precision. Improvements depend on the workload; this release makes no universal latency claim.
- Committed-only query fallbacks now expose their stage and reason through a bounded-label counter and tracing event. This adds diagnostics to existing behavior; it does not change WAL freshness guarantees.
- Parquet and Thrift dependencies include the allocation advisory fix. SQLite 3.54.1 addresses RUSTSEC-2026-0459 through a narrowly patched SQLx 0.8.6 dependency, retaining the existing driver API.

Upgrade the engine and operator together to `0.4.1`; both Helm charts carry the same version. There are no intentional API, configuration, or storage-format migrations in this patch. Existing documented limitations still apply, and optional promotion and index features retain their previous defaults.

[Changelog](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.4.1/CHANGELOG.md) · [Limitations](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.4.1/docs/LIMITATIONS.md)

The earlier failed 72-hour attempt remains failed; this patch does not claim a new 72-hour soak, a final-image upgrade/rollback experiment, multi-replica failover or tenant-isolation qualification. The historical hybrid-WAL omitted-WARN incident remains unresolved. Optional promotion and index features remain off by default.

Siglake 0.4.0 ships query correctness fixes, bounded query work, improved OTLP log fidelity, and SQL response accounting. Automatic promotion and segmented-index reads/writes remain off by default.

## Changes

- Preserve projected column names in empty responses, exact dotted-key lookup semantics, and residual handling for fresh WAL-backed rows.
- Bound clipped LIMIT scans and use exact Parquet metadata or ordinary-plan fallback for eligible numeric Top-K and count queries.
- Preserve additional OpenTelemetry context and typed values without changing existing flat attribute lookups.
- Expose execution-phase accounting and cache/handler timing, and include query-audit tables in bounded maintenance.

See the [tag-pinned changelog](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md#040) for the full change list and measurement limits.

The final engine rebuild had different filesystem layers, so it received the separate released-image smoke above; this is not a final-image upgrade/rollback replay.

## Scope and limitations

Chart packaging/rendered resource contracts and opt-in defaults were checked. This release does not claim live Kubernetes/operator installation or CRD rollback qualification, tenant-isolation or multi-replica failover qualification, retention/deletion or cancellation-soak qualification, or a new 72-hour soak. The earlier 72-hour attempt remains failed. Optional auto-promotion and segmented-index field qualification remain incomplete and their defaults stay off. The historical hybrid-WAL omitted-WARN incident remains unresolved; no hybrid-freshness or every-internal-plan claim is made.
