Siglake 0.3.0 adds a read-only MCP adapter for agent workflows, accelerates supported grouped `AVG` queries, and reduces memory pressure during compaction and index rebuilds. It also includes fixes to promoted attributes, distributed query accounting, and WAL query consistency.

- **Connect Claude and Codex.** The [MCP adapter](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.3.0/integrations/mcp/README.md) supports table discovery, schemas, bounded SQL queries, and query cost estimates.
- **Use less memory during storage maintenance.** More compaction and index-rebuild work runs through bounded batches and disk spools. WAL admission and allocator handoffs reduce overlapping memory use, and cancellation retains memory accounting until work finishes.
- **Speed up supported numeric aggregates.** Grouped `AVG` can use Parquet footer summaries. Queries fall back to an exact scan when summaries are missing or incompatible.
- **Improve correctness and operational visibility.** Fixes preserve JSON and dotted-key behavior for promoted attributes, report measured distributed scan statistics, serialize concurrent PostgreSQL catalog initialization, and keep WAL queries consistent across normal file lifecycle moves.

**Known limitations:** auto-promotion remains disabled by default. The latest opt-in comparison failed its freshness target; eventual row coverage passed, but a required completion log was missing. Remaining optional qualification is deferred to 0.4.0. Segmented-index reads and writes also remain disabled by default, and their full cost qualification is unfinished. Keyword and recent-event query latency improvements remain planned for 0.4.0. This release does not claim those performance or cost targets are met.

See the [full changelog](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md), [documented limitations and measurements](https://github.com/siglake/siglake/blob/v0.3.0/docs/LIMITATIONS.md), and [benchmarks](https://benchmarks.siglake.dev/) for details and comparison methodology.

## Bug fix

Fixed a startup crash when running `openhack` from a directory containing a `.env` file with keys the scanner doesn't define.

Because openhack scans arbitrary target repositories, a target's `.env` could carry unrelated keys (e.g. `gemini_sandbox_proxy_command`). pydantic-settings defaults to `extra="forbid"` and validates **every** key found in a CWD `.env` file, so any unknown key aborted the CLI before it started with:

```
pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Settings
gemini_sandbox_proxy_command
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden]
```

The value was never executed — it only tripped settings validation. Setting `extra="ignore"` makes openhack skip unrelated keys in a CWD `.env` (or environment), matching how unknown environment variables were already handled.

**Upgrade:** `pip install --upgrade openhack`

**Full diff:** https://github.com/openhackai/OpenHack/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2

## What's Changed

### License
- **Switched from AGPL-3.0 to MIT** — LICENSE file, package metadata, and README all updated.

### Custom endpoint support
- **Custom setup redesigned** — now asks for what an OpenAI-compatible endpoint actually needs: Base URL → API Key → Model string (free text). No more forced model menu.
- **New `prompt_caching` setting** (default on) — disable with `/config prompt_caching false` or `PROMPT_CACHING=0` for endpoints that reject `prompt_cache_key` (e.g. Groq).
- **Auto-recovery** — if the endpoint rejects `prompt_cache_key`, the client retries without it and stops sending it for the rest of the session. Scans self-heal instead of failing.

### Setup wizard fixes
- Cancelling setup or login (Ctrl+C / `q`) now exits cleanly instead of dropping into an unconfigured TUI.
- All text prompts now support full line editing — Option+Left/Right word jump and Option+Delete work on macOS.
- Fixed `asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop` crash in the custom setup flow.

### Other
- `/config` accepts `prompt_caching` and `openhack_base_url`, and applies changes immediately.
- README: new badges and updated docs.

## What's new

- **Session resume**: New `superserve resume` command to resume previous sessions with full context
- **`@app.session` SDK**: Session decorator for building multi-turn agents with persistent state
- **Zero-config deploy**: Automatically detect dependencies and runtime from your project files
- **SDK idle timeout**: Default idle timeout set to 29 minutes

## Fixes

- CLI field corrections
- Framework doc examples fixed (EOFError handling for clean session exit)
- Playground dev mode and UX improvements
- npm package name updated

### Patch Changes

- c523ef2: Comments work end to end (#464). Comments escape backslashes, so ClickHouse stores the exact text (a trailing `\` no longer breaks the statement), and an empty comment is the same as none. A table comment change plans `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COMMENT`; a view, materialized view or dictionary comment change is the same `MODIFY COMMENT` instead of a drop and recreate (or `CREATE OR REPLACE DICTIONARY`). A column comment change alone is `COMMENT COLUMN`, and a removed column comment runs `MODIFY COLUMN ... REMOVE COMMENT`, so it no longer stays on the server. `drift` reports a changed table, view, materialized view or dictionary comment as `comment_mismatch`, with both values. `pull` writes the comments of tables, views and materialized views, reads every comment from `system.tables.comment` (decoded by ClickHouse), finds the `AS` and `TO` of a view outside its `COMMENT`, and skips a materialized view with an inner table, and that table, with a warning. The same comments reach `drift` and `pull` when they run through the ObsessionDB console API.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`, `@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`, `@chkit/plugin-pull`, `chkit`, `@chkit/clickhouse`</sub>
- fffb87b: `importModuleFile` moved to the `@chkit/core/loader` subpath, so importing `@chkit/core` no longer pulls in the Node-only jiti loader.

  - Breaking: import `importModuleFile` from `@chkit/core/loader` instead of `@chkit/core`.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- 96fade0: Add `query`, `createQuery`, `p` and `t` to `@chkit/core`: typed ClickHouse queries written as tagged templates, composed as subqueries and called with their params, with `t` types shared by table columns and params. `zod@^4.3` is now a peer dependency of `@chkit/core`.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- c9f5483: Bundlers can now drop the parts of `@chkit/core` an app doesn't import, such as the migration planner.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- 81dffea: `pull` then `generate` plans nothing, and `drift` reports nothing, on a database chkit migrated (#466).

  - `pull` keeps every setting the server stores, including `index_granularity`, with a comment on the ones that cannot be altered on an existing table, and leaves out chkit's migration journal (`_chkit_migrations` or `CHKIT_JOURNAL_TABLE`) and the hidden `auto_minmax_index_*` skip indexes ClickHouse creates for the `add_minmax_index_for_*` settings.
  - A MergeTree table without `index_granularity` is treated as having the server's default, the value ClickHouse stores, so new `CREATE TABLE` statements write `SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192`. Existing projects plan nothing for it. A server with another `<merge_tree><index_granularity>` sets it in the new `clickhouse.indexGranularity` config value (default 8192). `drift`, `check`, `migrate` and `pull` stop when the server's default differs from it, with a message that names the value to set.
  - Setting values compare by value (`4096` and `"4096"`, `2.0` and `2.`, `true` and `1`), exactly, so a change between two large integers is not lost. A literal column default compares by value with the expression pull reads back (`7` and `{ expression: '7' }`, `"it's"` and `'it\'s'`, `1e21` and `1e+21`, newlines and tabs as ClickHouse escapes them), in `generate` and in `drift`. A string escape chkit does not know for certain (`\N`, `\u0041`) compares as text.
  - A column type compares in the spacing ClickHouse stores (`Decimal(10,2)` and `Decimal(10, 2)`) in `generate` and `drift`; text in quotes compares as written. Skip indexes, projections, constraints and columns compare whatever order their keys are written in.
  - A change to a setting ClickHouse cannot alter on an existing table (`index_granularity`, `index_granularity_bytes`, the `add_minmax_index_for_*` settings and others) plans `DROP TABLE` and `CREATE TABLE`, like an `ORDER BY` change, instead of an `ALTER` the server rejects. `--cutover` supports such a change: its swap guards now also tell the old table from the new one by these settings, and its first statement checks that the table stores the read-only settings the migration expects before anything is created or copied.
  - On an ObsessionDB host, the ObsessionDB plugin treats a table without `storage_policy` as `storage_policy: "'s3'"`, the policy ObsessionDB writes into every `Shared` table, in the schema and the snapshot, and `generate` rejects a schema that changes it. A new `onSnapshotLoaded` plugin hook applies a plugin's schema rewrite to the previous snapshot, so a snapshot written before the rewrite plans no change, and dropping `--force-shared-engines` no longer plans a `RESET SETTING storage_policy`.
  - A dictionary `lifetime` compares in the form ClickHouse stores (`300` and `MIN 0 MAX 300`), and dictionaries compare whatever order their keys are written in.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`, `@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`, `@chkit/plugin-pull`, `chkit`, `@chkit/clickhouse`</sub>
- 30a421f: Query rows now return 64-bit and wider integers that a JS number would round as strings of their exact digits, with no ClickHouse setting needed.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- bcc27f7: Add a `logComment: false` option to `createQuery` and to query calls so `readonly = 1` users can run named queries; without it they now get an error that names the fix.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- 8c01425: `chkit ingest doctor` and `chkit ingest repair` stream the journal table instead of loading it whole, so their memory grows with the selected stream's history rather than with the whole journal.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 10c2676: With `clickhouse.cluster` set, `chkit ingest run` creates its journal as one `ReplicatedMergeTree` on every replica and refuses to run on a journal that is not.

  - Breaking: on a cluster, a local journal an earlier version created now fails `ingest run`; copy its rows into a replicated journal and set `journalTable` to it.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- bdf8a2d: A rate-limit hint too far in the future for a `Date` no longer fails the stream with "Invalid time value"; ingestion waits it out like any other long hint.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- c467d57: Ingestion no longer silently drops row fields the destination has no column for: they land in a `_chkit_rest` JSON column when the table declares one, and the run logs their names.

  - Breaking: without `_chkit_rest`, a yielded field with no column fails the stream; map it to a column or declare `_chkit_rest`.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 262fbb1: Async `migrate` statements no longer fail on a fresh ClickHouse server that has not created `system.query_log` yet.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- dc813e4: `chkit generate` and `chkit check` warn when a plain string default is written as a quoted SQL literal, such as `default: "'standard'"`, which stores the quotes in the value.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>

### Patch Changes

- e8f8e06: `clickhouse.secure` now follows the `clickhouse.url` scheme and defaults to `true` for `https://` (#298).

  Breaking: a `secure` that contradicts the URL scheme is now a config error instead of being ignored.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- aba9e86: Support Distributed, Memory, Null, Log, Buffer and Merge tables in schemas, pull and drift without `orderBy` or other key clauses; setting a key on them fails validation with `engine_unsupported_clause`. The ObsessionDB plugin rejects Distributed tables when targeting ObsessionDB.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- cad89db: Typed `GCD` codec chains such as `[{ kind: 'GCD' }, { kind: 'LZ4' }]` now validate (#408). A chain of only `Delta` and `GCD` steps, which ClickHouse rejects, now fails validation with `codec_chain_must_end_with_general`.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- ae1caf7: The typed `T64` codec can now precede a general codec, as in `CODEC(T64, LZ4)`, without `codec.raw`; `T64` after a general codec fails validation (#434).
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- 0062ee8: Support `vector_similarity` skip indexes and table `constraints` (`CHECK`/`ASSUME`) in schemas, migrations, pull and drift. Pull keeps an index it cannot express as a `type: 'raw'` index instead of rewriting it, and dropping a column together with an index or constraint that reads it no longer fails.
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- b769649: `view({ comment })` and `materializedView({ comment })` now set the comment in ClickHouse instead of dropping it (#406).
  <sub>`@chkit/core`</sub>
- 640ca7a: `chkit check` judges a backfill plan sent with ObsessionDB `submit` by its job instead of reporting it as pending until the plan file is deleted; an unfinished, failed or unverifiable job fails the check (#304). CI that runs `chkit check` needs an ObsessionDB session until every submitted job is confirmed completed.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- 9a52cde: `chkit plugin backfill status --job-id` and `cancel --job-id` now work, because `chkit plugin <name> <command>` accepts flags that other plugins add (#303). The ObsessionDB job commands print the job in text mode, where they printed nothing, and return the standard `--json` envelope instead of the raw console API object.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- c0b5a23: `chkit plugin backfill list` lists an ObsessionDB service's backfill jobs, using the selected service when `--service-slug` is omitted (#311).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- 3be3fd8: `chkit plugin backfill submit --plan-id <id>` re-submits a saved plan whose ObsessionDB job failed or was cancelled, skipping chunks that already finished, and `chkit check` follows the new job (#313).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- 15c0e67: With `--json`, ObsessionDB `backfill status --service-slug` and `backfill list` report `service_not_found` or `service_not_in_active_organization` instead of a generic `error` code.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- dc55385: ObsessionDB `chkit plugin backfill submit` now applies the `backfill({...})` options such as `stateDir` and `maxChunkBytes`, so `chkit check` finds its submissions in a custom `stateDir` (#309).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- c230ec3: `JobsClient` types `lastError` and `metadata` on every returned job, including from `list` (#327).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- 55c1fe9: A service outside the chkit session's active organization now fails with `service_not_in_active_organization` or `service_not_found`, naming the organizations and pointing to `chkit obsessiondb service select`, instead of a bare `Not Found` (#305).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-obsessiondb`</sub>
- d48915f: Invalid checkpoint strategy ids or versions and invalid planned timestamp bounds now fail when a stream runs, and `Date` objects from another realm are no longer accepted.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 684428d: Invalid ingestion definitions and host limits, such as a missing `read` or a non-integer or out-of-range budget, are reported as configuration errors instead of failing the first run or ending it before the first fetch.

  Breaking: declared tags may no longer start with `stream:` or `pipeline:`.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 0771d42: A reader's retained `context.fetch` and `context.attempt` now reject once the reader ends, a custom iterator whose `return()` throws no longer replaces the stream's outcome, and a large `Retry-After` no longer causes repeated one-millisecond waits and warnings.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 6f8a34c: Streams that yield chunks above roughly 125,000 rows no longer crash Node with "Maximum call stack size exceeded".
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 9e55a96: Ingestion loading keeps rows and values intact in more cases:

  - Invalid `maxRowsPerInsert` values are rejected instead of hanging or silently dropping rows, and replaying a batch with a different insert size can no longer skip unsaved rows.
  - DateTime and DateTime64 columns accept ISO timestamps and `Date` objects, and JSONEachRow keeps non-finite floats and `Map`s; a non-finite number aimed at a non-float column now fails or lands as text instead of becoming zero or null.
  - Missing declared ingestion metadata and unflattened Nested inputs are rejected.
  - In native JSON columns, space-separated timestamp strings that used to be inferred as DateTime now stay String, so a path can hold both types across older and newer rows.
  - Upgrade: batch hashes and deduplication tokens changed, so an interrupted run replayed across the upgrade can insert duplicates once; do not recover one run with both old and new loaders.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 4c0b805: Ingestion retries only transient failures, at the request:

  - Network errors, timeouts and HTTP 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried; any other failure fails the stream at once, and the next run resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting the stream within the run.
  - Readers get `context.fetch`, which shares the pipeline's request queue (a `Retry-After` pauses every request of the pipeline), retries transient failures, aborts after 30 seconds and throws `HttpError` for unsuccessful responses.
  - `HttpError.withStatus(response, status, { retryAfterMs })` marks a failure the classification cannot see, such as a rate limit reported as 403.
  - An invalid ingestion definition no longer breaks `generate` or `migrate`; it is reported when an ingest command selects the pipeline and by `chkit check` as `ingest_invalid_pipeline`.
  - `@chkit/plugin-ingest/testing` adds `createSourceContext` and `createReadContext` for testing a client or reader directly.
  - Breaking: `classifyError` is removed; map rate limits with `HttpError.withStatus`.
  - Breaking: `FetchContext` is now `SourceContext`, `context.attempt` rejects with the original error, and `retry` moved to `runIngestion` without `shouldRetry`, `shouldConsumeRetry` or `factor`.
  - Breaking: `FetchFailure`, `IngestConfigError`, `ErrorClassifier` and `FailureClass` are no longer exported.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 31702ac: `chkit ingest status` only reads, so read-only users can run it; without a journal table it reports `v0 (no checkpoint)` instead of creating one.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- b58b1d2: New opt-in `stagedLoader` stages each batch, keeps one row per key and inserts only keys missing from a single-server MergeTree destination; `simpleLoader` remains the default.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-ingest`</sub>
- 56a4a54: Backfill chunks no longer break when a settings profile makes `SELECT *` include MATERIALIZED and ALIAS columns, which failed copy backfills and could write mv_replay values into the wrong target columns.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- 6d51fb8: `chkit check` no longer passes a submitted backfill plan when no ObsessionDB plugin is loaded to verify it; it reports `backfill_submitted_unverified` with the same severity as `backfill_required_pending` (#326).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- a1e3d62: `chkit plugin backfill plan --from/--to` now selects the right partitions for tables partitioned on a `Date` column, instead of none or all of them (#352).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- 5f9c453: Backfill resume finds a plan's chunks exactly when its query ID prefix contains backslashes, quotes or LIKE wildcards, without matching unrelated queries.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- 9328651: mv_replay backfills insert by column name, so a `SELECT *` view into a target with reordered columns or extra `DEFAULT`, `MATERIALIZED` or `ALIAS` columns now replays. Planning, `run` and `resume` fail with a clear error when the view's columns do not fit the target.
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- 29cd6e4: `backfill plan --from/--to` no longer selects a partition outside the window because an empty part, for example one left by a DELETE mutation, reports a 1970 `min_time` (#320).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- 65bac5c: `backfill resume` checks chunk status on every replica of a multi-replica target, so it no longer resubmits a chunk that is running or finished on another replica (#289).
  <sub>`@chkit/plugin-backfill`</sub>
- a1d85d7: Async `migrate` runs of the same migration against different databases or journal tables on one server no longer share a query id, so one run can no longer pick up the other's result and record `Applied` without loading its rows (#463).
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- efe9da4: On multi-replica targets such as multi-replica ObsessionDB services, async `migrate` checks every replica for a running attempt, so it no longer resubmits a statement or runs its `-- before-retry:` SQL while an earlier attempt is still writing (#246). Async statements sent through ObsessionDB now run under chkit's query id, so status checks and re-runs can find them.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 1c8852b: `migrate --apply` of a migration that creates the configured database no longer writes a stray journal row into the server's default database or fails there with `UNKNOWN_TABLE`.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- d9d6762: `chkit check` prints `Database ""` instead of `Database "undefined"` when the target database is missing and none is configured.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 6936791: An unknown `chkit ingest` subcommand now exits 1 with `unknown_subcommand` instead of printing help, flag errors under `--json` print a JSON error envelope, and `chkit ingest <command> --help` lists that subcommand's flags. `chkit add` errors name the missing template or the network cause instead of a bare ENOENT or "fetch failed".
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 0e22b16: `migrate` waits until every replica reflects a column's new type, default, comment and codec, a column rename, or an added or dropped index before running the next statement; a timeout names the replica and field that still differ (#290).
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 7f206d9: Connection errors and `CHKIT_DEBUG` logs no longer print credentials embedded in `clickhouse.url`, and such a URL no longer triggers `@clickhouse/client` override warnings on every run.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- b1289cb: With `CHKIT_DEBUG=1`, `queryJson` calls no longer drop their ClickHouse settings.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- e1a9d05: `migrate` no longer times out after `CREATE OR REPLACE DICTIONARY` while the dictionary reloads; it waits for the dictionary in every replica's catalog instead.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 105c99e: `chkit drift` and `chkit check` now report a column codec added, removed or changed on the server as `changed_column`, treating equivalent spellings such as `ZSTD` and `ZSTD(1)` as equal.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 72d93ae: `chkit drift` and `chkit check` now compare each view's and materialized view's query and `TO` target with the live ones, reporting `query_mismatch` or `target_mismatch` (#382). `drift` no longer falls back to plain text matching after "Session is locked by a concurrent client".
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- bce7e5c: `--json` output over 64 KiB is no longer cut off when piped to a slow reader such as `jq`.
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 2a7e698: New `chkit migrate --setting <name=value>` sends ClickHouse query settings with every statement a migration runs, for example `--setting max_table_size_to_drop=0` to drop a table larger than the server's drop limit (#321).
  <sub>`chkit`</sub>
- 61ea1dd: `chkit migrate --setting` rejects ClickHouse HTTP parameters such as `database`, `query_id` and `password` with a usage error before anything runs (#353).

## 0.15.0

### Minor Changes

- 6dd3f98: cli: output a person can read at a glance, and one place that says whether this computer is fine
  
  `sessionpipe doctor` now starts with a verdict (`All good`, or how many things need attention), sets out what it looked at in groups of aligned rows, each with a mark and a word, and ends with **To fix**: one plain sentence and, where there is something to run, one command each, in the order to run them. `sessionpipe status` is the same in a few lines. `--json` keeps its shape on both.
  
  Trouble that only the daemon's log knew is on that page: a disk that filled up, a key the service can't read from the keychain, a pool with no account left to try, a receiver that hasn't answered. Whether Claude Code is signed in is asked of the running service over its socket (a new, read-only `health` request), because a shell over ssh can't read a Mac's login keychain; before, doctor told people who were signed in to sign in again. A service that launchd or systemd doesn't have at all is said to be not loaded, where it used to read as offline.
  
  `sessionpipe control status` is a page at a terminal, and exactly the JSON it always printed when piped or given `--json`. `--help` is one page of every command in groups, each with what it is for in a line that fits 80 columns; a command's own `--help` folds its usage between options.
  
  Colour comes from one small module with no dependency: on at a terminal, off there with `--no-color`, `NO_COLOR` or `TERM=dumb`, on there with `FORCE_COLOR` whatever `NO_COLOR` says. A pipe is never coloured. Nothing is said by colour alone. Lines fold at the terminal's width under their own text, never inside a command; a pipe gets whole lines, as before. Nothing a program reads has changed: hook output, the worker, the status line, every `--json`, the daemon's log.
  
  What changes for a script, and what does not:
  
  - **`doctor`'s exit code.** `sessionpipe doctor` exits 1 when **To fix** holds a command to run, and 0 otherwise; it used to exit 0 always. A finding with nothing to type (a slow hook, a receiver that hasn't answered yet, a disk that was full and has room again, hooks an agent's own setting turns off) is on the page and counted in the verdict, and leaves the code at 0, so the code does not change with this computer's load. `doctor --json` exits 0 whatever it finds, as before. `status` exits 0, as before.
  - **A command that fails.** Where stderr is a terminal it prints two lines: `error` with what is wrong, and `try` with the one command to run next. That command is the one the code that failed names, or the failing command's own `--help`; it is never read out of the message, which may be a receiver's or npm's words. Where stderr is not a terminal it is the one line it always was, `sessionpipe: <message>`, and exit 1.
  - **`control pair` when a program runs it.** Not at a terminal its lines are the ones it has always written, to the byte: the link, `The page shows these digits too: 123456` or `enter:  123 456`, `✓ Paired with …`, `Daemon: …`. At a terminal the link and the digits stand each on a line of their own (`open:`, `check:` or `enter:`), and the last line starts `Background service:`.
  - **Lines that are worded anew, at a terminal and in a pipe.** `doctor`, `status` and `--help` are new pages, and `control mode` sets each mode out on its own line. `install` says `This computer: <name>` where it said `Machine: <name>`, `No coding agent found on this computer` where it said `No supported harness found on this machine`, and `Nothing leaves this computer yet` where it said `this machine`. `ask on`, `ask off` and `pool on` say `Background service: …` where they said `Daemon: …`. `Renamed the background service`, `The background service uses the new list within seconds` and `The background service uses the new setting within seconds` said `the control daemon`. `sink list` and `pool` keep their old lines in a pipe and get a layout that fits at a terminal. The line `ask <agent>` writes to stderr when the service goes away is unchanged.
  - **`--no-color`** is taken out of the arguments wherever it stands, before the command reads them, so it is never the value of the option before it.
  - **`doctor --json`.** The shape is the same. `claude_accounts[].signed_in` is now what the running background service sees, where it can be asked, and this shell's view only where it can't. `warnings` keeps its old strings and may hold three new ones: `the background service isn't loaded: <launchd|systemd> doesn't have it`, `this computer's disk is full: <n> MB left` (or `this computer's disk was full <when> ago, by the background service's log`), and `the pool has no account with room left: Claude Code sessions here are being refused`. `update.off` keeps the words it had.
  - **Words that are not sessionpipe's own** (a receiver's reason or last error, npm's last lines, a name from a file) are shown as words: escape sequences, other control characters and the characters that turn the writing direction round are taken out of every line written for a person, and a line break inside such a value is a space.
  - **Commands printed for pasting** (under **To fix**, and after `try`) quote a path, a name or an address a shell would otherwise act on.
  
  `sessionpipe-core/service` gains `serviceState`: whether launchd or systemd has a service now, without changing anything.
- 1240735: update: one command leaves the whole computer current
  
  `sessionpipe update` used to update only the copy it ran from and ask the daemon to restart "as soon as nothing is in hand". On a Mac with two copies (the one typed, and another the background service ran) the typed command stayed at an old version while everything looked updated; on a computer where some session is always working the restart never came, and people were told to type `launchctl kickstart`.
  
  Now, when it ends well, the copy you type, the copy the background service runs and the hooks are one version, the newest; the service is running it and has heard from its receivers; and the last line says so. It installs npm's latest into this copy, writes the hooks again from it, puts the service on this copy, and looks that it answers with the new version and has had an answer from each receiver since it started (it waits up to 40 seconds for that, the time a long-poll's first answer can take).
  
  How the service gets onto this copy depends on who runs it. One that launchd or systemd has, and that runs another copy or doesn't answer, is replaced with the safe replace from 0.13.7; it keeps the environment its service file gave it (its PATH, a `SESSIONPIPE_CLAUDE` added by hand), and only the program changes. One whose file is there with nothing running is put back. One that runs this copy restarts itself. One you run yourself (`control pair --no-service`, tmux, a container, WSL without systemd) is asked over its socket to restart itself, and no service is installed that nobody asked for.
  
  When it can't get there it stops with one line that says what is wrong and one that says what to run next: `sessionpipe update` again when npm can't be reached (what needs no download is still done, and nothing is ever moved back to an older release); a `sudo npm install … && sessionpipe update` line for a prefix this user can't write, with the prefix quoted (on Windows: `sessionpipe update` from a terminal opened as administrator); `npx sessionpipe@latest update` for a copy npm didn't install; `sessionpipe control run` where nothing runs the service and there is no service file for it. Where launchd or systemd refuses the new service, the one that was there before is put back and started again, and the command says whether anything answers now.
  
  Exit 0 means everything is current, 3 that the service finishes by itself, 1 that it stopped. A receiver that hasn't answered the service is not a failed update: the last line says the computer is up to date and names the receiver, in yellow, and the exit code is 0. `SESSIONPIPE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 sessionpipe update` changes nothing, as before: it says that updating is off because the variable is set, and how to run it once without it.
  
  A restart is now held back only by what the daemon itself holds: a turn it runs, a message in hand, a permission prompt it holds for an answer, a pooled request being answered. A session someone is working in, mid-turn in its own window, no longer holds it back: that it is mid-turn is written to the daemon's state at a stop and read back at the next start, so a message to it still waits for its Stop. `update` gives the daemon 25 seconds to finish what it holds; past that it says the service restarts by itself when that is done, and there is nothing more to type. Just before it replaces a running service it asks it to stop taking messages, in the same step in which the service is found to hold nothing. A service from before 0.15 does none of this, and restarts itself only once no session on the computer is mid-turn: where launchd or systemd has it, `update` replaces it at once, after writing down for the new one which sessions the old one knew to be mid-turn; one run by hand can only restart itself by its older rule, and `update` says so and exits 3. Into a pipe a failed `update` is one line that ends `Next: <command>`.
  
  The daemon's own daily update takes the same steps (`installEverywhere`): its own copy, the `sessionpipe` on its PATH when that is another install (the copy a person types), the hooks, then its restart. npm is only ever run on a folder that has `dist/cli.js` and a package.json that says it is sessionpipe. `sessionpipe doctor` sees a split between the three, says which, and names `sessionpipe update` as the one fix; it no longer sends anyone to `sessionpipe install` from an older copy, which was refused or, forced, put the hooks back. Where the service isn't running and there is no service file for it, `doctor` and `update` both name `sessionpipe control run`.
  
  Also: the registry asked for `latest` is the one `npm_config_registry` names, when it names one, since that is where npm installs from. A sessionpipe that keeps its files somewhere other than this computer's usual place (`SESSIONPIPE_STATE`, `SESSIONPIPE_CONFIG`, `XDG_*` or `HOME` point elsewhere: a test, a throwaway world, a profile of your own) never looks at, replaces or stops this computer's usual service, and says so; `SESSIONPIPE_SERVICE_LABEL=org.sessionpipe.<name>` gives it a service of its own, and no other name is taken.
  
  `sessionpipe-core/service`: `serviceState` also answers the program a service file names (`serviceArgv`), and says `manager: null` where launchd or systemd can't be asked from this process; `serviceEnvironment` reads back the environment a service file gives; `installService` restarts a systemd unit that was running onto the new file, and where the manager refuses the new service it puts back the file that was there and starts that one again (`ServiceRefused` says which).

## 0.14.2

### Patch Changes

- 554f990: outbox: a line that is not valid UTF-8 no longer costs a later event
  
  `Outbox.read` counted each line's length from its decoded text. Bytes that are not UTF-8, such as the end of an append cut off inside a character with the next append joined onto it, decode to U+FFFD, which is three bytes and can stand for one to three bad bytes, so the offset it returned could run a few bytes past the line's end. The next read then started inside a line, which failed to parse and was skipped without a word: the drain, `sessionpipe tail` and the GUI's outbox source all missed that event. Lines are now found and counted in the bytes as read, so the offset is always the byte after the newline.

## 0.13.5

### Patch Changes

- af298b3: An ACP agent that goes away with a message to it still unwritten no longer raises an error nobody catches. A message longer than a pipe holds waits in the pipe; when the agent then exits or is closed, the write fails afterwards, on the agent's input stream, which had no error listener: an uncaught `write EPIPE` in the daemon. The failed write is now heard like the agent's exit is: whoever is waiting for the answer gets "<agent> stopped taking input: …" (or its exit), and the session is closed so the next message opens another.
- 54736f5: A turn that was stopped no longer reads as answered with "No response requested."
  
  When a Claude Code session is resumed after its last turn was ended mid-way (a Stop sent
  through `sessionpipe control`, a killed process, a crash), Claude Code writes "No response
  requested." into the transcript as the assistant's, under its own `<synthetic>` model.
  sessionpipe sent that on as what the agent had said, so a receiver drew a stopped turn as
  answered with those words. It is now read as the end of a turn that was stopped, the way
  `[Request interrupted by user]` is: the turn goes out with what it had really said, which
  may be nothing. Claude Code's other synthetic rows, such as an API error, are still the
  turn's reply.
- 4d1a18e: A Claude Code session is found only under the id its transcript is filed as. On a disk that ignores case (macOS, Windows) a command naming `claude-code:8C132906-…` opened the transcript of `8c132906-…`, while the session's registry row and its hooks, which are what say it is open in a window or mid-turn, are kept under the id as Claude Code wrote it: the session looked idle and was resumed in place, `claude -p --resume 8C132906-…`, beside the person's own window. Such a command is now refused `no_session` ("no Claude Code session 8C132906 on this machine") on every platform, as it already was on Linux. A new session's id that differs from an existing session's only by case is still refused as taken (`bad_session`): on such a disk it would be written into that session's file.

## 0.13.4

### Patch Changes

- 2e80bf1: A message to a session whose headless run has just exited now resumes it in place at once. A transcript written in the last 90 seconds used to count as a session in use whoever wrote it, so a message sent 7, 9 or 39 seconds after a `claude -p` at a terminal had exited ran in a copy, and the reply said the session was open in a window. The session's own end, as its hooks report it (`SessionEnd`), now accounts for that write the way the end of the daemon's own run already did; a write nothing accounts for still makes a copy, since a writer may be behind it. Where a copy is made the ack says why, as the machine found it: `detail` opens "ran in a copy, because" and then "the session was open in Claude Code on this computer (a terminal window or the Claude app)", "another Claude Code process on this computer was running the session", or "the transcript of the session had been written to in the last 90 seconds by a process this computer could not find", followed where it applies by "; it could not be reached in place: …" with what the session's own inbox said. A later message that resumes the copy says "ran in the copy made earlier, because …". The copy itself is told "the original is open in a window" only when it is. The refusals for a held session that can't be copied say the same three things instead of "the session is open".
- 8fb6b5d: Nothing of a message's `id` reaches a session unless it is a whole ULID. The id is the receiver's and nobody signs it, and the last twelve characters of whatever it was went into the text written into a live session's inbox, inside the header that says "signed on the sender's device". This release puts that mark on every message handed to a live session, and makes it only from a 26-character ULID: `messageMark` in `sessionpipe-core/control` answers null for anything else, and `frameMarked` then frames the message without one. A message whose id is not a ULID is still delivered, as far as it can be without a mark. It is not handed to a session's `sessionpipe channel` and not written into its inbox, the two ways in whose only proof of delivery is the mark, so it takes the next rung instead: the session's Stop where a turn is running, else a resume or a copy (a copy's ack says "it could not be reached in place: the receiver gave this message an id that is not a ULID, so the turn it would cause there could not be told from any other"). Handed over at the session's Stop or to `sessionpipe wait`, it is acked `delivered` with no `reply` when the session's turn ends. Receivers that follow HTTP.md already send ULIDs and see no change.
- 04d615f: When the daemon can't read a Claude Code's options, the refusal says why in the command's own words: `claude --help` failed: env: node: No such file or directory (the first line it wrote to stderr), "no such file", "the file can't be run (permission denied)", or its exit code. It used to say only "failed", which gave the person who sent the message nothing to act on. The line is one line of at most 200 characters, with the home folder written `~` and anything shaped like a secret removed.
- d41c1ff: Closing an ACP agent that has already exited signals nothing. The daemon closes a held agent it finds gone, and the close armed its two timers all the same (SIGTERM after 2 seconds, SIGKILL after 12), whose only disarming was an exit that had already happened: both went to the number of a process group that no longer existed, or that the system had since given to another process.
- 489494e: A headless run that reaches its 30-minute cap no longer signals its process group ten seconds after the child has exited. The follow-up SIGKILL was on a timer that was never cleared, so it went to the group's number even when the group was gone: the one way the daemon could signal a process it had not started (a pid reused as a group leader inside those ten seconds). The timer is cleared when the child exits, whatever the child left in its group (a tool that ignores SIGTERM) is killed at that moment, once, and a cap that arrives after the child has exited signals nothing and no longer marks the finished run as timed out. A run ended by a Stop, which this release adds, is ended the same way.
- d9def02: The control daemon builds the words around a delivered message with the same definitions the transcript readers take them off with (`sessionpipe-core/control`), so the three wordings this release adds are left out of a turn's `user` text like the rest: the header that names the message where it is handed to a live session at its Stop or through its waiter (`Message via <host> (sessionpipe control, signed on the sender's device; message XXXXXXXXXXXX):`), the note to a copy whose original is not open in a window but in use by another process, and the mark in an ask handed over in place (`…with sessionpipe ask, message XXXXXXXXXXXX. Answer here in full: …`). The paragraph that says an agent asked stays, in its plain form (`(Asked by <harness>:<id> on this machine with sessionpipe ask. Answer here in full: …)`), whichever way the task arrived. `sessionpipe-core/control` exports `messageMark` (null for an id that is not a ULID), `frameMarked`, `copyNote(why)` and `unframe`, and `frameAsk` takes the mark as a third argument.
- d8523d5: The protocol's JSON Schemas (`schemas/v1/*.json`) are generated from `proto/sessionpipe/v1/*.proto`, the protocol's one definition (RFC 0001, step 1), byte-identical to what the Zod source produced. The Zod file stays this release and is held equal to the proto by a test; nothing on the wire changes.
- ce3f0ab: The reply to a message delivered in place (at a session's Stop, to its waiter, into its inbox) is now the answer to that message, or nothing. Three things went wrong on one day: a message handed over at a Stop came back with the sentence the session had written before the message arrived (Claude Code writes its transcript a moment after the fact, so the turn's last words landed after its Stop hook had asked); a message to a session that also had a copy was read from the copy's transcript, so its ack waited 215 seconds and carried a later message's answer; and another such message was acked 30 minutes late with no reply at all. The message now names itself in its frame, by the last twelve characters of its id (`…signed on the sender's device; message XXXXXXXXXXXX):`, and for an ask `…with sessionpipe ask, message XXXXXXXXXXXX.`), the reply is what the session wrote after the rows its transcript records for that message and before anything else begins (the next message, a prompt the person types, a turn a background task starts), it is read from the transcript of the session the message was handed to, and the final ack goes out when the session's own hooks say that turn ended. Where no answer can be put down to the message the ack is `delivered` without a `reply`, and no longer carries a file path in `detail` when the transcript can't be read.
- 26eec6c: Stop (`cancel`) now stops a turn the daemon itself is running. A session started or resumed from a page runs as a `claude -p` (or `codex exec`, `agy`) child of the daemon, and a Stop for it used to be acked `unsupported` while the turn ran to its end. The daemon now ends that child the way it ends one at the 30-minute cap (SIGTERM to its process group, then SIGKILL to whatever is left, ten seconds later or as the child exits), acks the cancel `taken` and then `delivered` with the turn's mode and "stopped the turn this computer was running for that session", and acks the stopped turn's own message `delivered` with what it had written, ending "(The turn was cancelled.)". A message queued behind the stopped turn still runs next, in order. A turn in a process the daemon did not start is never signalled: the cancel is `unsupported` and says who has the session ("…open in Claude Code on this computer (a terminal window or the Claude app)… press Esc there", or the pid of someone else's headless run), and a session nothing is running in is `expired` ("nothing is running in that session as far as this computer can tell, so there was nothing to stop"). spec/CONTROL.md §6 `cancel` says so, with fixtures `conformance/delivery/30`–`33`.
- 4d9654f: What 0.13.0 to 0.13.2 told a copy ("You are a copy of that session, started to answer this message: …") is taken off a turn's `user` text like the notes written today. No daemon says that sentence any more, but every copy those versions made has it in its transcript after the person's words, where a backfill reads it. Where another agent's task went to such a copy, the paragraph that says who asked is the last of the turn's `user` text, as for any other ask.
- b6ed157: A turn in a Claude Code terminal session reaches a tier-2 sink when it ends, not when the next one does. Claude Code writes its transcript up to 100 ms after the fact and a terminal's Stop hook fires sooner than that, so the worker used to read a file that did not hold the turn's last message yet: the receiver got "the turn ended" and then the prompt and the reply one turn late, or only when the session closed. The Stop names the turn's last words, and the worker now waits for the file to hold them: 400 ms with the turn's end, then for 5 s more behind it, then at the session's next hook. A turn is sent once, and whole: one that said something before a tool call is no longer sent as that half with the rest as a second turn that nobody asked. The hook itself does no more than before.
  
  A turn stopped with Esc or Ctrl-C is no longer lost. No hook fires for it, so at the session's next prompt, compaction, start or end the worker reads the interruption from the transcript and sends the turn with what it had said, and a `turn.ended` with `reason: interrupt` where the turn was still held as running. The next prompt is a turn of its own instead of being joined to the one that was stopped, and `[Request interrupted by user]` is never part of anyone's prompt.
- 59d0716: A turn's `user` text is what the person wrote, and nothing the machine wrote around it. A receiver draws that text as the person's own message, and three things were getting into it from Claude Code sessions. A subagent's report: when a subagent hands its report back, Claude Code records it the way it records a message from another session, and it was read as part of the prompt ("[Subagent hand-back] The text below is the final report of a subagent…"). sessionpipe's own words around a message it delivers: "(Sent via <host> with sessionpipe control, signed on the sender's device.)", "Message via <host> (sessionpipe control, …):", the note to a copy of a session ("You are a copy of that session, started because the original is open in a window…"), and the notes on how an answer travels. And `[Request interrupted by user]`. All are left out now, in `turn.transcript`, in `turn.progress` from its first moment, and in the title a session takes from its first ask; the list of attached files stays. sessionpipe's sentences come off only where the daemon puts them (the line before the words, the line or the note after them): the same words typed or pasted by the person stay, and a prompt that is nothing but one of them is sent as typed.
  
  Two of sessionpipe's own lines stay where they were, because a receiver tells an agent's words from the person's by them: the paragraph after a task another agent asked with `sessionpipe ask` ("(Asked by <harness>:<id> on this machine with sessionpipe ask. …)", the last paragraph of the turn's `user` text however the task arrived), and the first line of a handoff's answer ("Answer from <harness>:<id> (sessionpipe handoff, …):").
  
  A message delivered into a terminal session at a Stop hook is now a turn of its own: its `user` text is the message, marked `injected` like any message that arrived from elsewhere, and the reply is that turn's. Its reply used to be added to the turn before, or sent as a turn with no prompt.
  
  `sessionpipe-core/control` exports the sentences (`frame`, `frameStart`, `frameMarked`, `frameAsk`, `frameHandoff`, `IN_PLACE_ANSWER`, `copyNote`, `RE_ARM`) and `deliveredWords`, which takes off a text the ones that are not the message.

## 0.13.1

### Patch Changes

- 5892379: A config.json that does not parse (a hand edit's trailing comma, a byte-order mark, a file cut short) is no longer written over with the defaults, which erased the machine's name and every sink with its token. A command that would save it stops with an error naming the file and what is wrong with it; `install`, `connect`, `uninstall` and `control pair` stop before they change anything, and `sink add` before it asks the receiver anything. A config.json that is there but cannot be read is not written over either.
- 4eb5a68: Devin: the transcript walk ends at a node it reaches a second time, so a session store whose parent chain loops back on itself no longer hangs the reader.
- 439d8a6: A machine running workflows with hundreds of parallel subagents no longer runs a receiver out of requests (#208). A receiver is now sent a subagent's finished tool calls (`tool.ended`) at most one per session per minute, plus the one that shows a subagent's permission prompt was answered, the main thread's tool events as they happen, and at most one request a second from the machine, carrying everything that piled up meanwhile. Turns, prompts, permission questions, subagents and file changes are never thinned, and the local outbox still keeps every event. `sessionpipe sink add … --tools all|main|beat` picks what a sink is sent: `all` (every tool call, as before) is the default; a receiver that meters requests asks for `main` with `tools` in its well-known file, which the machine reads at `sink add` and `connect` and again once a day; `beat` thins the main thread too. No receiver's view changes on this upgrade unless it asked. `sink list`, `status` and `doctor` show each sink's setting; `replay` says how many tool events it thinned and takes `--tools all` to send every one once. A permission prompt now carries `agent_id` when a subagent asked, and a Codex subagent's tool calls carry one too. A worker near the end of its 15 s life no longer starts a drain it can't finish, and hands the work to a fresh worker instead; two workers can no longer both take over the same stale lock. In a simulated workflow of 100 subagents making 30 tool calls each over three minutes (6,214 events), a receiver got up to 6,214 requests before (one per event, with the jobs run one after another; real concurrent workers merged some) and 76 with the default; a replay of the issue's real events put the same rules at about 9,900 requests a day, against 39,500 with the one-a-second pace alone.
- 2f7f39c: `sessionpipe forget` takes the session out of every sink's cursor along with its outbox file, so a session that goes on after it (still running, or resumed later) is sent from its new file's first event. Before, each cursor kept the old file's end offset, and the sinks read nothing from the new file until it grew past that offset, then started mid-way, so the first events were never sent. The cursors are the drain's, so `forget` and `replay` wait for its lock (up to 10 s) before they change anything; past that they change nothing, say so and exit 1. A cursor file holding `null` or a list reads as empty instead of stopping a drain.
- a0197d5: A harness config file the system won't let sessionpipe write (read-only: EACCES, or EPERM on Windows after `attrib +r`; a read-only filesystem's EROFS) is reported for that one file with the code — `! claude-code: ~/.claude/settings.json — can't write it (EACCES); not touched` — the way a file that is not plain JSON already was, and `install` goes on to the next harness, so Codex and Gemini CLI are still hooked. Before, the first such file ended the whole command with `EACCES: permission denied` and left every harness after it unhooked. The refusal is caught where each file is written, so a file the adapter wrote before it (Codex's hooks.json before config.toml, one Claude Code account's settings.json before another's) keeps its report, `created` included, which `uninstall` needs. `uninstall` reports a file it can't write or delete the same way and goes on. Only a write that fails after the file was opened (ENOSPC) says the file may be cut short instead of "not touched".
- 7295fc9: A session whose outbox file was pruned (untouched for `keep_days`, 30 by default) and then resumed under the same id is sent again. Before, pruning also deleted the session's seq counter but left each sink's cursor at the old file's end, so the resumed session restarted at seq 0, which a receiver's (harness, session, seq) deduplication drops as already seen, and the sinks read nothing from the new, shorter file until it grew past the old offset, then started mid-line. Now the counter stays and each sink's cursor into the pruned file is removed.
- f24d3c2: pii@1 keeps an ISO date: `released 2026-10-31` stays as written instead of becoming `released [phone]`, and `2026-10-31 12:00` no longer becomes `[phone]:00`. A date (years 1900–2099, month 01–12, day 01–31) is kept only when nothing after it could carry the run on: no letter or digit, and no separator then two digits (a phone's group; `2026-10-31 5 files` keeps its date) unless that is a time's hour (` 12:00`, 00–23), and not right after a `)` or a `+` with a country code. A date after a `+` (a diff's added line) is kept too. A date that a phone's digit group follows directly, as in `2026-10-31 415-555-0132` or `2026-10-31 0132:`, is read as before (a `(`, `+` or `,` between them starts a new number, and the date stays).

## 0.13.0

### Minor Changes

- aa44c74: Control: a handoff's `reply_to`, and the events of an ask (CONTROL.md §3.1, §6 *Handoff*, §13; PROTOCOL.md §3, §4). A `prompt` or a `start` MAY carry `reply_to`, `<harness>:<id>` of a session on the same machine that gets the answer as a message once the command's turn ends. `sessionpipe-core/control` accepts it on those two kinds only, as a session ref by the adapter's rule and never the command's own session, and refuses the rest `bad_fields`; the command's acks are unchanged. Two event types on the asking session, `delegation.started` and `delegation.ended` (tier 0; `text` at tier 1, `reply` at tier 2), and one session field, `delegated_by` (from `SESSIONPIPE_ASKED_BY`, read like `launched_by`), say which session asked which and what came back. Schemas: `control-command` gains `reply_to`, `control-hello` and `control-pair` gain `ask` and `handoff`, `event` gains `session.delegated_by`, `event-data` the two types. Five new shared vectors (`165`–`169`). `jobEnv` and `claudeEnv` drop `SESSIONPIPE_LAUNCHED_BY`, `SESSIONPIPE_ASKED_BY` and `SESSIONPIPE_ASK_CHAIN` from the daemon's own environment (`withoutLineage`, `LINEAGE_ENV`), so a child carries exactly the lineage the daemon gives it and nothing the daemon's shell had.
- aedb6e9: Control: an `inbox` delivery mode (CONTROL.md §6.3). A message for a session somebody has open is written into Claude Code's own local inbox for it, so the turn runs in that live process, in the mode the person left it in, in the window or thread they are already looking at — instead of being answered by a copy. It sits between `turn` and `api` on the ladder, is chosen before the first byte (one live registry record in the account the session resolved to, the inbox protocol, an interactive process, a socket of this uid, a matching process start time read in UTC, an idle session, a signed `iat` at most 120 s old, a permission class), and is never retried or re-sent on another mode once a byte is written. The envelope declares THE MACHINE's own permission class, `bypass` only on an `inherit` machine whose account defaults to bypass and may; the mode is used only where that equals the session's own class. A write is confirmed by the row the session writes for the turn it caused, carrying that message's own mark; unconfirmed it acks `failed` with code `held`, says nothing was duplicated, and keeps the mode shut for that session while the message could still be released to it — across a restart of the daemon too, since the hold is kept in its state. Where the session the command named has a copy, all of that is the copy's: its inbox, its hold, its turn. The writer is the daemon's alone: not exported from `sessionpipe-core`, no CLI verb.
  
  Core: `liveRecords`/`liveRecord` read every live session registry row (`liveProcess` is now a question about that list); `findTranscripts` and `resolveHome` pick which Claude Code account a session id belongs to when several hold its transcript, and a message for an id that is filed in two accounts with none of them holding it open is refused `ambiguous_home`. New `hookMode`, `peerClass`, `modeRank`, `CLAUDE_MODES`, `homeSettings`, `NO_HOME_SETTINGS`, `relaunchMode`, `peerAsk`.
  
  Each session's own permission mode is recorded from its hooks (`permission_mode` on every Claude Code payload), in the daemon's own state and no Claude Code home, latest word wins, nothing written when it hasn't changed. A relaunch (`resume`, `fork`) of a session the daemon did not start now re-asserts just the narrowing the session itself chose — `plan` and `dontAsk` always, `acceptEdits` where the account's own default is at least that wide, nothing otherwise, and never `auto` or `bypassPermissions`; a start's own recorded options (#138) are untouched. The ack's `detail` says the mode the new turn recorded, and on an `auto` machine whose Claude Code has auto disabled, that the turn ran in Manual mode.
  
  A copy says so: `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_SOURCE_ALIVE` on a fork whose source is still open, a note in the message telling the copy it is one, `copy_of` on the ack, a record with a date and a reason (written beside the plain id map an older daemon reads), a `limits.copies_per_day` cap refused as `copy_limit`, and no copy of a copy. A peer-delivered ask is read as the turn's ask and marked `injected` on `turn.transcript` and `turn.progress`, so a running turn says the same about it as a finished one. `daemon.log` is created 0600, like the files beside it.
- aa44c74: **For receivers.** What a 0.13.0 machine sends and accepts beyond 0.12.0 (CHANGELOG.md, "For receivers (0.13.0)", has the detail).
  
  - **Hello and pairing request** say `ask` (sessions there may ask another agent) and `handoff: true` (a `start` or a `prompt` may carry `reply_to`). A machine that says neither is 0.12.0 or older: send it no `reply_to`, or it refuses the command `bad_fields`.
  - **`reply_to`** on a `start` or a `prompt`: a session on the same machine that gets the answer as a message after the command's final `delivered` ack, framed `Answer from <harness>:<short id> (sessionpipe handoff, asked via <receiver host>):`. The command's own ack is unchanged; the relay is not acked and never relayed further.
  - **Events:** `delegation.started` and `delegation.ended` on the asking session (tier 0; `text` at 1, `reply` at 2), with `relayed` saying how a handoff went, and `session.delegated_by` on every event of the session that answers. Lineage, never authority: join on `to` and `delegated_by`, never read `delegated_by` as a subagent, and keep a `delegation.*` event you don't know as any other type.
  - A receiver that pre-checks commands re-vendors 0.13.0's `sessionpipe-core/control` and its vectors (`165`–`169` are new).

### Patch Changes

- aedb6e9: `sessionpipe channel`: a Claude Code channel, so a message reaches a live session in its own thread. Claude Code runs it as one session's MCP server (`claude mcp add --scope user sessionpipe -- sessionpipe channel`, then `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:sessionpipe` while channels are a research preview). It parks on the daemon's local socket as that session's waiter for as long as the session runs, and pushes each message in as a `notifications/claude/channel`: the session takes it in its own permission mode, as the person's own words, and shows it as a message from `sessionpipe` in the terminal and in the Claude app. The daemon routes to it as a waiter while the session is idle and reads the answer back from the transcript. The transcript reader now keeps a channel's message (`origin.kind: "channel"`, wrapped in `<channel source="…">`) as its turn's ask: a turn asked through a channel, Telegram's included, used to reach a receiver with nothing asked.
- b4a0d39: Control: a `claude --help` that couldn't be read is never taken for a Claude Code with no permission modes (#152). `detectCaps` marks a run that times out, or fails without listing `--permission-mode`, as `unread` (and takes a timeout, 30 s by default); `modeFlags` then refuses every level but `inherit`, saying why ("this machine couldn't read its Claude Code's options (`claude --help` timed out after 30 s); try again in a minute"), where it used to refuse `auto` as a mode that Claude Code lacks and to run `safe` with no permission flag at all. The daemon asks an unread `--help` again a minute later, and logs each one, instead of keeping it until a restart. A channel takes a message only while its session is idle: Claude Code folds a channel message that arrives during a turn into that turn, where the model need not answer it, so a running turn takes the message at its Stop. A channel's delivery is proven the way an inbox write is, by the turn the session begins for it; one the session began no turn for is acked `failed` with code `held`, and that channel is handed nothing more, since Claude Code drops a channel's messages in silence where it didn't register the channel. `sessionpipe channel` no longer parks in a `--print` or Agent SDK session, which ignore the channel flags (the Claude app's sessions run so). An answer the model thought about first comes back whole: the reader took the thinking record that ends such a turn (`stop_reason: end_turn`, no text) for the end of the answer, and acked it with no reply. A channel's ask is marked `injected`, as a peer's is.
